Alexa Help Compendium

Official Amazon help for Alexa and Alexa+ on Echo devices and the Alexa app

2026-07-18

Alexa Help Compendium

This compendium contains the main content of 738 articles from Amazon’s official Alexa help section, covering Alexa and Alexa+ on Echo devices and the Alexa app used to configure them. Categories follow Amazon’s own Alexa help hubs, sorted alphabetically, with article titles alphabetized within each category. Site navigation, feedback prompts, and pages outside the Alexa section have been removed. This second edition adds the deeper articles linked from within the hub-curated set, including detailed notes on individual Alexa+ features and per-device pages; a small residue of mostly per-device legal and safety notices remains outside the collection.

Alexa App Settings

Alexa App is Slow or Unresponsive

Force stopping the Alexa app resolves most issues with responsiveness.

To solve most issues:

  • Force stop the app.

  • Sign out of the app.

  • Uninstall and then reinstall the app.

  • Force Stop an App on an Android Device

  • Force Stop an App on an Apple Device

  • Sign Out of the Alexa App

  • Download the Alexa App

For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

Alexa App OS and Software Version Compatibility

The Alexa app is compatible with iOS and Android operating systems. It’s also compatible with Fire OS.

The Alexa app is compatible with the following operating systems and software versions:

  • iOS 16.0+
  • Android 10.0+
  • Fire OS 7.0+

Note: Features are limited for Android devices running software version 11 or older.

Ask Alexa to Speak in Multiple Languages

To enable multilingual mode, ask Alexa to speak in multiple languages or change the default language.

  • “Speak Spanish.”

    Change the default language.

  • “Speak English and Spanish.”

    Speak to Alexa in either language and she responds in that language. On-device text appears in the primary language.

  • “Speak English and Spanish.”

    Switch back to primary language.

  • Change the Language on Your Echo Device

Can’t Log Into the Alexa App

To resolve most issues, confirm your username and password, check your internet connection, and ensure that your Alexa app is updated.

On the login screen in the Alexa app, verify your Amazon email or phone number, and password are correct.

Change the Language You Use to Talk to Alexa in the Alexa App

You can change the language spoken in the Alexa app and on Alexa accessories that connect through the Alexa app.

To change the language Alexa speaks in the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app.

  2. Open More and select Settings .

  3. Select Alexa App Settings.

  4. Under Language, select the current language.

  5. Choose your preferred language.

    Tip: Your Alexa experience is best when you select the language supported for your marketplace.

Important: Changing the language Alexa speaks in the app doesn’t change the text language in the app. The Alexa app text language matches the language set in your mobile device settings.

Change Your Alexa Device Location

Your device’s location is used for weather, time, and other features.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select your device.
  4. Select Device Settings.
  5. Select Device Location.
  6. Enter your complete address, and then select Save.

Download the Alexa App

Download and install the Alexa app from your mobile device app store. Add the Alexa widget for easy home screen access.

  1. Open the app store on your mobile device.
  2. Search for the Amazon Alexa app.
  3. Select Install.
  4. Select Open and sign in with your Amazon Account.
  5. Install Alexa widgets (optional).

Tip: Widgets allow easier access to Alexa from your device home screen. Alexa widgets become available in the device widget menu after you sign in to the Alexa app. On iOS (iOS 14 or newer) or Android devices, long-press the home page of your device and follow the instructions to add widgets.

  • What is the Alexa App?
  • Manage Smart Home Devices with the Widget on iOS
  • Alexa App OS and Software Version Compatibility

Set Alexa App to Light or Dark Mode

Change how pages, menus, and controls display.

To switch between light or dark mode:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Select Alexa App Settings.
  4. Select Color Theme and choose Light or Dark. To continue automatically matching your device’s mode setting, select System Theme.

Note: Some mobile device OS versions don’t support dark mode. The Alexa App comes in only light mode on devices with these OS versions:

  • iOS version 12 or older
  • Android version 9 or older
  • Fire OS

Sign Out of the Alexa App

You can sign out of the Alexa app in the app settings.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Scroll down, and then select Sign Out.

Turn Adaptive Volume On or Off

Activate Adaptive Volume to adjust Alexa’s volume automatically when background noise increases.

There are multiple ways that you can turn Adaptive Volume on or off.

To turn Adaptive Volume on or off with your voice, you can tell Alexa, “Turn on Adaptive Volume.”

To turn Adaptive Volume on or off with the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select .
  3. Select Settings.
  4. Select Voice Responses.
  5. Turn Adaptive Volume on or off.

Type Requests to Alexa

Use Type with Alexa to interact with Alexa on your device, when speaking isn’t the preferred option.

To talk to Alexa by text, use the Alexa app.

  1. In the Alexa app, open Home, and select the keyboard icon.

    Or, tap the Talk to Alexa icon and then select the keyboard icon from the bottom of the Alexa voice screen.

  2. Type in your request, just as you speak to your Alexa devices. You don’t need your wake word.

  3. To send the message to Alexa, select Return or Go on the keyboard.

Tip: Alexa provides Auto-Suggestions as you type. Alexa might suggest common requests (such as “What’s the weather?” or “Tell me a joke”) or pages in the Alexa app (such as “Reminders,” or “Set a timer”). Select a suggestion if it matches what you want.

Update Wake Sensitivity in the Alexa App

You can change your device’s sensitivity to make your device more or less responsive to the wake word. Changes only affect the device you choose.

To update Wake Sensitivity in the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  2. Select Devices .

  3. Select the device that you want to change.

  4. Select Device Settings.

  5. Select Wake Sensitivity.

  6. Choose the wake sensitivity that you prefer.

    Note: This setting doesn’t affect which device responds when multiple devices detect the wake word.

    • If your device fails to detect the wake word, choose More Sensitive.
    • If your device interprets another word as the wake word, choose Less Sensitive.

    Note: Your device’s sensitivity may change over time as Alexa’s overall quality improves.

  • Change the Wake Word on Your Echo Device

Use Your Wake Word to Talk to Alexa in the Alexa App

Talk to Alexa on your Alexa app using your wake word.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Select Device Settings.
  4. Turn on Enable Alexa Hands Free.
  5. Give mic and location permissions if prompted.

Note: The Alexa app must be open and running in the foreground to use the wake word.

  • Change the Language You Use to Talk to Alexa in the Alexa App

What is the Alexa App?

The Alexa app gives you access to Alexa on your mobile device and allows you to easily manage your Alexa experience.

With the Alexa app on your mobile devices, you can:

  • Use the Alexa in-app assistant on the go.
  • Manage Alexa-enabled devices.
  • Drop In on your friends and family or at home.
  • Track upcoming reminders, alarms, and active timers.
  • Control smart home devices and music playback across Alexa devices.
  • Get information, answers, and play games with Alexa Skills.

Alexa Devices

About Camera Settings on Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) or Echo Show 11 (2025 release)

Enabling or disabling your camera can affect features on your device.

Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) and Echo Show 11 (2025 release) camera powers features like Live View, Drop In, and Visual ID. Learn how enabling or disabling the camera impacts your device’s functionality and personalization options.

Table 1. Camera Settings

  • Live View: Drop In; Live View allows you and household members to check in on your home while away by viewing your compatible device’s live camera feed remotely through the Alexa app. Turning off the camera disables Live View.: The Drop In feature lets you easily connect with your closest friends and family on supported Echo devices. Outside your household, Drop In works only with contacts approved by you. When Drop In is enabled on the device, you can start an instant video (if camera is enabled) or audio call without the other person having to answer.
  • Live View: Visual ID; Live View allows you and household members to check in on your home while away by viewing your compatible device’s live camera feed remotely through the Alexa app. Turning off the camera disables Live View.: Visual ID uses the device’s camera to recognize you and other enrolled individual household members. Once you or household members are recognized using visual ID, the device offers content personalized to you, and it can also trigger personalized routines, including playing the news, turning on the lights, setting the temperature, and more.
  • Live View: Adaptive Content; Live View allows you and household members to check in on your home while away by viewing your compatible device’s live camera feed remotely through the Alexa app. Turning off the camera disables Live View.: Adaptive Content adjusts the screen on Echo Show devices based on your proximity to the device using the camera or Presence Detection using ultrasound.
  • Live View: Presence Detection Using Camera; Live View allows you and household members to check in on your home while away by viewing your compatible device’s live camera feed remotely through the Alexa app. Turning off the camera disables Live View.: Your device uses the camera to detect presence or proximity (without identifying any specific person). The device may also use ultrasound and, in some cases, ultrasound combined with Wi-Fi signals to detect presence or proximity. Once presence is detected, the device can perform routines, such as turning on a light when someone enters a room. Presence detection is also used to power Adaptive Content.
  • Live View: Personalized Reminders; Live View allows you and household members to check in on your home while away by viewing your compatible device’s live camera feed remotely through the Alexa app. Turning off the camera disables Live View.: Personalized Reminders allows you to assign reminders to other members in your household and have Alexa deliver the announcement the next time your device recognizes them using the camera and Visual ID. For example, if you say, “Alexa, remind Claire to water the plants, when you see her,” Alexa surfaces that reminder when the device recognizes Claire, via a voice announcement and full-screen display of the reminder text on the screen in Echo Show devices.

Add Widgets on Your Echo Device with a Screen

Customize your home screen by adding widgets from the Widget Gallery.

For a list of compatible devices, go to What Are Alexa Widgets?

Note: The Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

To add widgets to your device:

  1. Go to the Widget Gallery:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select the Widget Gallery icon. You can also access the Widget Gallery by pressing on a widget for a few moments on your home screen and selecting Add Widget.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, select the Widget Gallery icon on your screen. For Echo Show 15 and Echo Show 21, swipe down from the top of the screen and select the Widget Gallery icon.
  2. Select the widget that you want to add. You can add one or more widgets by selecting
    • in the top-right corner of each widget.
  • Remove or Arrange Widgets

Adjust the Level of Passthrough on Echo Buds

Use the Alexa app to adjust the amount of ambient noise you hear with Passthrough.

Tip: To quickly access Passthrough settings in the Alexa app, you can press the Echo Buds card in the Alexa app. If you don’t see the Echo Buds card, use the following steps to update your device settings:

  1. Turn on Bluetooth on your phone.

  2. Open the Alexa app .

  3. Open the case, and place the Echo Buds in your ears.

  4. Select Devices .

  5. Select your Echo Buds device:

    • Echo Buds (1st Generation)
    • Echo Buds (2nd Generation)

  6. Under Ambient Sound Control, select Passthrough.

  7. Under Passthrough, choose plus or minus to adjust the amount of noise you hear.

    Note: For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd generation), you only see this option if Passthrough is turned On. Passthrough isn’t available with Echo Buds (2023 release).

  • Turn On Noise Reduction and Passthrough with Alexa on Echo Buds (2019 release, 1st Generation)
  • Turn On Noise Cancellation and Passthrough on Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd Generation)

Adjust the Rubber Tips of Your Echo Frames

Echo Frames with rubber temple tips are adjustable for a better fit.

[Embedded video omitted]

You can adjust temple tips on Echo Frames with rubber temple tips. You can’t adjust temple tips on Echo Frames with acetate temple tips by yourself. If your Echo Frames have acetate temple tips, share Echo Frames Optician Card (PDF) with your optician.

Note: Rubber temple tips are soft and have a matte finish. Acetate temple tips are hard and have a glossy finish.

To adjust rubber Echo Frames temple tips:

  1. Try on the Echo Frames.
  2. Hold the rubber area and bend slightly until the frames fit comfortably. Adjust the rubber portion to fit the curvature of your ears.

Important:

  • Do not apply heat to the frames or rubber temple tips.
  • Do not adjust Echo Frames with pliers.

Adjust the Volume on Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa

  (3rd Generation) {#adjust-the-volume-on-your-echo-frames-2nd-generation-and-sma}

Use the volume control button on the temple of your device to change the volume.

For Echo Frames (2nd Generation), use the volume control button on the right temple to change the volume.

For Echo Frames (3rd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa, use the volume control button on the left temple to change the volume.

You can also use voice commands, such as, “Set the volume to [1 - 10],” “volume up/ volume down,” or use your smartphone’s volume controls.

If you can’t reach the maximum volume, check your smartphone to confirm you’re at maximum volume. In quiet environments you can check the volume to reduce what others can hear. To check, hold the device at arm’s length and lower the volume until the audio isn’t noticeable.

Note: On Echo Frames (2nd Generation), Auto Volume can be set to automatically adjust when audio is about to play based on the noise level of your environment and your selected listening profile. Auto Volume increases the volume in noisier environments and lowers the volume in quieter environments.

After Moving, Update Device Location on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Alexa uses your device’s location for weather, time, traffic, and other local features.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings .
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Device Options.
  3. Select About This Device and enter your complete address.
  4. If you’ve moved to a different time zone, under Device Options select Time Zone and make sure it reflects your correct location.

Alexa App Is Disconnecting from Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with

  Alexa (3rd Generation) {#alexa-app-is-disconnecting-from-echo-frames-2nd-generation-a}

Alexa doesn’t respond or tells you to open the Alexa app.

  1. Check your device’s Bluetooth settings. Make sure that Bluetooth is turned on for your device and that your smart glasses are connected and active.
  2. In the Alexa app, open Devices and navigate to your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) device. Check that your smart glasses are Online.
  3. Update the Alexa app to the latest version.
  4. Close the Alexa app and open the app again.

Tip: If these steps don’t work, forget Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) from your device’s Bluetooth settings. Delete the Alexa app from your device and reinstall it again from your device’s app store. After reinstalling the Alexa app, follow the steps in the app to pair your smart glasses to the app again.

  • Reset Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation)

Alexa Can’t Discover Your Amazon Smart Plug

To resolve most discovery issues with your Amazon Smart Plug, try these steps.

  • Check that your Alexa device and the Alexa app have the latest software version.
  • Make sure that your Alexa device and your Amazon Smart Plug are connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
  • Check that your paired device is within 30 ft (9 m) of your Amazon Smart Plug.
  • Reset your Amazon Smart Plug: press and hold the button on the side of the device for 12 seconds. Then set up Amazon Smart Plug again.

Alexa Doesn’t Understand or Respond to Your Request

Alexa doesn’t respond to your request or can’t understand you.

To fix issues with your Echo device not responding:

  • Make sure you’re using the power adapter that came with your device.

  • Make sure that you have an active internet connection.

  • Check that your device isn’t muted. The light indicator is red when your device is muted.

  • For Echo Speakers: press the Action button to see if your Echo device responds.

  • To make sure that Alexa hears you, move your device away from walls, other speakers, or background noise.

  • Try saying, “Did you hear me?”

    • With Alexa+, a pulsing blue light at the bottom of the screen means that Alexa is listening.

  • Unplug your device, wait 30 seconds, and then plug it back in.

  • If you have an Echo device with a Screen, visit Update the Wi-Fi Settings on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

  • If you have an Echo Device with a Screen, visit Reset Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

  • What Do the Lights on Your Echo Speaker Mean?

For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

Alexa for PC Doesn’t Recognize Your Microphone

Try these steps if Alexa for PC isn’t working with your microphone.

  • Check that your microphone isn’t muted and that the volume is turned up.
  • Make sure that your microphone is turned on.
  • Check that Wake Word is turned on.
  • Check that your microphone hardware isn’t damaged by trying it on another program or computer.

Alexa Isn’t Responding on Your Echo Buds

Alexa doesn’t answer your voice commands.

  • Proper fit and placement help the microphones pick up your voice commands. Check that your Echo Buds fit correctly with the fit test in the Alexa app.

    • For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen), check that your Echo Buds are oriented correctly. Turn the ear bud so the Amazon smile logo is right-side up. Then place the ear bud in your ear and rotate slightly to get a secure fit. You can hear a chime when the buds are securely placed in your ear.

  • Make sure that Echo Buds are connected to your phone via Bluetooth.

  • Check that the Alexa app is open and that Echo Buds are online.

  • Check your phone’s volume and increase it as needed.

  • Try pressing the Alexa button in the app to ask a question. If that works, make sure that the Echo Buds microphone isn’t muted in the app.

  • Make sure that the wake word is turned on from Device Settings in the Alexa app.

  • Check that your phone is connected to Wi-Fi or data.

  • Factory Reset Your Echo Buds

  • Echo Buds Lose Bluetooth Connection

  • Fit Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) to Your Ear

Alexa Isn’t Responding on Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation)

Alexa doesn’t answer your voice commands.

To fix common issues with Alexa on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation):

  • Press the action button. This triggers Alexa.

  • Check that the device’s microphones are on. To unmute your frames, double press the action button. The action button is the shorter button on the right arm of the frames.

  • Force close the Alexa app, then open it again.

  • Make sure that your smartphone is connected to Wi-Fi or cellular data.

  • Make sure that your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are connected to your phone. In the Alexa app, open Devices . Find your device. On the Device Settings page, check that your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are Online.

  • Turn your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) off and on again. Press and hold the action button until the status light flashes red. Then, press the action button once until the status light flashes blue and you hear Alexa say, “Connected.”

Arm or Disarm Your Security System with Echo Hub

Use your voice, or a few touches, when you’re leaving or coming back in.

Note: The following steps and procedures apply to Ring Alarm, the home security system currently compatible with Echo Hub.

Before using the Echo Hub to manage your security system, use the Alexa app to install the Alexa skill for the system. The process includes setting up a four-digit access code.

When You’re Leaving the House - Set to Away

Say, “Arm Ring for Away.”

On the Echo Hub:

  1. Select the Security shortcut, then select Away.
  2. An exit delay begins. Make sure you exit and close all doors before the exit delay expires.
  3. When the exit delay expires, the system begins monitoring in its Armed state.

When You Return Home - Set to Disarmed

Say, “Disarm Ring.” When asked, clearly speak your four-digit access code.

On the Echo Hub:

  1. Select the Away icon on the Echo Hub, to open the Security side panel and see the entry delay timer. The entry delay starts when you open a monitored door.
  2. Enter your four-digit access code.
  3. The system transitions to Disarmed if you enter the correct access code before the entry delay timer expires.

When You’re in, but Want Protection - Set to Home

Say, “Arm Ring for Home.”

On the Echo Hub:

  1. Select the Security shortcut, then select Home.
  2. An exit delay begins, for a duration according to your security system’s settings.
  3. When the exit delay expires, the system enters Home state and begins monitoring its perimeter sensors.

Note: Ring Alarm and all Ring Alarm accessories require a subscription for in-app features and notifications, including arming / disarming, and integration with other Ring, Echo, Alexa, and third-party products.

  • Connect Your Home Security System to Echo Hub
  • Activate Your Home Security System with an Alexa Routine

Audio Isn’t Playing from Echo Frames (2nd Generation)

If your audio plays from your phone or another connected device instead of your Echo Frames (2nd Generation), try these troubleshooting steps.

  1. Check your device’s Bluetooth settings. Make sure that Bluetooth is on for your device and that Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are connected and active.
  2. If you’re connected to a smartphone or tablet with the Alexa app, open Devices and select Echo Frames. Check that your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are Online. Turn your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) off and on again if they aren’t online.

Use these steps to make sure audio plays on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation):

  • When answering phone calls, swipe the touchpad on Echo Frames (2nd Generation) instead of answering on your phone.

  • For audio playback, such as listening to music or podcasts, tap the touchpad on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) to pause your audio, and double tap the touchpad to resume your audio.

  • On your device, select where you want your audio to play.

  • If your audio still isn’t playing on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation), try rebooting them. Your audio will play on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) after they turn back on and reconnect.

Battery Isn’t Charging for Echo Buds

Echo Buds aren’t charging when placed in the case.

  • Make sure that the case has a charge, or is plugged in to a wall outlet.
  • Make sure that the correct ear bud is in the correct charging pocket.
  • If using the wing tip, make sure it’s installed correctly. Check that the wing tip isn’t covering the IR sensor.
  • If the device is too hot, it may not work correctly. Place your device in an area away from sun and heat sources, then try again.
  • Try cleaning your Echo Buds.

Tip: Check that the three charging pins in the case aren’t broken. If they are broken, your device can’t charge. See the Amazon Device Warranty page for more info.

For optimal battery performance of your Echo Buds charging case, do not store your case in contact with or in close proximity to your cell phone, tablets, laptops or wireless charger for longer than 1 hour

Button Controls on Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Use the buttons on your smart glasses to answer calls, control media playback, or access other voice assistants.

  • Location: Right Temple; Touch Control: Press and hold the front and back action buttons for three seconds. Your Status light should pulse orange to show you’re in pairing mode.; Result: Pairing
  • Location: Press the front action button once.; Touch Control: Accept a call/accept notification
  • Location: Press the front action button once.; Touch Control: Pause/resume Media
  • Location: Press the front action button twice.; Touch Control: Mute/unmute Mic
  • Location: Press and hold the front action button, listen for the chime, then ask without having to say “Alexa.”; Touch Control: Talk to Alexa
  • Location: Press the back action button once.; Touch Control: Reject a call/decline notification
  • Location: Press and hold the back action button, listen for a chime, then ask.; Touch Control: Talk to Google assistant/Siri
  • Location: Left Temple; Touch Control: Press the front of the volume control.; Result: Increase volume
  • Location: Press the back of the volume control.; Touch Control: Decrease volume

Tip: To access your favorite feature quickly, customize your action buttons. Once selected, press and hold the corresponding action button on the right side of your frames.

Clean Your Echo Buds

Keep your Echo Buds clean to ensure the best audio performance.

[Embedded video omitted]

Tip: To keep your device in good working order, clean your Echo Buds periodically. To remove large particles, remove the ear tips and lightly brush the mesh screen with a soft, dry toothbrush. Then reattach the ear tips. Be careful not to push earwax or other debris into the mesh surface or port hole.

If you’ve tried the previous steps and you still experience a drop in audio quality, try deep cleaning your Echo Buds. To clean the ear tip and nozzle mesh:

  1. For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen): Remove the ear tips from your Echo Buds and wash them with mild soap.
    1. Rinse the ear tips thoroughly and dry them with a soft cloth.
    2. Make sure that the ear tips are completely dry, then reattach the ear tips to your Echo Buds.
  2. Face the nozzle mesh towards the ground. Apply a small amount of hydrogen peroxide (maximum concentration, 3 percent) to the mesh surface using a cotton swab. Be careful not to allow excess liquid to enter the open port on the Echo Buds.
  3. Let the Echo Buds sit with the nozzle facing down for 5 minutes to allow the wax to soften.
  4. Gently clean the downward facing nozzle with a new cotton swab soaked in hydrogen peroxide (maximum concentration, 3 percent).
  5. Wet a toothbrush with hydrogen peroxide (maximum concentration, 3 percent) and gently clean the downward facing nozzle to clear debris from the mesh. Don’t apply heavy pressure.
  6. After the mesh surface is clean, gently shake out any excess liquid and debris. Dry the Echo Buds with a soft cloth.
  7. Blow across the mesh several times to dry it.

If the audio is muffled or if you hear a chirping noise, lightly dab the nozzle area to draw out excess moisture. For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen): Let dry for 24 hours. If audio chirping noise continues after cleaning and drying your Echo Buds, disable Passthrough.

Cleaning Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Instructions on how to clean Echo Frames.

Important: Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) aren’t waterproof and shouldn’t be rinsed under running water or submerged in an ultrasonic cleaner.

Cleaning guidance:

  • Clean your smart glasses with a soft, dry cloth.
  • To clean lenses, use an alcohol-free lens cleaner and a soft cloth.
  • To remove ink from lenses, use up to 70% Isopropyl Alcohol.

Note: Do not spray lens cleaner directly onto lenses that are mounted into Echo Frames (2nd Generation) or Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation). Instead, spray the lens cleaner onto a soft cloth and use the cloth to clean the lenses.

Don’t use:

  • Water
  • Chemicals
  • Abrasive materials
  • Ultrasonic cleaners

Alcohol, acetone, and other solvents may damage the frame’s finish and electronics.

If oils or debris get trapped between the lenses and frame, remove the lenses and clean them separately. Wipe the eye wire or groove of the frame with a damp cloth before reinserting the lenses.

  • Safety and Compliance Information for Echo Frames
  • Safety and Compliance Information for Amazon Echo Frames (2nd Generation)
  • Safety and Compliance Information for Amazon Echo Frames (3rd Generation)

Cleaning Echo Loop

Clean your Echo Loop to maintain sound quality.

Cleaning your Echo Loop helps recover audio in the event that the microphones and speaker become obstructed. To clean your device, follow these steps:

  1. Mix one pump of dish soap with ½ cup of warm water.
  2. Submerge your device in this water and soak for 10 minutes.
  3. Rinse your device under warm water for one minute ensuring that the microphone and speaker perforation holes face the flow of water.
  4. Shake off residual water from your device then wipe it using a soft, lint-free cloth.
  5. Leave the device on the charger overnight to speed up drying inside the unit. Ensure the charging contact area is completely dry prior to placing the device on the charger.

Cleaning Your Echo Buds (2023 Release) Earbud Covers

How to clean the earbud covers on your Echo Buds (2023 release).

  1. Don’t run your earbud devices through water when cleaning the cover (or devices).
  2. Remove the earbud covers from your Echo Buds (2023 release) when using any liquid for cleaning.
    1. To remove earbud covers:
    2. Use your thumb and finger to hold the cover at the tip of the earbud.
    3. From the back of your earbud, gently slide the cover toward the speaker.
  3. Clean covers with a soft, dry, lint-free cloth, or soft cotton swap without any sharp objects to prevent any damage during the cover cleaning.
  4. If there’s skin oil on the cover:
    1. Clean the cover with mild hand soap with clean water.
    2. Rinse the cover thoroughly with clean water to prevent any residue on the cover.
    3. Dry it with soft, dry, lint-free cloth.
    4. Do not use the cover if they are not completely dried or dusty.
    5. Prevent trapping any liquid or water or dust in between the earbud and cover after the cleaning.
  5. Don’t use any aggressive cleaning agent that could potentially degrade the cover materials.

Note: Do not use dish soaps or other cleaning agents like household cleaners to clean cover. If you experience skin irritation, stop using the earbuds

Connect Your Home Security System to Echo Hub

Use Echo Hub to arm, disarm, and monitor your Ring Alarm or other home security system.

The Echo Hub can serve as the control panel for your connected home security system. A system connected to Alexa creates a Security shortcut on the Home Dashboard, and allows voice and touch control with Echo Hub.

Note: The following steps and procedures apply to Ring Alarm, the home security system currently compatible with Echo Hub.

To set Echo Hub to manage your Ring Alarm, load and activate the Ring skill in the Alexa app.

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  2. Open More , then select Skills & Games.

  3. Use Search Alexa Skills to find the Ring skill. Select it and then select Enable.

  4. In setting up the skill, sign in to your Ring account, to link it to your Alexa account.

  5. After you sign in, Alexa looks for Ring devices and connects with them automatically. If you don’t want a particular device to connect, select Forget.

    Your alarm system appears in your Devices list in the Alexa app.

Next, set an access code for your system, to use with Alexa and the Echo Hub.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select your Ring Alarm system, then select Settings .
  3. Under Disarm by Voice and Echo Hub, turn on Enable/disarm.
  4. Enter and confirm a 4-digit access code.

To disarm your Ring Alarm when you return home, enter the access code on your Echo Hub, by voice or by touch.

Note: Ring Alarm and all Ring Alarm accessories require a subscription for in-app features and notifications, including arming / disarming, and integration with other Ring, Echo, Alexa, and third-party products.

Control Echo Devices with Tap Gestures

Tap your device to control audio, including media playback, alarms, and calls.

You can use Tap Gestures on Echo Dot (5th Generation or later), Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio (2025 release) or later and Echo Pop devices. Tap the top of your device with your fingers in place of some voice commands.

Table 1. How to Use Tap Gestures

  • To Do This:: Pause/resume media; Tap Your Echo Device Like This:: Tap the top of the device to pause active media playback. Tap again to resume playback. Pausing media for 15 minutes stops playback, and tap to resume is no longer possible. Restart playback to continue listening.
  • To Do This:: End calls; Tap Your Echo Device Like This:: Tap once on the device while in a call.
  • To Do This:: End Drop-ins; Tap Your Echo Device Like This:: Tap once on the device while in a Drop In.
  • To Do This:: Dismiss Timers; Tap Your Echo Device Like This:: Tap once on the device while a timer is ringing.
  • To Do This:: Snooze alarms; Tap Your Echo Device Like This:: Tap once on the device while an alarm is sounding. Snooze alarm taps also work with: - Echo Dot with clock 3rd Generation - Echo Dot 3rd Generation - Echo Dot with clock 4th Generation - Echo Dot 4th Generation - Echo Dot Max - Echo Pop - Echo Show 5 - Echo Show 5 2nd Generation - Echo Show 5 3rd Generation - Echo Spot - Echo Studio (2025 release)

Tip: If Tap Gestures don’t work on your Echo device, confirm that the Microphones & Camera Disable/Enable light is off. Try tapping more firmly on the device. Tap Gestures work best when you use the midsection of your fingers, not your fingertips.

To turn off Tap Gestures on a device:

  1. Open the Alexa app.
  2. Select Devices.
  3. Select a device.
  4. Select Settings.
  5. In the general section, select Tap Gestures.
  6. Turn on/off Tap Control.

Control Echo Frames (2nd Gen) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen) with Alexa Hands-Free

Replace actions on your Echo Frames (2nd Gen) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen) by using the wake word with simple voice commands.

  • To resume media playback, say, “Resume” or “Play.”

Note: Volume can’t be changed during a phone call.

Customize Your Home Dashboard on Echo Hub

Add or change the widgets managing your smart home devices and groups.

Echo Hub creates your Home Dashboard automatically, building widgets and shortcuts that connect you with smart home devices and routines in your account. You can arrange and configure the dashboard to work best with your Smart Home setup.

Home Panel Widgets

The dashboard Home panel can hold widgets in any category, and you can add any widget multiple times. To add a widget:

  1. Say “Open widget gallery,” or swipe left to the end of the row of widgets, then select Widget Gallery .
  2. Browse to find the widget you want, or select a category to look in.
  3. Select the widget that you want to add.
  4. Select Back to return to the Home panel.

Note: You can add widgets only on the Home panel.

To remove a widget, press and hold the widget, then select Remove Widget .

Arrange Widgets, Panels, and Shortcuts

To change the order of widgets, panels or shortcuts:

  1. Press and hold on the widget row or panel list and then select Edit .

  2. Select Rearrange.

  3. Press and hold the handles on any dashboard item, then drag it into the order that you want.

    Tip: Dashboard items can only be rearranged within their own lists. For example, you can’t move a widget in among the shortcuts, or a shortcut into the panels list.

  4. Select Done to go back to the dashboard.

To hide or add a Smart Home Group panel:

  1. Press and hold on the widget row or panel list and then select Edit .
  2. Select Configure.
  3. To hide a panel, select on its name in the list.
  4. To restore a hidden panel, scroll down the list to find hidden panels, and select for the panels you want.
  5. Select Done to go back to the dashboard.

Note: The Home and Routines panels can’t be moved or hidden.

Configure Smart Home Widgets

Three widgets - Smart Home Cameras, Smart Home Groups, and Smart Home Favorites - allow you to configure them for a Group or device set of your choice.

For example, configure the Smart Home Group widget to present your Living Room group on the Dashboard. Configure the Smart Home Cameras widget to feature a set of cameras to give you the widest view around your house.

To configure a Smart Home widget:

  1. Press and hold the widget, then select Configure. Then:
    • To set a Smart Home Group widget, select the Group that you want featured on the widget. For more Groups to select, add Smart Home Groups in the Alexa app.
    • To set a Smart Home Cameras widget, select a camera, to add as many as six tiles to the widget. Use the arrows to change the order of the tiles. If the widget holds an odd number of tiles, the first one in order appears larger.
  2. Select Done .

Tip: Add multiple Smart Home widgets to your dashboard, and configure them to manage a different Group or set of devices. For example, add two more Smart Home Group widgets to the dashboard, one for Office Group and another for Kitchen Group.

Configure the Smart Home Favorites widget in the Alexa app. Open Home and under Favorites, select Edit. Add or remove devices as favorites to be managed with the Smart Home Favorites widget.

Manage Panels: Smart Home Groups and Devices

The panels on the left of the dashboard give you access to your Alexa Routines and to your Smart Home Groups. Select the Routines panel to start one or more routines remotely. Select a Smart Home Group panel, for example, Living Room, to manage any or all devices in the Living Room group.

To change panels, or their contents, change or add Smart Home Groups by voice or in the Alexa app.

  • To add a Smart Home Group panel on the dashboard, say, “Create a Group,” or build one in the Alexa app. To change devices shown in a panel, use the Alexa app to add or remove devices in the Group.
  • Routines shown in the Routines panel change when you add, remove, or change a Routine in the Alexa app.

Note: Changes made in the Alexa app might take a few minutes to appear on the dashboard.

  • Connect Smart Home Devices to Alexa
  • Create Smart Home Groups for Alexa
  • Create an Alexa Routine in the Alexa App
  • Use Active Media on Echo Hub

Display a Live Feed From Your Alexa App

Use your Alexa app to display a home monitoring live feed from an Echo device with a camera.

To display a live feed from your Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  2. Select Devices.

  3. Select the name of your device.

  4. Select Live View.

    A live feed from your device appears.

  • Display a Live Feed with Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Display a Live Feed on Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) and Echo Show 11 (2025 release) from Your Alexa App

Use your Alexa app to display a live feed from an Echo device with a screen.

To display a live feed from your Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select the name of your device.
  4. Select Live View .

A live feed from your device appears.

Note: You can only access Live Feed when you enable your device camera. To learn how to enable/disable the camera, go to Enable or Disable the Camera on Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) or Echo Show 11 (2025 release).

Display a Live Feed with Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Use your Echo device with a screen to access the live feed from another Echo device with a screen.

To access the live feed of your Echo device with a screen, Home Monitoring must be turned on. To turn on Home Monitoring, please refer to Set Up Your Echo Devices with a Screen for Home Monitoring. The display device doesn’t need home monitoring setup.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

To access the live feed from your dashboard:

  1. Say, “Go to Smart Home,” or navigate to the Smart Home dashboard on your device:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu on your screen, and then select Smart Home.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Smart Home.
  2. Select the tile of the device you want to see.

Tip: To access the live feed by voice, say, “Show me” followed by the name of your Echo Show device.

When using the live feed, double tap to zoom in, or use a pinching motion to zoom out. If the live feed is on an Echo Show 10, you can swipe left or right on the screen to move the camera.

Display a Live Feed with Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) or Echo Show 11 (2025 release)

Use your Echo device with a screen to access the live feed from another Echo device with a camera.

To access the live feed:

  1. Say, “Go to Smart Home,” or select the Menu icon.
  2. Select Smart Home.
  3. Select the tile of the device that you want to see.

Tip: To access the live feed by voice, say, “Show me” followed by the name of your Echo Show device.

Display Multiple Camera Feeds on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Ask Alexa to show up to four feeds from your cameras.

To display live feeds from multiple cameras connected to Alexa, you can say:

  • “Show my cameras.”
  • “Show me my [backyard] cameras” (for a smart home device group called “backyard”)

Display up to four live camera feeds together on:

  • Echo Show 8
  • Echo Show 10
  • Echo Show 11 (2025 release)
  • Echo Show 15
  • Echo Show 21

Display up to two live camera feeds together on:

  • Echo Show 5

Select a camera feed to zoom it to full screen and hear audio from that camera. For two-way audio with the camera you’re viewing, turn off mute on the screen. Select back on the screen to return to the multiple feeds view.

Note: When showing multiple camera feeds, Alexa can include feeds from most “Works with Alexa” cameras, including doorbell cameras. Alexa can’t include feeds from cameras on Echo Show devices.

Alexa shows the feeds with the most recent activity, such as motion, person, or package detections.

Dual Connect with Echo Buds

Enjoy music or make calls with just your left ear, right ear, or both buds at the same time.

Playback pauses when one or both of the earbuds are removed from your ear.

To resume playback on one earbud:

  • Single-tap the earbud that’s in your ear.
  • Ask Alexa.
  • Press the play button in your music app.

Note: When you start with a single earbud, then switch to both earbuds, on-ear detection automatically syncs both your earbuds and playback continues without interruption.

Echo Auto (1st Generation) Loses Bluetooth Connection

Follow these steps to resolve most issues with Bluetooth connectivity.

[Embedded video omitted]

Check if Echo Auto is connected to your phone between each troubleshooting step:

  1. Force close the Alexa app, and then launch it again.
  2. Unplug the micro-USB power cable from your Echo Auto (1st Generation). Wait 30 seconds, and then plug it back in.
  3. For Android phones: Turn on Airplane mode on your phone. Wait 45 seconds, and then turn it off. For iOS phones: Turn off Bluetooth on your phone and then turn it on.
  4. Restart your smartphone.
  5. Go to your Echo Auto settings in the Alexa app and forget the device. Then go to your phone’s Bluetooth settings to check if your phone is connected to Echo Auto. If your phone is already connected to Echo Auto:
    1. Unpair or forget the connection.
    2. Unplug the micro-USB power cable from your Echo Auto. Wait 45 seconds, and then plug it back in.
    3. Open the Alexa app and complete the setup again.
  6. Factory reset Echo Auto and complete setup in the Alexa app.

Echo Buds (2021 Release, 2nd Generation) Aren’t Pairing with a New iOS Device

If your Echo Buds aren’t paired with your iOS device, try these steps:

  1. Unpair Echo Buds from your mobile device’s Bluetooth settings.
    1. Open Your mobile device’s Bluetooth settings.
    2. Select your Echo Buds and Forget This Device.
  2. Remove Echo Buds from your Alexa account.
    1. Open the Alexa app.
    2. Select Devices, then All Devices.
    3. If your Echo Buds are listed, select them and Deregister.
  3. Factory Reset Your Echo Buds.
  4. Restart your mobile device.

Tip: If your Echo Buds still won’t pair after these steps, change the language in your iOS settings, follow the pairing steps, then return to the original language.

Echo Device Can’t Connect to Wi-Fi During Setup

Your device won’t connect to the Internet during setup.

Try the following steps to resolve connection issues during setup:

  • Check that you have the latest version of the Alexa app.
  • If your Echo device has eero Built-in, follow Connect Your Echo Device to Your eero Network. You must have your eero Network installed first before connecting your Echo device to eero.
  • Try the tips listed in Echo Device Is Having Wi-Fi Issues.
  • Restart Your Alexa Enabled Device
  • If all the previous steps fail, Reset Your Echo Device.
  • Try setup again using your phone as a Wi-Fi hotspot.

Tip: If you are experiencing connection issues on multiple devices, contact your Internet Service Provider.

Echo Device Is Having Bluetooth Issues

Your Echo device can’t pair to Bluetooth or your Bluetooth connection drops.

  • Make sure that your Echo device has the latest software update. Say, “Check for software updates.”

  • Make sure that your Bluetooth device uses a supported Bluetooth profile. Alexa supports:

    • Advanced Audio Distribution Profile (A2DP SNK)
    • Audio/Video Remote Control Profile

  • Move your Bluetooth and Echo devices away from sources of possible interference (such as microwaves, baby monitors, and other wireless devices).

  • Make sure that your Bluetooth device is fully charged and close to your Echo device when pairing.

  • If you’ve previously paired your Bluetooth device, remove your paired Bluetooth device from Alexa. Then try pairing it again.

Echo Device Is Having Wi-Fi Issues

Echo device can’t connect to Wi-Fi or has intermittent connectivity issues.

Note: In case your device loses its Internet connection and doesn’t reconnect, first try to Restart Your Alexa Enabled Device. If that doesn’t work, or if your device has intermittent connectivity issues, try the following steps to resolve most Wi-Fi issues:

  • Make sure that your Echo device is within 30 feet (or 10 meters) of your wireless router.
  • Check that your Echo device is away from any devices that cause interference (such as microwaves, baby monitors, or other electronic devices).
  • Check that your router is working. Check the connection with another device to determine if it’s an issue with your Echo device or with your network.
    • If other devices can’t connect, restart your Internet router and/or modem. While your network hardware restarts, unplug the power adapter from your Echo device for 30 seconds, then plug it back in. Make sure that you’re using the included power adapter for your Echo device.
    • If other devices are able to connect, make sure you’re using the correct Wi-Fi password. You can also try turning off some of your other devices temporarily to reduce interference and see if that affects your Echo device’s ability to connect.
  • If you have several devices connected to your Wi-Fi network, turn some of them off temporarily. That way you can check if multiple connected devices are impacting your Echo device’s ability to connect.
  • Check if your router has separate network names (also called SSID) for the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands. If you have separate network names, try moving your device from one network to the other.
    • For example, if your router has both “MyHome-2.4” and “MyHome-5” wireless networks. Disconnect from the network that you’re using (MyHome-2.4) and try to connect to the other one (MyHome-5).
  • If your Wi-Fi password has recently changed, Update the Wi-Fi Settings for Your Echo Device or Update the Wi-Fi Settings on Your Echo Show.
  • If your device is still having intermittent connection issues, Reset Your Echo Device.

Tip: If you’re experiencing connection issues on multiple devices, it might be a network issue. You can wait a few hours and try again if there’s a network outage, or contact your Internet Service Provider.

Echo Device Low Power Mode

Low Power Mode reduces energy consumption on your Echo smart speaker or smart display when it’s idle, except in certain situations.

When an Echo smart speaker or smart display is idle, it seeks energy efficiency gains through a suite of Low Power Mode optimizations to reduce its energy consumption. You do not need to manually turn Low Power Mode on or off. Your device exits Low Power Mode when you interact with it, including when you use the wake word, press any button, step in front of the camera (Echo Show devices only, when camera shutter is open and device is not muted), touch the display (Echo Show devices only), or change certain device settings using the Alexa app.

Certain features or use cases prevent your devices from entering Low Power Mode. These include:

  • eero Built-in
  • Connecting your Echo device to an external speaker or device using an auxiliary cable.

Other features or use cases prevent your devices from maximizing the energy efficiency gains from Low Power Mode in an idle state. These include:

  • Ultrasonic Motion Detection, for example, for use in Occupancy Routines or Alexa Together. For more information about Motion Detection, go to What Is Ultrasound Motion Detection?.
  • Active Smart Home connections.
  • Amazon Sidewalk.
  • Multi-room Music and Alexa Home Theater
  • Connecting your Echo device to an external speaker or device through Bluetooth.

Also, certain conditions can impact the energy efficiency of your Echo devices. These conditions include: a noisy environment, an environment with unusual light level fluctuations, the mic/camera on/off button is turned off on your Echo Show device, the camera shutter is closed on your Echo Show device, your Echo Show is in Do Not Disturb mode, or having a nearby Echo device that hasn’t completed setup.

Note: Features and use cases listed may not be available in all countries or for all Echo devices.

Echo Frames (2nd Generation) Aren’t Holding a Charge

Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are having charging issues or are draining battery too quickly.

  1. When charging, make sure that the charging cable is attached to your device and the power adapter is securely plugged into the USB power.
  2. Make sure the power LED on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) lights up when you’re charging the device.
  3. If the power LED doesn’t light up, press and hold the action button until the status light flashes red. Then try charging again. The action button is the shorter button on the right arm of the frames.
  4. Check the battery status by turning the device back on. Alexa reads the battery level to you. You can also check the battery level in your phone’s Bluetooth settings menu.
  5. Try lowering the volume during use. The battery drains faster at higher volumes.
  • Adjust the Volume on Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Echo Frames (2nd Generation) Lose Bluetooth Connection

To resolve most issues with Bluetooth connectivity, press the action button.

Tip: If you’re experiencing interference with other Bluetooth devices, try to reduce the number of active Bluetooth devices around you.

Check the connection between your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and your phone between each troubleshooting step by asking Alexa a question. If Alexa responds, your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) have reconnected.

  1. Make sure that:
    1. Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are 100 percent battery and on.
    2. The microphones on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are on.
    3. The volume is greater than 60 percent.
  2. Check your smartphone’s Bluetooth settings. Make sure that Bluetooth is on for your phone and that Echo Frames are connected and active.
  3. In the Alexa app, open Devices and navigate to your Echo Frames device. Check that your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are Online.
  4. Turn your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) off and back on again. Then force quit the Alexa app and reopen it.

Echo Frames and Smart Glasses with Alexa Aren’t Pairing with Your Phone

If your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) can’t pair with your phone, try these solutions.

  • Select Forget Device for your smart glasses from Device Settings in the Alexa app.
  • Forget your smart glasses in your phone’s Bluetooth menu.
  • Check that your smart glasses aren’t listed in your phone’s Bluetooth menu.
  • Update the Alexa app to the latest version.
  • For Echo Frames (2nd Generation), hold down the action button for ten seconds or until you see the blinking red and blue status light.
  • For Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation), press and hold the front and back action buttons for three seconds. The light blinks orange to show you’re in pairing mode.
  • Relaunch the Alexa app.
  • To set up your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) or Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation), follow the steps described in the Alexa app.
  • To pair your device to the Alexa app again, open the Alexa app and follow the on-screen prompts.

If these steps don’t work, try resetting your device.

Echo Hub Display Changes When I Approach

Echo Hub detects when someone is nearby, and automatically switches to the Home Dashboard.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

Echo Hub shows idle screen content, such as photos, clock, and weather, when it’s not busy. Auto-wake automatically transitions the display to the Home Dashboard when someone is within about 3 feet (1 meter) of the device.

When Auto-wake is off, Echo Hub displays idle screen content, or is dark, until it receives a touch or voice command.

To turn off Auto-wake:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Device Options.
  3. Select Proximity Detection.
  4. Turn off Auto Wake.

Auto-wake also turns off when you press the device Mute button, or when the device is in Night mode.

Echo Hub Setup Isn’t Working

Troubleshooting tips to resolve some of the most common setup issues.

Ensure that the device has enough power to start.

  • We recommend that you use the power adapter and cable that came with your Echo Hub. If you use a different adapter, make sure it supports device power requirements. Echo Hub power supply must comply with USB PD protocol and support both 5V/2.4A and 9V/3A ratings.
  • If you’re using Power Over Ethernet (PoE), the Echo Hub can’t connect directly to the Ethernet router. PoE also requires a PoE injector and PoE network switch to provide both power and data.

Ensure that your Echo Hub and your smart devices have good Wi-Fi available.

  • Try the tips in Echo Device Is Having Wi-Fi Issues.
  • If some devices can’t connect with the Echo Hub, try Checking Wi-Fi Connectivity on Smart Home Devices.
  • If you have connection issues with multiple devices, contact your internet service provider.

If some of your smart devices don’t appear in the Echo Hub dashboard:

  • Make sure that the devices and your Echo Hub are in the same Alexa account. Check this in your Alexa app.
  • Check that your smart device is compatible with Alexa. Use the manufacturer’s app to connect the device to Alexa. If using the device with Alexa requires an Alexa skill, make sure you’ve installed the skill from the Alexa app, and finished linking the account.
  • Confirm in the Alexa app which Alexa Smart Home Group the devices belong to.
  • Make sure that your smart devices connect to Wi-Fi or a smart home hub, if they require it.
  • To appear in the dashboard, Echo Show devices must have Home Monitoring turned on. Learn how to Set Up Your Echo Devices with a Screen for Home Monitoring.
  • Some device types or scenes that appear in your Alexa app, but not in the dashboard, may not yet have dashboard tiles. You can control such devices by voice or when they’re part of a routine, and receive announcements for them.

If these steps don’t resolve the problem, try restarting your Echo Hub. Press and hold the Mute button until the device restarts. Or, you can unplug its power adapter for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.

If a device restart doesn’t work, reset the device to factory settings. Learn how to Reset Your Echo Hub.

Echo Link Amp Hardware Guide

Echo Link Amp has multiple ports to connect audio equipment.

[Image: Echo Link Amp Audio Input Panel]

Headphone Jack

A 3.5 mm amplified headphone jack that’s located on the front of Echo Link Amp.

Subwoofer Out

Plug in the RCA cable of a powered subwoofer to this port.

Note: Wireless subwoofers aren’t compatible with this device.

Analog / Coaxial / Optical Out

Use these outputs to connect your stereo receiver, amplifier, or powered speakers.

Analog / Coaxial / Optical In

Use these inputs to plug in a cable from an audio component, like a CD player, MP3 player, or amplified turntable.

Speaker Out/Binding Posts

Connect passive speakers (speakers without power) using speaker wire or banana jack cables.

Ethernet

You can use the Ethernet port as an alternative way to connect Echo Link to your network after you set up your device with Wi-Fi.

Power

Plug in the power adapter included in the box to give Echo Link power.

Echo Link or Echo Link Amp Does Not Play Music

Internet connectivity issues can cause music to buffer or not play.

  • Check that your cables are plugged into your device and audio system or speakers. Make sure the cables fit properly and match the port you’re using.

  • Check that your cables work with other audio devices, if available.

  • Check that your speakers or audio system works with other inputs.

  • Make sure that your speakers, audio system, or other input devices are turned on and the volume on all devices are turned up.

  • Check that the correct input on the stereo system is selected.

  • Make sure that your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp is powered on.

  • Check that your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp are online and visible in the Alexa app. If your device isn’t in there, or shows as “offline”, try setting up the device again.

  • Check that other devices connected to your Wi-Fi network are working. You can verify that your mic-enabled Echo device is connected by asking, “What time is it?”

  • Make sure that you are using supported input and output formats (for example, Uncompressed PCM) with your stereo system and Echo Link or Echo Link Amp.

  • If you’re streaming over Bluetooth, try pairing your Bluetooth device again.

  • For Multi-Room Music:

    • Check that Echo Link or Echo Link Amp are in the Multi-Room Music Group.
    • Make sure that all your Echo devices are on the same Wi-Fi network.

  • If your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp are in a Smart Home Device Group:

    • Confirm that your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp is the Preferred Speaker.
    • Check that your Group contains a mic-enabled Echo device (like Echo Dot).

  • If your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp is not the Preferred Speaker, or not in a Group, add the name of the device to your voice requests. For example, “Play music on [device name].”

Echo Link or Echo Link Amp Lost Ethernet Connection

To solve most issues with connectivity, restart your device.

A red LED on the back of the device means it has lost internet access.

  • Restart Echo Link or Echo Link Amp by unplugging and plugging it back in.

  • Plug the Ethernet cable into another device and confirm that you have access to the Internet.

  • Unplug the Ethernet cable and press the Action button for 6 seconds. Use the Alexa app to go through Wi-Fi setup again.

  • If the previous steps don’t work, reset your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp. Then complete Wi-Fi setup in the Alexa app and reconnect the Ethernet cable when prompted.

Echo Loop Charging Issues

Experiencing charging issues? Try the following steps.

  1. To charge your device plug the micro-USB cable into the charging cradle and the other end into a USB power adapter (5W or higher and safety-certified for your region).
  2. When placing your ring on the cradle, line up the charging contacts on the ring with the charging contacts on the cradle.
  3. Make sure the LED on your Echo Loop’s charging cradle lights up when you’re charging the device.
  4. If the LED doesn’t light up:
    1. Make sure the charging contacts on Echo Loop line up with the contacts on the charging cradle.
    2. Make sure the charging contacts on the Echo Loop are clean by using a soft, lint-free cloth to wipe away any lotion debris.

Echo Loop Loses Connection

Force closing the Alexa app and restarting your Echo Loop solves many issues related to connectivity.

Note: Check your Echo Loop connection to your phone between each troubleshooting step by asking Alexa a question. If Alexa responds, your Echo Loop has reconnected.

  • Make sure that your Echo Loop is charged and turned on.

  • Check your smartphone’s Bluetooth settings. Make sure that Bluetooth is enabled on your phone and that Echo Loop is connected and active.

  • Turn your Echo Loop off and back on again.

  • Force quit the Alexa app then reopen it.

  • Turn Bluetooth off and on again on your phone, then select Echo Loop from the list to reconnect it.

  • Factory reset your device then complete setup in the Alexa app.

Enable or Disable the Camera on Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) or Echo Show 11 (2025 release)

Use your device’s settings to enable or disable your camera.

Note: The camera on your device is enabled by default. Turning off the camera disables some features.

You can enable/disable your camera through the Microphones & Camera Enable/Disable button, which turns off both the microphones and camera.

You can also enable/disable just the camera from your device:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:

    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings .
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings .

  2. Select Privacy & Permissions.

  3. Select Camera Access.

  4. Toggle Camera to enable or disable the camera.

    A Camera Disabled appears on the screen when the camera is disabled.

You can also enable/disable the camera from the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select the name of your device.
  4. Select Settings .
  5. Select Camera Settings.
  6. Enable/disable camera.

When you set up your Echo device with a screen, you can create a Visual ID for each member of your household. You can also set up Visual ID later.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select
  3. Select Settings.

To enroll in Visual ID from your Echo devices with a screen, go to: Enroll in Visual ID on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

Factory Reset Your Echo Buds

If your Echo Buds are unresponsive, or you want to erase your device settings, factory reset your device.

Note: Having trouble with your Echo Buds? Restart your Echo Buds first: place your Echo Buds in the case close the case, and wait 30 seconds. Before you start a factory reset, try playing music again.

[Embedded video omitted]

If that doesn’t work:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Check if Echo Buds are listed. If yes, select the device and select Forget Device.
  4. Unpair Echo Buds from your phone’s Bluetooth settings.
  5. Put your Echo Buds in the case and charge until the LED is green.
  6. With your Echo Buds in the case, close the case, and press the button on the case for 15 seconds.
  7. Release the button when the LED begins flashing orange. When the LED stops flashing orange the factory reset is done.
  8. Go to Set Up Your Echo Buds to start setup again.

Note: After a factory reset, you must unpair your Echo device from any other paired devices, such as a laptop or tablet. After setting up your Echo Buds, you can pair them to a new device in the Alexa app.

Fit Echo Buds (2019 release, 1st gen) to Your Ear

Use the right sized ear and wing tips to improve comfort and audio quality.

[Embedded video omitted]

To test your eartip fit:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select your Echo Buds device.
  4. Select Eartip Sizing Test.

Important: If the Eartip Sizing Test isn’t in the Alexa app, your Echo Buds (1st Gen) need a software update. Software updates happen while your Echo Buds are in the case and the lid is closed. Check the Alexa app again in 24 hours.

When exercising, try the wing tip to create a comfortable, secure fit.

Note: Make sure the horizontal lines on the wing tips align with the top of the letter R or L on the bud. When placing Echo Buds in the charging case, press down on each bud until the LED light turns green. Then close the case.

Fit Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) to Your Ear

Use the correctly sized ear and wing tips to improve comfort and audio quality.

[Embedded video omitted]

Tip: To find the best fit, test different ear tip sizes and choose the one that is both comfortable and provides a snug fit. Your Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) come with four ear tip sizes. You may need a different ear tip size for each ear. Use the Amazon smile logo to orient the ear bud. Turn the ear bud so the smile logo is right-side up. Then place the ear bud in your ear and rotate slightly to get a secure fit.

To test your ear tip fit:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. On the home screen, locate the Echo Buds card.
  3. Tap the settings icon on the card.
  4. Select Ear Tip Fit Test.

When exercising, try the wing tip for a secure fit.

Note: The wing tips may provide a more secure fit for some. To find the best fit, try your Echo Buds with and without the wing tips. To use the wing tips: place the left wing tip, marked with an L, around the left ear bud, also marked with an L. Don’t cover the IR sensor on the ear bud. Remove the ear tip from the ear bud before attaching or detaching the wing tips. To avoid tearing the wing tip, hold it by the wing and pull gently when you attach or detach it.

Fit Echo Buds (2023 Release) to Your Ear

Find your preferred fit to improve comfort and audio quality.

Echo Buds (2023 release) come with preinstalled, removable, silicone earbud covers for comfort. Your Echo Buds (2023 release) should rest comfortably from your ears.

If you prefer a roomier fit, remove the silicone earbud covers:

  1. Use your thumb and finger to hold the cover at the tip of the earbud.
  2. From the back of your earbud, gently slide the cover toward the speaker.

Tip: Avoid pinching the cover with your fingernail tip.

To put the silicone earbud covers on your Echo Buds (2023 release):

  1. Place the cover onto the earbud so that the cover’s holes line up with the earbud’s speaker and audio port.
  2. Use your thumb and finger to gently pull the cover around the earbud until snug.
  3. When complete, the cover shouldn’t block the earbud’s speaker or audio port.

Note: An additional pair of silicone earbud covers are included in the box.

Echo Buds are semi-in-ear earbuds designed to keep you connected to your surroundings.

  • Echo Buds are designed to gently rest in your ear to deliver a barely there feeling and should not be wedged into the ear canal.
  • Semi-in-ear earbuds do not use ear tips and do not seal off the ear canal, allowing the user to hear outside noise whether riding through busy traffic or tranquil nature.
  • Echo Buds design allows for unobstructed air flow and cooling ventilation for your ear canal.

[Image: earbud direction image]

Ear Placement Procedure

Gently place the earbuds in your ear so they rest naturally. They should evoke a ‘barely there’ feeling (for long term comfort). Do not push towards ear canal to block sounds - Echo Buds (2023 Release) are designed to allow external sounds in for awareness.

For natural fit, you may need to rotate your earbuds once placed in your ear. Typically, the bottom tip of your Echo Buds should point in the direction of your mouth.

Note: The stability ring in Echo Buds (2023 Release) are designed to provide extra grip and stability during activities. This ring is not an ear tip and does not seal the ear canal. Please do not push further inside your ear.

[Image: stability ring]

Ear Fit FAQ

Buds Feel Larger in Ear: Echo Buds (2023 release) come with preinstalled, removable, silicone earbud covers for comfort. For some ears these covers are not needed and can be removed to make the buds slightly smaller.

Buds fit well, but uncomfortable over time: Please make sure to follow the insertion steps above. Your Echo Buds are designed to naturally rest in your ear and not block the ear canal. They should allow outside noises in to keep you aware of your surroundings.

Buds feel like they will fall out, but haven’t fallen out: Traditional earbuds use ear tips and other stabilization aids to help wedge the bud in ear. Echo Buds (2023 Release) are designed to rest naturally in ear for comfort. They are not designed to provide the wedged in feeling similar to traditional earbuds. If the loose feeling persists, perform a vigorous head shakes or jumping motion to see if the buds stay secure in ear.

Buds feel small in ear, falls out with activity: Since ear sizes are unique, Echo Buds (2023 Release) may feel loose in some ears. If open style earbuds fall out of your ears, Echo Buds (2023 Release) may exhibit a similar fit as well.

For Opticians: Adjust Echo Frames for Fit

Adjust the Echo Frames temple tips for a better fit.

Important: The temple tips are the only adjustable parts on Echo Frames.

Don’t apply heat from the metal accent to the frame front or adjust with pliers. Don’t bend the temple tips while the material is cold or use your fingernails to adjust the temple tips.

To adjust the temple tips:

  1. Heat the temple tip to approximately 100 – 120°F. Apply the heat in 10 second intervals until the acetate is pliable enough to be properly adjusted. Don’t over heat.
  2. After heating, hold the metal accent to provide support. With the other hand, gently bend the temple tip downward and inward until you achieve the desired form.
  3. Hold the temple tip in the desired form until the frame cools.
  • Echo Frames Optician Card (PDF)

For Opticians: Edging, Inserting, and Removing Lenses for Echo Frames

Instructions on how to fit or remove lenses for Echo Frames.

Edging

Trace and edge prescription lenses to the actual size of the frame, accounting for calibration of edger.

Don’t cut lenses oversized. This can stretch or put pressure on the frame and damage the electronics.

Echo Frames have a “U” groove bevel. However, you can use a standard “V” bevel when cutting lenses.

Tip: You may need to adjust the size of the cut lens to allow for a proper fit.

Inserting and Removing Lenses

Important: Don’t heat the frames to insert or remove lenses. Use cold mount only.

If you send Echo Frames to a lab for fitting, include “cold mount only” as a physical or digital note along with the frames.

Gently insert the lenses from the front of the frame. To remove the lenses, apply pressure to the back of the lens near the top outer edge. Then push them out.

  • Amazon Device Return FAQs
  • Echo Frames Optician Card (PDF)

For Opticians: What Kind of Prescriptions Work with Echo Frames?

Echo Frames have been tested for +3.00 diopter to -6.00 diopter prescriptions.

For best results, keep the base curve of the prescription lenses as close to 4.25 diopters as possible.

If desired, progressive lenses may be used but the pantoscopic tilt can’t be adjusted. Do not use heat.

Aspheric polycarbonate, Trivex, or high-index lenses are recommended to minimize weight.

Help Loved Ones Set Up Their Echo Devices with a Screen Remotely

If loved ones have difficulty setting up an Echo Show, family members or caregivers can help with the setup remotely.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

If you’re gifting an Echo Show and want to do remote setup, send the device to yourself first and choose the gift option at shipping to prevent the device from syncing to your account.

Before sending the Echo Show to your loved one, you can set it to connect to your loved one’s Wi-Fi network.

First, plug in the device to start initial setup:

  1. Tap the screen and select a language.
  2. Select your Wi-Fi network name from the list of available networks.
  3. Enter the Wi-Fi password, then tap done in the bottom right corner.
  4. Type in your loved one’s Amazon account email and password and tap Sign in at the bottom.
  5. Confirm the time zone and tap Continue to complete setup.

After setup is complete, use the following steps to save your loved one’s Wi-Fi network:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Device Options.
  3. Select Network.
  4. Scroll down and select Add a Network under Preferences.
  5. Type in the name of your loved one’s network.
  6. Use the drop-down arrow under Security and select WPA/WPA2 PSK.
  7. Type in the password (case sensitive) under Wi-Fi Password.
  8. Select Save.

You can now unplug Echo Show, re-package it and send it to your loved one. When your loved one plugs in the power adapter, the Echo Show connects to the Wi-Fi network that you set. To complete setup, your loved one only needs to sign in to their Amazon account when prompted on the screen to register the device.

How Can I Hide the Echo Hub Power Cable?

Tips to help put excess power cable out of sight.

[Embedded video omitted]

Install your Echo Hub anywhere an electrical outlet is nearby. There are a few ideas to help hide the power cable between the device and the power outlet.

  • Hide extra cable in the wall mount cavity on the back of the device. Loop the excess cable and press it gently into the notches on the back of the device. Leave enough cable length to reach the power outlet after mounting the device.
  • Use a shorter USB-C cable. The Echo Hub works with most USB-C cables, as long as they allow sufficient power to the device. If you find a shorter cable compatible with Echo Hub power requirements, you can use it.
  • Use on-wall cable management, such as cord hiders. Use hiders when you don’t want to make holes in your wall. Many come in different lengths, and are paintable.
  • Use in-wall cable pass-throughs, or grommets. Pass-throughs allow easy routing of the power cable behind the wall. Many come with a saw or drill bit that creates the correct size hole. Install one behind the Hub mounting bracket, and the other near the power outlet. Follow the manufacturer’s installation instructions.

Tip: The Hub’s mounting bracket matches the size of most standard in-wall electric boxes. If an installed electric box is convenient, you can use it as one of the cable pass-through points.

  • Use a Power Over Ethernet (PoE) port. If your home has Ethernet wiring, which supports PoE+ or PoE++, you can use a PoE port instead of the Hub power cable. This connection also requires a PoE switch or a PoE injector.
