How Does Calling and Messaging Work On Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses

  with Alexa (3rd Generation)? {#how-does-calling-and-messaging-work-on-echo-frames-2nd-gener}

Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) use data or minutes from your smartphone plan for calling and messaging.

  • When you ask Alexa to make calls, your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) route the call through your smartphone using your plan minutes.

  • Android only: When you ask Alexa to send messages, your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) route the messages through your smartphone using SMS messaging.

  • Alexa-to-Alexa calls and messages use data from your smartphone plan unless you’re connected to Wi-Fi.

  • Make Alexa Calls with Your Voice

  • Turn Phone Notifications On or Off for Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

How is Calling and Messaging Different with Echo Auto?

Echo Auto uses data or minutes and texts from your smartphone plan for calling and Alexa Calling and Messaging.

  • Calls to phone numbers use your plan minutes.
  • Texts to phone numbers use your plan texts.
  • Alexa-to-Alexa calls and messages use data from your smartphone plan.

Note: Charges may vary depending on your smartphone plan or service provider.

  • Echo Auto (1st Gen) Text messaging is supported with Android only.
  • Echo Auto (2nd Gen) Text messaging is supported on iOS and Android.

How Is Calling and Messaging Different with Echo Buds?

Echo Buds use data or minutes and texts from your mobile provider for calling and messaging.

  • Calls to phone numbers use your minutes.
  • Texts to phone numbers use your text allowance (Android only).
  • Alexa-to-Alexa calls and messages use data from your mobile phone provider.

How is Calling and Messaging Different with Echo Loop?

Echo Loop uses data or minutes from your smartphone plan for calling.

  • Calls to phone numbers use your phone plan minutes.
  • Texts to phone numbers use your text allowance.
  • Alexa-to-Alexa calls use data from your mobile phone provider.
  • Program one speed-dial number that is called by double-pressing the action button.
  • You can’t talk to Alexa during a call.

Note: Messaging, Inbound Drop In, and Do Not Disturb are not available with Echo Loop.

  • Set Up or Change Your Echo Loop Top Contact

How to Charge Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Wake up your new Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) to get started.

[Embedded video omitted]

  1. Use the cable to plug in the charging stand to a power source.

  2. Place the Frames on the charging stand with the lenses facing up.

    Tip: Don’t be afraid to push down until snug.

  3. A pulsing white light displays while detecting your Smart Glasses.

  4. Once the device detects proper placement, the blinking light changes to a solid color that reflects your Smart Glasses battery status.

    • A solid orange light means that the frames are charging.
    • A solid green light means that the frames are 100% charged.
    • Blinking red means there’s an error detecting your frames.

  5. When you place your Smart Glasses correctly, the blinking light shifts to a solid color, saying the battery status.

Note: Allow 2 ½ hours for a full charge.

If the LED light on your charger is off, blinking red, or blinking red and white, try these troubleshooting steps:

  1. Remove Frames from the charger for 20 seconds, and then reinsert them into the charger.
    • Open Frames temples and wait 15 seconds.
    • Close the temples and wait 10 more seconds.
    • Reinsert Frames into the charger.
  2. Check that the placement of the frames is correct:
    • The lenses should be facing up (not forward).
    • Fold the tops of the frame arms one over the other, ensuring they touch the back wall of the charger.
    • The nose bridge of the Frames should touch the front of the charger.
    Note: If difficulty arises, it may be due to previous temple tips adjustment.
  3. Try to unplug and replug the power cable from the cradle and outlet.
  4. Try using a different power source, like an alternative USB port, power adapter, or outlet.
  5. If the charging stand or frames feel warm, allow them to cool down before attempting to charge again. Ensure that your device stays away from direct sunlight and heat sources.
  • Set Up Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen)
  • Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen) Fit Adjustments
  • Get Prescription Lens for Echo Frames (2nd Gen) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen)

How to Make Calls with Echo Loop

Use the Action button to make, accept, or end phone calls.

  • What you can do: Answer or end a call; How to use the action button: Click once.

  • What you can do: Ask Alexa to call a contact or a phone number; How to use the action button: Click once, wait for the vibration, then say “Call [name/number].”

  • What you can do: Reject an incoming call; How to use the action button: Press and hold for one second.

  • What you can do: Call your top contact; How to use the action button: Double-click, and Alexa will connect the call for you.

  • Set Up or Change Your Echo Loop Top Contact

How to Reassemble Your Echo Pop

If you remove the silicone sleeve and front plate from your Echo Pop device, follow these instructions to reassemble correctly.

[Embedded video omitted]

  1. Place the silicone sleeve on the device, making sure the buttons and microphones are not covered by the sleeve.
  2. Find the slits in the front plate, located at 7 o’clock and 5 o’clock.
  3. Find the notches in the interior of the silicone sleeve, also located at 7 o’clock and 5 o’clock.
  4. Insert the front plate onto the silicone sleeve, aligning the slits and notches.
  5. Hold the front plate and pull the silicone sleeve forward around the device to ensure the front plate is securely attached.

How to Set Up the Premium Adjustable Stand For Your Echo Show

Scan the QR code on your device screen for a guided setup in the Alexa app.

Table of Contents

  • Basic Requirements
  • Compatible Echo Show Devices
  • How to Set Up the Premium Adjustable Stand

Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts and accessories ready:

  • Premium Adjustable Stand components:
    • One Stand Base
    • One mounting plate
  • In-box accessories kit:
    • One hex key
    • Four hex socket screws (M4*12 mm)
    • A Quick Start Guide
  • A compatible Echo Show device

Compatible Echo Show Devices

  • Echo Show 15
  • Echo Show 15 (2nd Generation)
  • Echo Show 21

Note: The Echo Show 21 and Echo Show 15 stands aren’t cross-compatible. You can check which stand you have by going to Your Orders.

How to Set Up the Premium Adjustable Stand

  1. Place Your Echo Show face-down on a flat surface.

  2. Pass the power adapter cable through the hole in the mounting plate handle, and then through the slot in the mounting plate.

    [Image: Power adapter cable being guided through the mounting plate handle hole first, followed by threading through the mounting plate slot]

  3. Plug the power adapter into your Echo Show device. Adjust the cord so that it fits into the slot on the back of your device.

    [Image: Power adapter cord being threaded through the mounting plate handle hole and through the mounting plate slot]

  4. Place the mounting plate on the back of your Echo Show Device.

  5. Use the hex key and hex screws provided in the box to fix the mounting plate to the back of your Echo Show device.

    [Image: Hex key being used to secure the mounting plate to Echo Show device with four hex screws at designated corner points]

  6. Fix the round base of the stand to the bottom of the cylindrical handle of the mounting plate.

  7. Tighten the screw at the bottom of the round base.

    [Image: Bottom screw of the round base being tightened to secure the stand assembly]

  8. You can now place the device at your preferred location.

To get started, download or update the Alexa app, connect to Wi-Fi and then follow the instructions provided.

Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts, accessories, and information ready:

  • Your Echo Dot (5th Generation) and power adapter.
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password.
    • Don’t have an account? To make one, go to Create an Amazon Account.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password.

How to Set Up Your Device

Video guide to set up your device

Tip: Before setup, download the Alex app from your mobile device’s app store.

To set up your device:

  1. Plug in your Echo Dot device with the included power adapter.
  2. On your mobile device, open the Alexa app .
  3. Select Devices .
  4. Select Plus .
  5. Select Add Device.
  6. Select Amazon Echo.
  7. Select Echo, Echo Dot, Echo Pop and more.
  8. Follow the instructions to set up your device.

Note: The Echo Dot has a light ring that communicates its status. For more information on what the light indicators mean, go to What do the Lights on Your Echo Speaker Mean?

Privacy and Support

To turn your device’s microphones on or off, press the Microphone button.

A blue light on the device means that Alexa is listening and processing your request in Amazon’s secure cloud.

You can review or delete your voice recording history at any time. To learn how, visit Review Your Alexa Voice History.

For more information about Alexa and privacy, visit the Alexa Privacy Hub.

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try these suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to Forgot Your Password.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, you can find more troubleshooting in Echo Device Can’t Connect to Wi-Fi During Setup.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.

For more help and troubleshooting, visit Support for Echo Dot online or go to the Help & Feedback section in the Alexa app.

Accessibility Features on Echo Devices

Echo devices have a set of features designed to enhance the user experience for customers with disabilities. This included features like Tap to Alexa, captioning, the screen magnifier, and VoiceView. For more information, go to Accessibility for Alexa.

You’re Set Up, What’s Next?

Once you’ve finished setting up your device, you can explore more features to improve your Echo Dot experience. To learn more, go to:

  • Connect Smart Home Devices to Alexa
  • Pair Your Phone or Bluetooth Speaker to Your Echo Device
  • What are Alexa Skills?

How to Set Up Your Echo Show

Video guide to set up your device

To set up your device:

  1. Plug in your Echo Show with the included power adapter.
  2. Select a device language.
  3. Connect to your Wi-Fi network.
  4. Log in to your Amazon account and register your device.
  5. Continue following the on-screen steps to set up and customize your device.

When you see the Alexa home screen and clock, your device is ready to use.

Remote Overview

Your device comes with a remote that you can use to browse and play Fire TV content on your Echo Show 15. To insert the batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press firmly and slide the cover down. For best performance, use alkaline batteries. To pair your remote, follow the steps in Pair an Alexa Voice Remote with Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen. Note: There are no LED light indicators on the Alea Voice Remote.

For an overview of button placement, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)? Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

Note: The remote controls only the Fire TV experience. While your Echo Show is on the Home screen, you can press the remote’s Home Button to launch the Fire TV experience.

Privacy and Support

Turn off the Echo Show 15 device microphones by pressing the Microphone off Button on top of the device.

A blue indicator light on the device screen means that Alexa is listening and processing your request in Amazon’s secure cloud.

You can review or delete your voice recording history at any time. To learn how, visit Review Your Alexa Voice History.

For more about Alexa and privacy, visit Alexa Privacy Hub.

For help and troubleshooting, visit Support for Echo Show 15 online, or go to Help & Feedback in the Alexa app.

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, here are some suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to Forgot Your Password.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, you can find more troubleshooting available in Echo Device Can’t Connect to Wi-Fi During Setup.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.
  • If your Echo device is highlighting on-screen items or reading them out loud when you select them, the VoiceView Screen Reader may be on. To turn off VoiceView you can say, “Turn off VoiceView,” or:
    1. Press and hold the Microphone/Camera button until there is a sound.
    2. Let go of the Microphone/Camera button.
    3. Use a single finger to double tap the screen and hold for five seconds.

Echo devices have a set of features designed to enhance the user experience for customers with disabilities. This includes features like Tap to Alexa, captioning, screen magnifier, and VoiceView. For more information, go to Accessibility for Alexa.

Set Up Your Echo Spot

Video guide to set up your device

  1. Plug in your Echo Spot device to an electrical source, using the included power adapter.

  6. Follow the on-screen instructions to set up your Echo Spot the way you want it.

How to Use the Action Button On Your Echo Loop

Use the Action button to talk to Alexa, answer or reject incoming calls, or call popular contacts.

  • What you can do: Talk to Alexa; How to use the action button: Click once, feel the vibration, then talk to Alexa.
  • What you can do: Answer or end a call; How to use the action button: Click once.
  • What you can do: Reject an incoming call; How to use the action button: Press-and-hold for one second.
  • What you can do: Call your top contact; How to use the action button: Double-click, and Alexa will connect the call for you.
  • What you can do: Access Siri or Google Assistant; How to use the action button: Press and hold for one second. Siri/Google Assistant Chime will indicate when it’s ready for your command.
  • What you can do: Power off; How to use the action button: Click once, then press-and-hold for three seconds. A long vibration will let you know it’s powered off. (Click once to power on.)

Issues with Sound Quality on Echo Link or Echo Link Amp

Loose or unplugged cables can cause issues with sound quality.

  • Check that your cables are plugged into your device and your audio system or speakers. Make sure the cables fit properly and match the port you’re using.

  • Check that your cables work with other audio devices, if available.

  • Check that your speakers or audio system works with other inputs.

  • Make sure that your speakers, audio system, or other input devices are turned on and the volume on all devices are turned up.

  • Check that the correct input on the stereo system is selected.

  • Make sure that your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp is powered on.

  • Check that your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp are online and visible in the Alexa app. If your device isn’t there, or shows as “offline”, try setting up the device again.

  • Check that other devices connected to your Wi-Fi network are working. You can verify that your mic-enabled Echo device is connected by asking, “What time is it?”

  • Make sure that you are using supported inputs and outputs formats (for example, uncompressed PCM) with your stereo system and echo link or echo link amp.

  • If you’re streaming over Bluetooth, try pairing your Bluetooth device again.

  • Set Up Your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp

  • Echo Link Hardware Guide

  • Echo Link Amp Hardware Guide

  • Supported Connections, Inputs, and Outputs for Echo Link and Echo Link Amp

Learn About Using Alexa on Your Fire Tablet

Ask questions, shop, search, play music, and more on your compatible Fire tablet.

Amazon designs Alexa with multiple layers of privacy protection:

  • When you want to talk to Alexa, you have to first wake up your tablet by using the wake word (for example, “Alexa”) or another wake word that you have set up. Only then does the device begin recording and sending your request to Amazon’s secure cloud.
  • You can ask Alexa to speak faster, speak slower, or speak at default rate.
  • All of your interactions with Alexa are encrypted in transit to Amazon’s cloud where they are securely stored.
  • You’ll always know when Alexa is recording and sending your request to Amazon’s secure cloud because a blue light bar appears on your tablet.
  • To view, hear, or delete your recordings, go to the or the Alexa app. To delete by voice, say, “Delete what I just said,” or “Delete everything I said today.”
  • To deactivate Alexa hands-free, use the Alexa Hands-Free Mode on/off switch in your tablet settings.

Note: You must log in with your main profile to use Alexa features on your Fire Tablet. Secondary profiles, such as child profiles, can’t access Alexa features.

To learn more about Alexa, visit the Alexa and Alexa Devices FAQs page.

  • Switch to Show Mode on Your Fire Tablet
  • Use Alexa Hands-Free on Your Fire Tablet

Link Video Streaming Services on Echo Devices with a Screen

To link a video streaming service, go to your device settings or say, “Go to video home,” and choose from the available providers.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

To link a video streaming service from your device settings:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:

    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.

  2. Select Fire TV, then select Applications.

  3. Select whether to find apps on Silk Browser or in the Fire TV Appstore, or to manage apps you already have.

  4. When you find the apps you want, follow the on-screen instructions to install the app and log in with the account information for that provider.

    Note: Some services might require you to install the provider’s app or sign into a subscription before you can watch their video content.

  • Set Up Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen
  • Pair an Alexa Voice Remote with Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen
  • Watch Video Streaming Services on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Make Video Calls On Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Calls to Echo Show devices can use the camera, and add visual effects and reactions.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Go to Communicate in your device settings:

    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu on your screen, then select Communicate.
    • If you are using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Communicate.

  2. Select Call.

  3. Select which contact on your account you want to call.

  4. Select the device that you want to reach them with – select an Echo Show device for a video call.

    To turn off the camera at any time, select Video Off , or press the device Mute button. Press the device Mute button again to turn the camera back on.

Note: Animated Effects and Reactions in calls require Alexa Communication Enhanced Features. You can turn on Enhanced Features when prompted in a call, or with the Alexa app. You only need to turn on Enhanced Features once.

To add animated visual effects during a call, tap the device screen and select Effects , and select the effect you want. If prompted to turn on Enhanced Features, select Enable. The effect activates on all screens on the call. To stop an effect, tap the screen and select Clear, or select another effect.

To send animated reactions during the call, select Smile and select a reaction. The reactions play on all screens on the call.

  • Create Your Calling Group
  • Turn Alexa Communication Enhanced Features On or Off

Manage Ads and Other Suggested Content on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Personalize your ad preferences and select other suggested content to display on your Echo Show.

[Embedded video omitted]

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices receive a software update soon.

The Echo Show displays recommendations for new movies, shows, products, and more. These ads are marked with Sponsored at the bottom of the screen. You can’t turn off these ads, but you can skip an ad by swiping from right to the left on the screen.

Manage Interest-Based Ad Preferences

Interest-based ads are also referred to as personalized or targeted ads. We show interest-based ads to display features, products, and services that might be of interest to you.

To turn Interest-based ads on or off, select the Receive interest-based ads delivered by Amazon on Alexa option in Manage Your Alexa Data, Alexa app, or on your Echo Show.

In the Alexa app:

  1. Select .
  2. Select Alexa Privacy.
  3. Select Manage your Alexa Data.
  4. Manage your preferences.

On your Echo Show:

  1. Say “Open settings,” or swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Alexa Privacy or Privacy and Permissions.
  3. Select Manage Your Alexa Data.
  4. Manage your preferences.

To help personalize your ads, activate Interest-based ads and go to Improve Your Recommendations. Select items to include or exclude from interest-based ads.

Note: You may still see ads provided by Amazon that aren’t based on your interests. For more information, see our Privacy Notice.

Hide a Specific Ad

An ad can be hidden for 30 days by selecting the information in the bottom right and then choosing one of the options. Providing feedback on an ad that’s offensive or inappropriate will hide the ad for 30 days and initiate an investigation.

Customize Other Suggested Content

You can also customize other content on your Echo Show home screen. This content doesn’t have Sponsored at the bottom of the screen. Including content such as Amazon Recommendations, Your Frequent Orders, and Explore Local Places.

To learn more, go to Customize the Home Screen on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

Important: Mount your Echo Auto on a hard, durable surface away from direct airflow of vents so Alexa can hear you clearly. Avoid placing the device where it interferes with the operation of the vehicle or the driver’s vision. Don’t mount the device on soft plastic, leather, or fabric.

  1. Identify the mount placement.
  2. Clean the selected surface with the included cleaning pad.
  3. Peel the plastic off of the adhesive and firmly press the mount onto the surface for 30 seconds.
  4. Attach your Echo Auto to the mount using the magnet on the back of the device.
  5. Place your Echo Auto speaker module and cable where they don’t interfere with the safe operation of the vehicle.
  6. Use the cable wrap to secure the cable.

Tip: If you need to move or remove the mount, clean the area with a household adhesive remover, then follow steps 1-6.

Move Audio Playback to Different Echo Devices with a Screen

Use your Echo device with a screen to select which devices play your music or podcasts.

When you’re playing audio on your Alexa devices, you can use the Echo Show to assign or move streams to particular devices or rooms. You can move a podcast from your Echo Show to the office Echo Dot. Or, move music from the dining room Echo to the living room speaker group.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

To move audio playback between devices:

  1. If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu on your screen, and then select Active Media.
  2. Under Active Media List, find the audio stream you want to move, and select the Device Picker .
  3. Select the box for the device or speaker group where you want playback.
  4. Select Done.

Any playback moves end about an hour after you stop streaming. If you start streaming again after that time, repeat this procedure to move playback how you want it.

Note: You can move only active audio streams between your devices.

  • Play Music with Multiple Alexa Devices
  • Link Music Streaming Services to Alexa

Multipoint Pairing on Echo Buds

Use Multipoint Pairing to connect your Echo Buds to multiple devices and seamlessly switch between 2 devices to continue listening to your audio stream without pausing.

Use Multipoint Pairing to connect your Echo Buds with up to eight devices at the same time. Alexa identifies which device is playing audio and switches to it automatically. This makes it possible for you to listen to your audio stream continuously without having to stop and take out your phone or reconnect to your laptop.

To switch between devices by voice say “Alexa, disconnect from my Fire TV.”

  • Set Up Multipoint Pairing on Echo Buds

Multipoint Pairing on Smart Glasses with

  Alexa (3rd Generation) {#multipoint-pairing-on-smart-glasses-with-alexa-3rd-generatio}

Use Multipoint Pairing to connect your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) to multiple devices and seamlessly switch between two devices to continue listening to your audio stream without pausing.

Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) can be actively connected to two devices at the same time. This allows you to switch between these devices seamlessly. For instance, you can listen to music on your tablet and take a call on your phone without needing to manually switch connections.

In addition to the multi-point pairing, your Smart Glasses can remember up to eight paired devices. This feature means that once you’ve paired a device, your smart glasses will recognize it in the future, making reconnection easier and quicker, without going through the pairing process again.

  • Set Up Multipoint Pairing on Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Music or Media Isn’t Playing with Echo Buds

Music playback doesn’t work on your Echo Buds.

  • Make sure that your Echo Buds are paired to your phone or another device via Bluetooth.

  • Make sure that your Echo Buds are connected to the Alexa app. The app home screen has an Echo Buds card when connected.

  • Check your phone’s volume and increase it as needed.

  • Place your Echo Buds in the case and close the lid for 30 seconds. Take them out and retry.

  • Make sure that your phone is connected to Wi-Fi or cellular data connection.

  • Make sure there’s sufficient battery for both ear buds. To make sure there’s sufficient battery, check the light on the case or check in the Alexa app.

  • Echo Buds automatically start playback when placed in the ear. Check that the ear buds are securely placed in your ear. You can hear a chime when the ear buds are correctly placed.

  • Factory Reset Your Echo Buds

  • Update the Software on Echo Buds

  • Use the Alexa App to Check Battery Status on Echo Buds

Music or Media Not Playing with Echo Auto

To resolve most playback issues, check that your car stereo is set to the correct input.

If your car has:

  • Bluetooth music and calling: Set the input on your car stereo to Bluetooth. Make sure that Echo Auto is connected to your car using your phone’s Bluetooth.
  • Bluetooth calling only: Set the input on your car stereo to Auxiliary. Make sure that Echo Auto is connected to your car stereo using the included AUX cable.
  • No Bluetooth: Set the input on your car stereo to AUX. Make sure that Echo Auto is connected to your car stereo using the included AUX cable.

Tip: Before each drive, make sure that your car stereo input is set to Bluetooth or Auxiliary. Your phone volume should be turned up and your car stereo volume set to a comfortable level.

Mute the Microphone on Echo Buds with the Alexa App

Turn on the microphone or mute it with the Alexa app.

The microphone is on by default. It stays on until you mute it or take out both buds.

Tip: When your Echo Buds are connected to your phone, look for the Echo Buds card on the home page of the Alexa app. Select the microphone icon to mute or unmute the microphone on your device.

Note: For Echo Buds (2019 release, 1st gen), if you don’t see the Echo Buds card on the home page of the Alexa app, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select Echo Buds .
  4. Under Alexa and Microphones, use the slider to select Mute Microphones.

Note: For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) and Echo Buds (2023 release), you can customize touch controls on your device to mute the microphone.

  • Customize Tap Controls on Echo Buds

Notes for You on Echo Show

Leave notes for others in your home from your Echo Show.

Notes for You is available on devices that support visual ID.

Use Notes for You to send notes to anyone in your home. This feature requires both visual ID and voice ID. To send a note say, “Send a note to [name].” You can tell Alexa who you’d like to send a note to and what the note should say. The next time the recipient is recognized on your Echo Show device, they’ll see a home card on their device. Select the home card to open the note.

Note: Anyone with access to your account voice history can review Notes that have been shared.

To leave a note for someone:

  • The recipient must have a profile on your Amazon account.
  • The recipient must have set up both voice ID and visual ID on at least one device.

You’ll see new notes on your Echo Show home screen after Alexa recognizes your visual ID. Say, “Show my note,” or select the note to view it.

  • What is Visual ID on Echo Show?
  • Enroll in Visual ID on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Notes on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Leave at-a-glance notes or video messages for everyone in the home to see.

Notes let you share information with everyone in your home.

To leave a note with your voice, say something like:

  • “Create a note.”
  • “Add a note.”
  • “Make a video note.”
  • “Create a video note.”
  • “Leave a note for Carlos to take out the trash.”

To create and leave messages with touch, select the notes card on Alexa Home, or use the notes widget.

Notes pin to the device used to create them. To access notes on that device, say “Show my notes,” to show all notes from all of your devices. You can also say:

  • “Open the third note.”
  • “Unpin the second note.”
  • “Delete all notes.”

Tip: Video Notes play automatically in a loop when opened. Select the Expand button to open it full-screen.

To access notes by touch, select Notes , at the top-right corner of your screen. The Notes widget on your Alexa Home also shows up to three of the newest Notes. Select the widget to see all Notes and create

If your device doesn’t support widgets, find your recent notes in a card on Alexa Home.

To see notes in the Alexa app on your mobile device, go to the Notes tab in the Lists and Notes section.

Note: Anyone with access to your device can see and delete notes left on the device. Parents can review, edit, or delete content from kids’ accounts.

Video Notes are available on all Echo devices with a screen, except Echo Show (1st and 2nd Generation) or Echo Spot devices.

Pair a Phone or Bluetooth Speaker to Your Echo Device with a Screen

Pair Bluetooth devices with your Echo through on-screen settings. These steps also work for the Echo Spot.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Set your Bluetooth device to pairing mode.

  2. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:

    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.

  3. Select Device Options, then select Bluetooth.

    Select Scan if you don’t see the device you’re looking for.

  4. Find your Bluetooth device and select Connect.

Once the initial pairing is complete, certain Bluetooth devices might automatically reconnect to your Echo device when in range. If a device doesn’t automatically connect, turn on Bluetooth on the device and say, “Pair Bluetooth.”

Pair an Alexa Voice Remote with Your Echo Show 15 or Echo Show 21

You can control the Fire TV experience on your Echo Show 15 or Echo Show 21 with an Alexa Voice Remote.

[Embedded video omitted]

These remotes are compatible with Echo devices with a screen:

  • Alexa Voice Remote (3rd Generation)
  • Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)
  • Alexa Voice Remote Pro

To pair your first remote, say “Go to Settings,” and then select Get Started With Fire TV Remote. Follow on-screen instructions to pair.

If you already have a remote paired with your device, use the following instructions to pair another one:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the MenuIcon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Fire TV.
  3. Select Fire TV Remotes.
  4. On the Alexa Voice Remote, press and hold the Home Button for 10 seconds. The Echo Show tells you when it discovers the remote. Note: There are no LED indicators on the Alexa Voice Remote.
  5. Complete pairing by selecting Connect on your device’s screen.

We recommend a remote as the best way to use Fire TV on the Echo device with a screen. The remote controls only Fire TV actions and features on the device, and can’t control Alexa widgets or other skills or services.

Pair Echo Buds with a New Device

Use Bluetooth to connect Echo Buds to a laptop or tablet.

For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) and Echo Buds (2023 release), you must register your Echo Buds in the Alexa app first in order to pair them successfully to a device.

Note: You must register your Echo Buds in the Alexa app first in order to use it with any Bluetooth device. Alexa only works when paired to the Alexa app on an iOS or Android device.

  1. With your Echo Buds in the case, open the case. Press the button on the case for 3 seconds. When you see a pulsing blue light on the case, your Echo Buds are ready to be paired with other devices.
  2. Place the Echo Buds in your ears.
  3. On your computer, tablet, or other device, go to Bluetooth settings and pair your Echo Buds.
    1. When pairing Echo Buds with a laptop, Windows may show multiple devices when in pairing mode. Select the option with the headphones icon.

Tip: If your new device won’t pair to your Echo Buds, make sure that you have enabled Bluetooth on your phone, computer, tablet, or other device. Then try again.

Pair Your Phone or Bluetooth Speaker to Your Echo Device

Use the Alexa app to pair your phone or Bluetooth speaker with your Echo Device.

  1. Put your Bluetooth device in pairing mode.
  2. Open the Alexa app .
  3. Select Devices .
  4. Select your device.
  5. Select Device Settings .
  6. Select Bluetooth Devices, and then Pair A New Device.

Next time you want to connect, turn on Bluetooth on your phone or Bluetooth speaker and say, “Pair Bluetooth.” Once the initial pairing is complete, certain Bluetooth devices may automatically reconnect to your Echo when in range.

Personalize Your Echo Hub Idle Screen

Set the clock and background that you want to see when your Echo Hub isn’t busy.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Display & Appearance.
  3. Select Select Clock and Photo Display, then browse and choose the clock face and background that you want.
  4. Select Photo Display, then browse and choose the clock face and background that you want.
  5. To have Echo Hub display a dark screen when not active, turn off Idle Screen.

Personalize Your Echo Spot (2024 Release) Display

Use device settings to choose clock face, colors, or turn on night mode.

To change your display, say, “Go to Settings,” or go to your device settings:

  • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
  • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.

To change the clock face:

  1. Select Clock & Theme, then select Clock Face.
  2. Select the option that you like, and select Done to apply it.

To choose a different color:

  1. Select Clock & Theme, then select Color Theme.
  2. Select the option that you like, and select Done to apply it.

Note: The color theme applies to the clock face and many Alexa features, such as timers, alarms, and reminders.

To show a 24-hour clock:

  1. Select Clock & Theme, select Clock Format, then select 24-Hour Clock.
  2. Turn on 24-Hour Clock. Turn it off to show 12-hour time.

To turn on Night Mode:

  1. Select Display, then select Night Mode.
  2. Turn on Enable to activate Night Mode. Turn it off to keep your display at the same brightness all the time

Note: Night Mode turns the Echo Spot display red at night, for easier visibility in the dark. The Echo Spot comes with Night Mode turned on by default. Turn it off to keep the same display brightness and color all the time.

Tip: You can also make each of these display changes in the Alexa app. Select Devices , select your Echo Spot, and then select Settings .

Personalized Music on Echo Frames (3rd Generation) and Smart Glasses

Play recommended music from your Alexa profile’s default music service.

Double-press the back button to play recommended music playlists and stations from your default music service (Amazon Music, Pandora, Apple Music, or Spotify).

To customize playlists (Amazon Music and Pandora only):

  1. Open the Alexa App .
  2. Go to Device Settings.
  3. Turn on Personalized Music.
  4. Select Manage Personalized Music.
  5. Select Custom.
  6. Select a playlist to replace.

Note: To add a playlist to Personalized Music when using Amazon Music, open the Alexa app and ask Alexa to play the desired playlist by voice command (for example “Alexa, play [playlist name]”). This makes the playlist available in your Personalized Music library.

To change your music service provider:

  1. Open the Alexa App .
  2. Go to Device Settings .
  3. Turn on Personalized Music.
  4. Select Manage Personalized Music.
  5. Use the Music Settings link to change the provider.

Note: If you haven’t set a preferred music service from the ones listed earlier, recommendations from Amazon Music play for both curated playlists and customization options.

Play Audio on Echo Spot (2024 Release)

Start playback by voice, then you can use the on-screen controls.

Your Echo Spot can play any music, podcast, or audio sources that you’ve linked with Alexa.

Start and select your audio content by voice. You can say,

  • “Play [song / album / artist / playlist].”
  • “Play [station name].”
  • “Play [news source].”
  • “Play the latest episode of [podcast name].”

Controls on the Echo Spot screen let you pause, stop, or resume playback. You can also use voice commands to control playback.

Note: Echo Spot (2024 Release) doesn’t support video playback or streaming.

Play Music with Your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp Using Your Voice

Add the name of your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp to the end of phrases that you use to play music.

  • “Play [artist name] on [device name].”
  • “Play [song title] on [device name].”
  • “Set volume to 7 on [device name].
  • “Stop on [device name].

Note: When your device is the preferred speaker in a smart home group, you don’t have to add the device name to your commands. Your Group also needs a compatible Echo (like Echo Dot) to give your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp commands.

Put Echo Frames (2nd Generation) Into Pairing Mode

After pairing Echo Frames (2nd Generation) for the first time, use the action button to put your device back into Bluetooth pairing mode. Echo Frames (2nd Generation) can be paired with up to eight devices.

To pair your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) with a new device:

  1. Ensure that your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) are turned off. To turn off your Echo Frames (2nd Generation), press and hold the action button until the status light flashes red.

    Note: The action button is the shorter button on the right arm of the frames.

  2. Put your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) into pairing mode. Press and hold the action button until the status light turns blue, then flashes red and blue. Then release the button.

Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) will exit pairing mode when you connect to a device via Bluetooth. To exit pairing mode, go to your device’s Bluetooth settings and reconnect your Echo Frames (2nd Generation).

Tip: To swap between paired Bluetooth devices, select Echo Frames (2nd Generation) in the device’s Bluetooth settings. Alexa functionality is only available when connected to the Alexa app.

Rearrange Widgets on Your Echo Show

Widgets can be rearranged on your compatible Echo Show’s Widget Panel.

To rearrange your widgets, follow these steps:

  1. Long press the widget that you want to rearrange.
  2. Select Rearrange Widgets .

You can also rearrange your widgets from the Widget Panel.

  • In portrait orientation, swipe up and select Rearrange Widgets.
  • In landscape orientation, swipe left and select Rearrange Widgets.

For a list of compatible devices, go to What Are Alexa Widgets?

  • Add Widgets on Your Echo Device with a Screen

Remove Paired Bluetooth Devices from Your Echo Device

Use the Alexa App to remove previously paired Bluetooth devices.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select your device.
  4. Select Settings .
  5. Select Bluetooth Devices.
  6. Select the device you want to remove, and then select Forget Device. Repeat this step for each device you want to remove.
  • Remove Paired Bluetooth Devices from Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Remove Paired Bluetooth Devices from Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Use your Echo Show’s Bluetooth settings to remove previously paired devices. These steps also work for Echo Spot.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Device Options.
  3. Select Bluetooth.
  4. Select Info next to the device you want to remove, and then select Forget Device. Repeat this step for all devices you want to remove.

Reset Your Echo (1st Generation)

If your Echo (1st Generation) isn’t responding, and you’ve tried to restart it, reset your device.

If your device is unresponsive, first restart your device. Unplug the power adapter from the device or the outlet and wait for 10 seconds. Plug it back in to restart it.

[Embedded video omitted]

To reset your device and keep your smart home connections:

  1. Use a paper clip (or similar tool) to press the Reset button briefly.
  2. Wait for the light ring to turn off and on again.
  3. Your device enters setup mode. For setup instructions, go to Set Up Your Echo.

To reset your device to its factory settings:

  1. Use a paper clip (or similar tool) to press and hold the Reset button for 8 seconds.
  2. Wait for the light ring to turn off and on again.
  3. Your device enters setup mode. For setup instructions, go to Set Up Your Echo.

Note: This reset erases all your personal information and any device and smart home connections.

Tip: If resetting your device isn’t helpful or you no longer want to use your device, Deregister Your Device from your Amazon account. Deregistering your device erases all device settings.

For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

Reset Your Echo (2nd Generation)

If your Echo (2nd Generation) isn’t responding, and you’ve tried to restart it, reset your device.

If your device is unresponsive, first restart your device. Unplug the power adapter from the device or the outlet and wait for 10 seconds. Plug it back in to restart it.

[Embedded video omitted]

To reset your device and keep your smart home connections:

  1. Press and hold the Action button for 20 seconds.
  2. Wait for the light ring to turn off and on again.
  3. Your device enters setup mode. For setup instructions, go to Set Up Your Echo.

To reset your device to its factory settings:

  1. Press and hold the Microphone off and Volume down buttons for 8 seconds.
  2. Wait for the light ring to turn off and on again.
  3. Your device enters setup mode. For setup instructions, go to Set Up Your Echo.

Note: This reset erases all your personal information and any device and smart home connections.

Tip: If resetting your device isn’t helpful or you no longer want to use your device, Deregister Your Device from your Amazon account. Deregistering your device erases all device settings.

For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

Reset Your Echo Devices with a Screen

If your Echo device is unresponsive, or you want to erase your device settings, factory reset your device. These steps also work with Echo Spot.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

Before a full device reset, try restarting your device first to resolve most common issues. Unplug the power adapter from the device or the outlet, wait 15 seconds and then plug it back in. If the restart doesn’t solve your issue, try the following reset procedure.

You can reset your device to factory defaults using either the device’s buttons or the on-screen menu.

[Embedded video omitted]

Reset with device buttons:

  1. Press and hold the Microphones & Camera Disable/Enable and Volume Down buttons until you see the Amazon logo (about 15 seconds).
  2. When prompted, follow the on-screen instructions to set up your device.

Reset with the on-screen menu:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    1. If you’re using Alexa+, select Menu on your screen, and then select Settings.
    2. If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Device Options.
  3. Select About this Device.
  4. Select Reset to Factory Defaults.
    • If you’re using an Echo Show (2nd Generation) or Echo Show 10 and want to reset without losing your smart home device connects, select Reset to Factory Defaults but retain Smart Home Device Connections. Otherwise, select Reset.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to set up your device.

Tip: If resetting your device doesn’t help, or you no longer want to use your device, Deregister Your Device from your Amazon account. Deregistering your device erases all device settings.

  • Set Up Your Echo Devices with a Screen

For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

To set an alarm in the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  5. Select Save.

Set Kid-friendly Features on Your Echo Show 5 Kids

Use Amazon Kids and the Alexa app to add skills, games, educational content and more.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

When you turn on Amazon Kids on your Echo Show 5 Kids, you can add lots of fun, educational, and useful settings and features. Here are a few we recommend.

On the Echo Show 5 Kids device:

  • Swipe down from the top of the device screen, and select Amazon Kids . Choose from lots of Stories, Skills, Videos, and Music sources just for kids.
  • Give Alexa fun character voices, character images, and personalities, such as an owl, panda, dragon or tiger. Just say, “Pretend to be a dragon,” “Use your tiger voice,” or “Act like an owl.”

On the Alexa app:

  • Open , then select Routines . Routines can set reminders about play dates, turn on Do Not Disturb during nap times, or play “clean-up” music for 20 minutes.
  • Open , then select Skills & Games. Search in the Kids category for activities to enjoy on any of your Alexa devices.
  • Open Devices , select your Echo Show 5 Kids device and select Settings . Then select Alexa’s Voice and choose kid-friendly voices and personalities for Alexa.
  • At any time, open Communicate to make an announcement or start a Drop In call to the Echo Show 5 Kids device.

On the Parent Dashboard:

Go to Parent Dashboard and sign in with your Amazon account.

  • Select Settings to set content filters and parental controls that you want for the Kids profile.

  • Open Content to explore the full store of apps, games, videos, books and more.

  • Set up an Amazon Kids+ account on the Parent Dashboard. Your new Echo Show 5 Kids device comes with a year of Amazon Kids+.

  • Turn on Amazon Kids on Echo Devices with a Screen

  • What Is Amazon Kids+?

  • Set Up Drop In on Echo Show 5 Kids

Set Timers on Echo Dot with clock

Say “Set a timer for 20 minutes.” The display shows the timer countdown.

The device displays a dot on the upper right when a timer exceeds 1 hour. The countdown display starts when the timer hits 59 minutes.

Note: If you set multiple timers, the display shows the timer with the least time left.

Set Up a Pre-owned Echo Devices with a Screen

If your device once belonged to someone else, start setup with a factory reset.

Your pre-owned device might still carry some of the previous owner’s settings or preferences. A factory reset erases those old settings.

To start, connect the device to its power adapter. Once the screen begins to light up, factory reset the device:

  1. Press and hold the Mute and Volume Down buttons until you see the Amazon logo (about 15 seconds).

  2. After a few seconds, device setup begins. When prompted, follow the on-screen instructions to:

    • Select a language.
    • Connect to your Wi-Fi network.
    • Log in to your Amazon account and register the device to your account.
    • Confirm your time zone.
    • Confirm your address.
    • Confirm the location of your device.
    • Choose a name for your device.
    • Choose a wallpaper for your device.

When you see the rotating content screens of device Home, your device is ready to use. We recommend ensuring your device has all the software updates it might need. See how to Update the Software Version on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

  • Echo Device Is Having Wi-Fi Issues
  • Connect Smart Home Devices to Alexa
  • Link Other Music Streaming Services to Alexa

Set Up Audio Personalization for Echo Buds

Echo Buds can perform an audio assessment to help tune audio for your unique hearing preferences.

Tip: Before setup, ensure that your Alexa app and Echo Buds software are updated to the latest version. Echo Buds firmware must be version 603594926 or greater. Update the Software on Echo Buds

Audio Personalization is only available on Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd Gen, or later) devices.

  1. Open the Alexa app.
  2. Select Devices, then All Devices.
  3. Choose the Echo Buds that you want to personalize and select the Settings () icon.
  4. Select Audio Personalization, then follow the on-screen instructions.
  5. To turn off this feature, follow steps 1 through 3, go to Audio Personalization, and turn Audio Personalization off.

Note: This feature is not intended to diagnose or treat any hearing conditions.

Set Up Doesn’t Work on Your Echo Device

Some things you can try when your Echo device has difficulty setting up.

Most problems with device setup arise from a few common issues. If they come up, try the following.

  • Check that your device has a strong internet connection.

  • If your device setup uses the Alexa app, check that you have the latest version of the app.

  • Restart your Echo device. Unplug it from power, wait 30 seconds, then plug it back in.

  • If none of these steps help, or if you have problems registering the device, reset your Echo device to clear up most issues.

  • Echo Device Is Having Wi-Fi Issues

  • Download the Alexa App

  • Restart Your Alexa Enabled Device

  • Reset Your Echo Device

Set Up Drop In on Echo Show 5 Kids

You can use your nearest Echo device to talk through the Echo Show 5 Kids.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

Use the Alexa app to turn on Drop In, and allow communication through your Echo Show 5 Kids device.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open Devices .
  3. Select Echo & Alexa, then select your Echo Show 5 Kids device.
  4. Select Settings and then select Communications.
  5. Turn on Communications. Then select Drop In, and select which devices can Drop In on your Echo Show 5 Kids.

To Drop In with any other Echo device in your account:

  • If you’re using Alexa+, say, “Drop In on [device name].” Or, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Communicate . Select Drop In, and then select your Echo Show 5 Kids device.

  • If you’re using the original Alexa, say “Drop In on [device name].” Or, swipe down from the top edge of the screen and select Communicate . Select Drop In, and then select your Echo Show 5 Kids device.

  • Set Up Echo Show 5 Kids for Live View

Set Up Echo Show 5 Kids for Live View

Use an Echo Show device or the Alexa app to see the live view from your Echo Show 5 Kids device camera.

Use the Alexa app to turn on Drop In, and allow communication through your Echo Show 5 Kids device.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Privacy & Permissions.
  3. Select Home Monitoring, then turn on Home Monitoring.

To see a live view in the Alexa app, open Devices , select Cameras, and then select your Echo Show 5 Kids device.

Tip: When using live view on another Echo Show device, double tap the screen to zoom in, or use a pinching motion to zoom out. Use your device volume controls to adjust the live view audio.

Set Up Lock Screen Security with Alexa

Turn on the lock-screen security setting to block personal responses from Alexa while your smartphone is locked.

Important: This setting isn’t available with Alexa+.

Lock-screen security is available on:

  • Echo Buds
  • Smart Glasses with Alexa
  • Echo Frames (Any Generation)
  • Echo Loop

Turning this setting on and off applies to all compatible devices in your account.

To block personal responses while your phone is locked:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select your device.
  4. Select Block Personal Responses, and turn the setting on or off.

When active, Alexa blocks responses on personal topics, such as your Amazon account, contacts, shopping, location, and smart home devices.

Smart Glasses with Alexa (including Echo Frames): Once you unlock your smartphone, you can receive all Alexa responses for a 2-hour period.

Note: If you have Voice ID enabled and Alexa recognizes your voice, you can receive Alexa responses related to your smart home devices.

Echo Loop: Once you unlock your smartphone, you can receive all Alexa responses for a 2-hour period.

Echo Buds: Once you unlock your smartphone, Alexa no longer blocks responses as long as you use at least one Echo Bud.

Set Up Multipoint Pairing on Echo Buds

Use the Alexa app to pair your Echo Buds to multiple devices at the same time.

  1. Open the case lid. Press the button on the case for 3 seconds to enter pairing mode. Confirm that the blue light is flashing.
  2. Your Echo Buds will appear as an available device to connect to.
  3. Select your Echo Buds to compete pairing.

Note: You must register your Echo Buds in the Alexa app first in order to pair with multiple devices.

  • Multipoint Pairing and Seamless Switching on Echo Buds

Set Up Multipoint Pairing on Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Use the Alexa app to pair your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) to multiple devices at the same time.

  1. Turn on your Smart Glasses by opening the temples.
  2. Press and hold the front and back action buttons on the right temple for three seconds.
  3. Release the buttons when the status light blinks orange. This shows that your smart glasses are discoverable and ready to pair.
  4. Select your Smart Glasses to compete pairing.
  5. On the device you want to pair with, go to the Bluetooth settings and select Echo Frames to complete pairing.

Note: Register your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) in the Alexa app first to pair with multiple devices.

Tip: You can keep using Alexa as long as one of your connected devices is connected to the Alexa app.

  • Multipoint Pairing on Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen)

Set Up Photo Display on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

To set up your photo display, use your Echo device’s on-screen settings.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

You can use these steps on:

  • Echo Show (1st Generation)
  • Echo Show (2nd Generation)

Set Up VIP Filter Reply and Alexa Hands Free Messaging (SMS) on iOS (2nd Generation)

To ensure that VIP Filter Reply or Alexa Hands Free Messaging (SMS) works on your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation), follow these steps in your iOS settings.

  1. Pair your smart glasses to your iOS phone and the Alexa app.
  2. Go to Bluetooth Settings on your iOS phone.
  3. Find your smart glasses in Bluetooth Settings.
  4. Select the icon next to your device.
  5. Ensure that Show Notifications is on.
  6. Restart your smart glasses.

Note: To use these features, make sure you’re on the latest version of iOS. Also, ensure that you have the latest software version for your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) and the Alexa app.

Set Up Your Echo Buds

To play media and access Alexa, set up your Echo Buds with the Alexa app.

[Embedded video omitted]

For Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) and Echo Buds (2023 release), you must register your Echo Buds in the Alexa app first in order to set up your device successfully.

Note: When setting up a replacement pair of Echo Buds (2023 Release), the replacement earbud needs to be set up as a pair and cannot mix with a previous earbud. For more information, refer to your Quick Start Guide that comes with your replacement buds.

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  6. Select the pop-up notification.

    1. If you don’t receive the notification, open the Alexa app.

    2. Select Devices .

    3. Select .

    4. Select Add Device.

    5. Select Amazon Echo , and then select Echo Buds .

      Note: You might have to approve the pairing request on your phone.

  7. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Note: It may take up to 2 minutes for your Echo Buds to appear in the available devices list.

Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts, accessories, and information ready:

  • Your Echo Pop Kids and the included 15W Power Adapter.
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password.
    • Don’t have an account? To make one, go to Create an Amazon Account.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi network name and password.
  • The Alexa app installed on a compatible iOS or Android mobile device.

Meet Your Echo Pop Kids

The Echo Pop Kids is a compact, screenless smart speaker designed for children. It features built-in Alexa voice controls, a light ring for status indication, a physical microphone button for privacy, and is pre-configured with Amazon Kids+ for a safe, family-friendly experience.

Echo Pop Kids

Compact Smart Speaker with Alexa for Kids

In the box

  • Echo Pop Kids
  • 15W Power Adapter
  • Quick Start Guide

Note: Your Echo Pop Kids has a light ring that shows device status through different colors. For more information, go to What Do the Lights on Your Echo Device Mean.

How to Set Up Your Device

Tip: Before setup, download the Alexa app from your mobile device’s app store.

To set up your device:

  1. Plug in your Echo Pop Kids device with the included power adapter.
  2. On your mobile device, open the Alexa app .
  3. Select Devices .
  4. Select Plus .
  5. Select Add Device.
  6. Select Amazon Echo.
  7. Select Echo, Echo Dot, Echo Pop and more.
  8. Follow the instructions to set up your device.

Privacy and Support

To enable or disable your device’s microphone, press the Microphones enable/disable button. A red light on the button means that the microphone is disabled. To turn your device’s microphones on or off, press the button.

A blue light on the device means that Alexa is listening and processing your request in Amazon’s secure cloud.

You can review or delete your voice recording history at any time. To learn how, visit Review Your Alexa Voice History.

Alexa Privacy Hub

Parental Controls

Your Echo Pop Kids comes with 6 months of Amazon Kids+ (auto-renews at the applicable rate after the trial period).

Amazon Kids+ on Alexa lets you create a personalised experience for your children and choose what content they can access. To set daily time limits, monitor activity, share content, and manage your child’s experience, use the Parent Dashboard.

Tip: Amazon Kids+ provides access to age-appropriate content, books, music, and skills. You can manage content filters and screen time directly from the Parent Dashboard at parents.amazon.com.

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try these suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to Forgot Your Password.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, you can find more troubleshooting in Echo Device Can’t Connect to Wi-Fi During Setup.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.

For help and troubleshooting, visit Support for Echo Pop Kids online or go to the Help & Feedback section in the Alexa app.

Accessibility Features on Echo Devices

Echo devices have a set of features designed to enhance the user experience for customers with disabilities. This includes features like Tap to Alexa, captioning, the screen magnifier, and VoiceView. For more information, go to Accessibility for Alexa.

For richer sound quality, pair your Echo Sub to a supported Echo device, Stereo Pair, or with an Alexa Home Theater.

[Embedded video omitted]

Before setting up Echo Sub, make sure that you have a supported Echo device is already set up on your Amazon account. Verify it’s online in the Alexa app.

  1. Place your Echo Sub on the floor in the same room as your Echo speakers or home theater.
  2. Open the Alexa app .
  3. Select Devices .
  4. Select [Image: the plus icon].
  5. Select Add Device.
  6. Select Amazon Echo, and then Echo Sub.
  7. Plug in your device.
  8. Follow the on-screen instructions in the Alexa app to complete setup.
    1. If you’re trying to add your Echo Sub to an existing speaker set, delete the speaker set first.
    2. If you’re trying to set up an Alexa Home Theater, do not pair the Echo sub to a speaker during initial setup. Navigate to your Fire TV and follow the Alexa Home Theater setup instructions to add the Echo Sub. For more information, go to Set Up Alexa Home Theater on Your Fire TV.

Set Up Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Use the Alexa app to set up your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation).

Note: Before setup, download the latest version of the Alexa app from your mobile device’s app store. Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen) only support Android 9.0 or greater and iOS 14.0 or greater.

[Embedded video omitted]

  1. Plug charging stand into a safety certified 5W USB power adapter (not included).
  2. Place your smart glasses into the charging stand with the lenses facing up.
  3. Wait 6 seconds for the pulsing light to turn orange. If it blinks red, re-insert smart glasses.
  4. Take your smart glasses out of the charging stand and put them on.
  5. Open the Alexa app .
  6. Select Devices and select .
  7. Select Add Device.
  8. Select Glasses .
  9. Follow the instructions in the Alexa app to set up your device.
  • How to Charge Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

Show Me Camera Feeds and Snapshots on Echo Hub

Select a camera’s tile for a full-screen look at its feed.

To see a camera feed, open the Cameras widget or Cameras Home shortcut, then select a device’s tile. If the camera has a microphone, the view also includes sound.

Select a tile of an Echo Show device - which appear in the Echo Hub dashboard as cameras - to see Live Feeds from those devices.

If you have more than one camera connected to Alexa, select Multiview to add another camera’s feed on the screen.

Note: Some tiles on the Camera widget access snapshots of the camera feed on the Camera widget. Snapshots are available only with Ring cameras under a Ring subscription. To set a Ring camera to access snapshots on the widget, use the Ring app to turn on “Motion Detection.” To access the most recent snapshots from the device, turn on “Snapshot Capture.”

  • Display a Live Feed with Your Echo Devices with a Screen
  • Display a Live Feed with Your Alexa App

Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) Fit Adjustments

To improve fit, you can manually adjust your temple tips with slight adjustments along with adding nose pad adhesives.

If you need additional adjustments for a proper fit, visit a local optician. They can adjust your frames as needed. You can share the Optician Card with your provider to ensure that they have the necessary information about your smart glasses.

[Embedded video omitted]

Your temple tips are the part of the frames that hug behind your ear. If your frames feel heavy on your nose or face, try adjusting the temple tips downward. If the frames feel loose or slide on your nose, try adjusting the temple tips inward.

As you adjust your temple tips, check the fit of your frames with the charging stand. As a guide, the frames should be touching the charger at the nose and back wall. Overbending the temple tips can prevent the ability to place your frames in the charger. You may need to unbend the temple tips for charging.

To bend the temple tips:

  1. Hold firmly on the metal ring area with one hand.
  2. With the other hand, place your thumb below the curved portion of the temple tip.
  3. Make slight adjustments by putting light pressure on the wire and pushing gently upward or downward.

Tip: Adding nosepad adhesives to the inner nosebridge of the smart glasses can also help prevent the frames from slipping.

Smart Home Dashboard on Echo Show

Smart Home dashboard displays compatible smart home devices in your home.

Use the Smart Home dashboard to see and control compatible smart home devices in your home from your Echo Show. Your dashboard shows:

  • Lights
  • Plugs
  • Switches
  • Cameras
  • Thermostats

Your smart home devices must be connected to your Amazon account to display on the Smart Home dashboard.

To add a device, say, “Discover devices.” You can also add devices from the Alexa app.

You can add compatible smart home devices to your Favorites. Use the Alexa app to add favorite devices.

You can also add the Smart Home Favorites widget to your Widget Panel to see and control your favorite compatible smart home devices. To add the Smart Home Favorites widget to your home screen, go to the Widget Gallery. You can also say “Add the Smart Home Favorites widget to Home.”

  • Connect Smart Home Devices to Alexa
  • Create Smart Home Groups for Alexa

Smart Home Devices Aren’t Working with Echo Hub

Try these troubleshooting steps if devices don’t connect to Echo Hub, or are unresponsive.

  • Scenario: Echo Hub doesn’t connect with all of your smart home devices.; Troubleshooting Steps: - Ensure all of your devices are connected to Alexa. Check with the Alexa app, and with the manufacturer’s app. - Check that all of your devices connect to Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or a Smart Home hub. - Check that your smart home devices are on. If a device is battery-operated, try inserting fresh batteries. - Make sure your Echo Hub and the Alexa app have the latest software version. - If your smart home device uses an Alexa skill: - Try controlling your device with the manufacturer’s app. It might help to reconnect the device to Alexa. Then, in the Alexa app, remove the skill and then add it again. - Otherwise, check the device’s internet connection in the manufacturer’s app. If neither of these steps work, try resetting your smart home device.
  • Scenario: Your smart home device is unresponsive, or shows the incorrect state.; Troubleshooting Steps: - To refresh the status of your smart home device, select the device’s tile on your Echo Hub. If a device shows no state or is unresponsive, it’s not communicating its state to the Echo Hub. Most devices refresh their state information every minute or so, while some devices refresh after several minutes. - On the Echo Hub, select the device’s tile to force an information refresh. - Check the device state on the device or manufacturer app, and make sure it connects to the Alexa app. - If the device still shows as unresponsive, consult manufacturer instructions.
  • Scenario: Echo Hub doesn’t have tiles for some smart home devices.; Troubleshooting Steps: Some smart home devices and scenes don’t yet have tiles on Echo Hub. However, you can still use the device by voice, or as part of a routine, or to receive announcements from them. These device types don’t yet have device tiles: - Temperature sensors - Motion sensors - Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors - Water leak detectors - Music systems, including speakers - Garage door openers and gates - Ring Intercom Locks - Printers - Trackers - Network hardware - Remotes

Note: Some Alexa-compatible devices don’t provide functions that the Echo Hub is designed to manage. Such devices include mobile phones, tablets, laptops, clocks, or smart watches.

Snooze Alarms on Echo Devices

Use tap gestures on the device to snooze your alarms.

To snooze an active alarm, firmly tap the device with more than one finger. The default snooze time is 9 minutes.

Note: The tap to snooze gesture doesn’t work if the device is muted.

  • Control Echo Devices with Tap Gestures

Soft Reset Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

If your experiencing any issues with your smart glasses, soft reset your device.

Tip: Having trouble using your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Gen)? Restart your device first to see if it resolves the problem. Close your glasses to turn them off, wait two minutes, then turn them back on by opening them again.

To reset your device:

  1. Put both temples in the open position.
  2. Press and hold both the front action (on the right temple) and volume up buttons (on the left temple) for 45 seconds.
  3. Keep holding until you hear a sound and witness three blue LEDs blinks.
  4. After the blue LED stops flashing, close both temples for one minute.
  5. Open the temples and check if the issue resolves by turning on your device again.

Software Updates on Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa

  (3rd Generation) {#software-updates-on-your-echo-frames-2nd-generation-and-smar}

Your smartphone automatically downloads software updates for Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) when connected to the Internet.

When an update is available, it installs the next time your smartphone connects to your smart glasses over Bluetooth, after they’ve turned off and on.

If you’re still experiencing issues with updating your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation), please follow these steps:

  1. Make sure that your smart glasses are powered on (with temple arms open) and connected to your phone. Keep the Alexa app open.
  2. Ensure that your smart glasses have at least 50% battery life.
  3. For the fastest download, avoid using your smart glasses for about 20 minutes:
    • Only keep your smart glasses connected to your phone, and disconnect from any other devices.
    • Refrain from playing audio or interacting with your smart glasses.
  4. Check Device Settings to see a confirmation that the software update is complete.
  5. Restart your smart glasses by closing the temple arms to turn them off, wait two minutes, then open the arms to turn them back on.
  6. Charge your smart glasses for approximately 15 minutes.

Tip: Make sure that you have the latest version of the Alexa app from your mobile device’s app store.

  • Check Your Echo Device’s Software Version
  • Alexa Device Software Versions

Sound Isn’t Clear on Echo Buds

The audio on your Echo Buds is choppy or you hear a squeal, buzzing, or static.

  • Make sure that you have a strong Wi-Fi or data connection.
  • Make sure that your phone is within Bluetooth range (about 30 feet).
  • If sound is muffled, check to make sure there’s no earwax buildup. Wipe your Echo Buds with a clean, dry cloth.
  • On your Echo Buds (2019 release, 1st gen) and Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen):
    • Try turning down the Passthrough volume, or turning off Passthrough.
    • If you hear a feedback noise, try turning off Passthrough.
    • If you hear background noise or a hissing sound while on a call, turn off Sidetone. In the Alexa app, go to Device Settings and select Sidetone.
    • If static is interrupting your sound, check your Echo Buds for a secure fit using the fit test in the Alexa app.

Supported Alexa Features by Region for International Version Echo Devices

A limited selection of Alexa features are available on “International Version” Echo devices shipped from Amazon to eligible regions, and on eligible third-party Alexa devices. The features listed aren’t exhaustive, vary by region, are subject to change or withdrawal at any time without notice, and may require separate subscriptions or other fees.

Unsupported Features for all “International Version” Devices

  • Shopping
  • Local traffic and business search
  • Select skills from the Alexa Skills store
  • Location-specific news and information
  • Audible
  • Certain music service providers, such as iHeartRadio, Pandora, and SiriusXM
  • Podcasts

Generally Supported Features

  • TuneIn
  • Spotify
  • Amazon Music Unlimited (where available)
  • Smart Home
  • Timers
  • Calendars
  • Alarms
  • News
  • Info
  • To-do/shopping list
  • Weather

Amazon Music Unlimited

Amazon Music Unlimited is currently available in the following regions: Argentina, Belgium, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Cyprus, Malta, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Iceland, Bulgaria, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Portugal, Slovakia, Sweden, and Gibraltar.

Note: Devices in Switzerland can play purchased music but can’t use Amazon Music Unlimited.

Alexa App Availability

Access to the Alexa app on a smart phone is required to use the advanced smart home routines functionality. The Alexa app isn’t available for download in all regions, but you can confirm availability in your local app store. You can go to alexa.amazon.com to complete the setup of your device, but some additional features are only available through the Alexa app.
