Supported Connections, Inputs, and Outputs for Echo Link and Echo Link Amp

To play music, connect Echo Link or Echo Link Amp to speakers or your stereo system.

You can use your Echo Link or Echo Link Amp to stream music to your directly connected speakers or stereo system.

You can find technical details on the product detail pages for Echo Link and Echo Link Amp.

Analog Input and Output Specifications

  • Analog Line-in (L/R stereo RCA): 1.3Vrms (Consumer) or 1.9Vrms (Professional), adjustable in the Alexa app
  • Analog Line-output L/R stereo RCA, subwoofer RCA): 1.9Vrms

Supported Digital Connection Formats

  • Digital Audio Inputs (optical TOSLINK and coaxial RCA) - Uncompressed PCM audio (Sample rates of 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, and 192kHz)
  • Digital Audio Output (optical TOSLINK and coaxial RCA) - Maximum output of 48kHz Uncompressed PCM stereo

Unsupported Connections

  • TV/video connections
  • Casting to Multi-Room Music from Bluetooth input
  • The Amazon Music Unlimited Single Device Plan
  • Compressed digital audio input, such as Dolby DTS/Dolby 5.1.

Synchronize Your Fire TV Content to Your Echo Devices with a Screen

When you synchronize your Fire TV content, you can access the same Fire TV apps, your Watchlist, and recent content on your Echo Show.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

For list of compatible Echo Show devices, visit Set Up Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen.

To synchronize your Fire TV content, go to Echo Show settings:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Fire TV.
  3. Select Content & Applications.
  4. SelectSync Recent Content.
  • Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote
  • Link Video Streaming Services on Echo Devices with a Screen
  • Watch Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Show with Alexa

Tap Controls on Echo Buds

Use tap controls to reduce noise, increase ambient sound, or pause and resume music.

Echo Buds (2019 release, 1st gen)

  • Touch Control: Double tap.; Result: Switch between Bose Noise Reduction and Passthrough.
  • Touch Control: Press and hold.; Result: Access Google Assistant and Siri.
  • Touch Control: Take out one (or both) buds.; Result: Pause music.
  • Touch Control: Put one (or both) buds in.; Result: Music resumes.

Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen)

  • Touch Control: Single tap.; Result: Play or pause music.
  • Touch Control: Double tap.; Result: - Next song. - Answer/end a call.
  • Touch Control: Triple tap.; Result: Previous song.
  • Touch Control: Long hold.; Result: - Switch between Active Noise Cancellation and Passthrough. - Reject a call.
  • Touch Control: Take out one (or both) buds.; Result: Pause music.
  • Touch Control: Put one (or both) buds in.; Result: Music resumes.

Echo Buds (2023 Release)

  • Touch Control: Single tap.; Result: Play or pause music.
  • Touch Control: Double tap.; Result: - Next song. - Answer/end a call.
  • Touch Control: Triple tap.; Result: Previous song.
  • Touch Control: Long hold.; Result: - Talk to Alexa. Passthrough. - Reject a call.
  • Touch Control: Take out one (or both) buds.; Result: Pause music.
  • Touch Control: Put one (or both) buds in.; Result: Music resumes.

Note: With Echo Buds (2021 release, 2nd gen) and Echo Buds (2023 release), you can customize the long hold touch control in the Alexa app for the following actions:

  • Access Google Assistant and Siri.

  • Volume up/volume down.

  • Mute microphones.

  • Customize Tap Controls on Echo Buds

Text Messaging with Echo Auto

You can use your voice to send and read text messages with Alexa.

  • Echo Auto (1st Gen) Text messaging is supported with Android only.
  • Echo Auto (2nd Gen) Text messaging is supported on iOS and Android.

You can say:

  • “Send a text message to [number / contact name].”
  • “Read my text messages.”

Touchpad Controls on Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation)

Use the touchpad on the right temple of Echo Frames (2nd Generation) to answer calls, control media playback, or access other voice assistants.

[Embedded video omitted]

Table 1. Touch Control Results

  • Touch Control: Swipe either direction.; Result: Accept a call or accept a notification.
  • Touch Control: Tap the touchpad.; Result: Reject a call, decline a notification, or pause media.
  • Touch Control: Double tap the touchpad.; Result: Resume media.
  • Touch Control: Press and long hold.; Result: Access other voice assistants.

Turn Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids On or Off

Use your voice to turn Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids on or off.

While setting up your new Echo Pop Kids, select the Disney Princess or Marvel’s Avengers theme in the Alexa app to turn it on. When setup is complete, use your voice to turn the theme on or off.

To turn on Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids, say “Turn on the [Disney Princess/Marvel’s Avengers] Theme.”

To turn off Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids, say “Turn off the [Disney Princess/Marvel’s Avengers] Theme.”

Note:

Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids require an active Amazon Kids+ subscription and only work if the device has Amazon Kids turned on. Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids are intended for kids ages 3-12 years and are available in English.

Currently, Disney Princess and Marvel’s Avengers are the only available themes.

  • What are Alexa Themes for Echo Pop Kids?
  • Turn Amazon Kids on Alexa On or Off Using the Alexa App

Turn On Adaptive Color on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Adaptive Color blends on-screen colors with the tone and hue of the room environment for more natural images. To turn Adaptive Color on or off, use your Echo Show’s on-screen settings.

You can use these steps on:

  • Echo Show 8 (2nd Generation or newer)
  • Echo Show 10
  • Echo Show 11 (2025 release)
  • Echo Show 15
  • Echo Show 21

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings .
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Display & Appearance, then select Display.
  3. Use the switch to turn Adaptive Color on or off.

Turn on Amazon Kids on Echo Devices with a Screen

Set up any Echo Show with a child profile and turn on fun, kid-friendly features.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. If you don’t have a child profile set for your kid, open Accounts & Profiles, then select Your Profile & Family.
  3. Select Add someone else and create a child profile under your Amazon account.

Open Amazon Kids anytime in Settings to add skills, games, content, and features for kids.

Turn On Auto Volume Control (AVC) for Alexa Smart Glasses

Auto Volume automatically adjusts the volume to your surroundings when Alexa or media plays on Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) and Echo Frames (2nd Generation).

To turn on Auto Volume Control (AVC):

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select Echo Frames.
  4. Turn on Auto Volume.
  5. Select your preferred listening volume profile.

If you adjust the volume manually, AVC maintains that level but dynamically change it if ambient noise changes. During phone calls, AVC adjusts the volume at the start but doesn’t change it further during the call based on noise conditions.

Note: While audio plays, you can use the volume buttons to adjust the listening profile level. Auto Volume then dynamically adjusts the volume based on your surroundings and the new profile level that you set. However, on Echo Frames (3rd Generation), adjusting volume buttons doesn’t change the selected listening profile itself.

Turn On Closed Captions On Your Alexa App

Many setup videos include Closed Captioning services that you can turn on with your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation).

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. While the video is open and playing, press on your smartphone screen.
  3. Select the Closed Caption (CC) button in the top-right corner of the video.
  4. Restart or resume playing the video.

For list of compatible devices Echo Show devices, visit Set Up Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen.

Note: Set parental controls settings for Fire TV separately from the Echo Show device settings. Each work on different functions and services.

Turn Presence Detection Off or On with Your Echo Show 8 (2025 release) or Echo Show 11 (2025 release)

Press the Microphones & Camera Enable/Disable button on your Echo device, or use the Alexa app to turn off Presence Detection.

Echo devices with Presence Detection capabilities use ultrasound and, in some cases, ultrasound combined with Wi-Fi signals to detect that someone is present. Presence Detection on Echo Show devices powers Adaptive Content experience by default.

To turn off Presence Detection without disabling features that rely on Presence Detection, press the Microphones & Camera Enable/Disable button on your Echo device. Press the Microphones & Camera Enable/Disable button on your Echo device again to enable Presence Detection capability.

To turn off Presence Detection without turning off the microphones and the camera from your device:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:

    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.

  2. Select Device Options.

  3. Select Privacy & Permissions.

  4. Toggle Presence Detection to Off.

    To turn it back on, select it again and toggle it to On.

To turn sunrise alarms on or off, use your Echo device’s on-screen settings.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

When enabled, your Echo device’s screen gradually brightens 15 minutes before your alarm sounds. You’re able to set a sunrise alarm between 4 a.m. and 9 a.m. Sunrise alarms are enabled by default on some devices.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Display & Appearance, then select Display.
  3. Select on or off for the Sunrise Effect.

Turn Your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

  On or Off {#turn-your-echo-frames-2nd-generation-and-smart-glasses-with-}

How to power your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and smart glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) on or off.

To turn on Echo Frames (2nd Generation), press the action button once until the status light flashes blue.

To turn off Echo Frames (2nd Generation), press and hold the action button until the status light flashes red. Then release the button.

To turn on Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation), open your glasses.

To turn off Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation), close your glasses. To power off while wearing your smart glasses, press both action, and back button on the right temple for 10 seconds. To turn them back on, close and open both arms of your frames.

To turn off your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) microphones:

    Tip: The action button is the shorter button on the right arm of the Echo Frames (2nd Generation).

  2. The status light flashes red when the microphones are turned off.

    Note: The mic and phone notifications off light turns red when Echo Frames (2nd Generation) microphones are off.

To turn your Echo Frames (2nd Generation) microphones on again, press the action button twice. Turning on the microphones also turns phone notifications back on. The status light flashes blue when the microphones are turned on.

Understanding Lights on Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa

  (3rd Generation) {#understanding-lights-on-echo-frames-2nd-generation-and-smart}

Echo Frames (2nd Generation) and Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation) use the status light and power LED to communicate their status to you.

Echo Frames (2nd Generation)

  • Status Light Colors: Cyan and Blue; Dark Blue: Alexa is active.
  • Status Light Colors: Red; Dark Blue: There’s an error or the microphone and phone notifications are turning off.
  • Status Light Colors: Red and Blue; Dark Blue: The device is in Bluetooth pairing mode with your smartphone.
  • Status Light Colors: White; Dark Blue: The OS assistant is active.
  • Status Light Colors: Power LED; Dark Blue: Green; The device is looking for a Bluetooth connection.: The device is 100% charged.
  • Status Light Colors: Amber; Dark Blue: The device is charging.
  • Status Light Colors: Mic & Phone Notifications Off LED; Dark Blue: Red; The device is looking for a Bluetooth connection.: The microphone and phone notifications are off.

Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation)

  • Status Light Colors: Blinking Blue; Fading Orange: Bluetooth connectivity.
  • Status Light Colors: Blinking Cyan/Blue; Fading Orange: Alexa is active.
  • Status Light Colors: White; Fading Orange: The OS assistant is active.
  • Status Light Colors: Fading Red/Fading Blue; Fading Orange: Microphone is muted/mic is on.
  • Status Light Colors: Solid Red/Solid Blue; Fading Orange: Power off.
  • Status Light Colors: Blinking Red; Fading Orange: Error with Echo Frames: Follow the troubleshooting in Soft Reset Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation).
  • Status Light Colors: Charging Stand; Fading Orange: Solid Green; The device is in Bluetooth pairing mode.: Full battery.
  • Status Light Colors: Solid Orange; Fading Orange: Charging.
  • Status Light Colors: Blinking White; Fading Orange: Detecting smart glasses placement.
  • Status Light Colors: Blinking Red/ Blinking Red and White; Fading Orange: Error: Reinsert glasses. Follow the troubleshooting in How to Charge Your Smart Glasses with Alexa (3rd Generation).

Update the Software on Echo Auto

Your smartphone automatically downloads available software updates for Echo Auto when connected to the Internet.

When your phone has downloaded Echo Auto updates, they install the next time your phone connects to your Echo Auto over Bluetooth. You can check the software version in the device settings section of the Alexa app.

Note: To force an immediate update for your Echo Auto, uninstall and reinstall the Alexa app on your smartphone. To remove the app, use your phone’s uninstall procedures. Then, find the Alexa mobile app at your phone’s app store and reinstall it. Uninstalling the app doesn’t affect your existing device connections. Reinstalling the app sends updates to your on-the-go Alexa devices, including Echo Auto.

  • Alexa Device Software Versions

Update the Software on Echo Buds

Your Echo Buds automatically download software updates when they’re in their case and connected to the internet.

Recent updates install over Bluetooth when you charge your Echo Buds in their case. You can check which software version you own by referring to the devices section of the Alexa app.

Note: To receive software updates, first register your Echo Buds in the Alexa app.

To manually update the software on Echo Buds:

  1. Download the latest version of the Alexa app on your phone.
  2. Place your Echo Buds in the case and keep the lid open.
  3. In the Alexa app, check that your Echo Buds are connected to your phone.
  4. Check that your Echo Buds and case area at least 30% charged.
  5. Close the case lid.
  6. Keep your Echo Buds next to your phone with the case closed for at least 30 minutes.
  • Alexa Device Software Versions
  • Use the Alexa App to Check Battery Status on Echo Buds

Update the Wi-Fi Settings for Your Echo Device

Use the Alexa app to update your device’s Wi-Fi settings, or connect to a network.

Note: If you have an Echo screen device, update or change the Wi-Fi settings on the device itself. For those instructions, visit Update the Wi-Fi Settings on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select your device.
  4. Select Device Settings .
  5. Select Change or remove a Wi-Fi network.
  6. Connect to one of your previously connected Wi-Fi networks. If you don’t see the Wi-Fi network that you want to connect to, select Join another Wi-Fi Network.
  7. Then follow the instructions in the Alexa app.

Tip: If you have an Echo Spot (2024 Release), select the Wi-Fi Off icon on the device screen. Then scan the QR code with your mobile device, and select the link to start the Wi-Fi settings process in the Alexa app.

Echo devices connect to Wi-Fi networks used in most homes such as Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz / 5 GHz networks that use the 802.11a / b / g / n standard. Echo devices can’t connect to ad-hoc (or peer-to-peer) networks.

Vision Insurance Reimbursement and FSA|HSA for Echo Frames and Smart Glasses

If you purchase Echo Frames and add prescription lenses, you can submit an out-of-network reimbursement claim for your Echo Frames.

Some insurance providers allow you to submit an out-of-network claim for reimbursement of your Echo Frames and Smart Glasses. They aren’t directly covered in-network by any vision insurance provider.

Amazon has confirmed with the following insurance provider that Echo Frames and Smart Glasses are eligible for out-of-network reimbursement depending on your plan. You may be able to get reimbursed for your purchase by your vision insurance company. Amazon can’t confirm reimbursement for you. It’s best to confirm coverage in advance with your insurance company directly.

Steps for Reimbursement

  1. Fill out a health insurer specific claim form.
  2. Please submit both invoices for your prescription lens and Echo Frames and/or Smart Glasses. Print your detailed invoice receipt and include with the claim form. To find an invoice for your purchase, go to your Order History.
  3. Select the following links to learn more about the steps to submit your claim form and receipt.
  • VSP Vision Care: Submit oon claim (vsp.com)
  • EyeMed: Out of network claims (eyemed.com)
  • Cigna: Home (public.cignaenvoy.com)
  • MetLife: Vision insurance (metlife.com)

Didn’t find your insurance? Contact your insurance company directly for instructions on applying for reimbursement.

FSA | HSA

Your Echo Frames and Smart Glasses frames may be eligible for FSA or HSA reimbursement if you have corrective lenses. You can check with your FSA | HSA provider for details on your plan and review the provider’s instructions on how to submit claims for reimbursement. Don’t forget to check the balance on your FSA | HSA account.

All the FSA | HSA money you set aside is 100% tax-free. HSA funds don’t expire from year-to-year like FSA funds. Typically, you need to use your FSA money within the plan year, which often ends on December 31.

Steps for Reimbursement

  1. Fill out a health insurer specific claim form.
  2. Please submit both invoices for your prescription lens and Echo Frames and/or Smart Glasses. Print your detailed invoice receipt and include with the claim form. To find an invoice for your purchase, go to your Order History.
  3. Select the insurance provider links to learn more about the steps to submit your claim form and receipt.

Wall Mount Your Echo Hub

Use the hardware included with your Echo Hub.

[Embedded video omitted]

Your Echo Hub comes with a power adapter and the mounting hardware needed to wall mount your device. If you don’t want to wall mount your Echo Hub, you can purchase a compatible stand.

To mount the Echo Hub on the wall, you need:

  • Included wall mounting template
  • Included wall mount and mounting hardware
  • Electric drill, with 1/4” (or 6.5 mm) drill bit and Phillips #2 driver bit
  • Hammer
  • Spirit level or level app
  • Wall-safe tape, such as painter’s tape

Important: Please note these tips before mounting your device:

  • Don’t drill holes where you might impact studs, electrical wire, or piping.
  • Before mounting, unplug the device from electric outlets. Keep your device away from water.
  • Consider the height of everyone using the device. We recommend placing it at about eye level for the people who will use it most.

To mount your Echo Hub:

  1. Use the mounting tips and included mounting template to identify where to mount your device.
  2. Place the template on the wall, with the triangle at the top, at your chosen height and location.
  3. Use a level or level app to level the template, then tape the template in place. You can also mark the drill points with a pencil.
  4. Use an electric drill with a 1/4” or 6.5-mm drill bit. Drill through the designated holes in the template. Remove the template after you drill the holes.
  5. Slowly hammer the two included anchors into the holes until they’re flush with the wall.
  6. Place the wall mount against the wall, then align the two holes with the installed anchors.
  7. With the Phillips driver bit, drive the screws through the two wall mount holes and into the installed anchors. Tighten until the screws are flush against the wall mount.
  8. Plug the supplied power cord into your Echo Hub. Don’t plug the power adapter into a wall outlet yet.
  9. Place the Echo Hub over the top of the wall mount, parallel to the wall, with the device buttons on the right. Slide the device down over the mount, so that the mount hooks engage firmly with the device. Make sure that all four hooks in the wall mount engage with your device.
  10. Connect the device power adapter into a wall outlet.

Wall Mount Your Echo Show

Use the wall mounting hardware included with your compatible Echo Show to mount your device on your wall.

[Embedded video omitted]

Your Echo Show 15 or Echo Show 21 device comes with a power adapter and the mounting hardware needed to wall mount your device. You can also purchase a compatible extension cable for your device. Stands, under-cabinet mounts, and extension cables are not included with your device and can be purchased separately.

If you’d prefer hiring a professional to wall mount your device, you can check your eligibility for Amazon Home Services in-home installation at Amazon Home Services.

A wall mounting template and instructions are included with your device.

Tools You’ll Need:

  • Electric drill with 5/16” (or 8 mm) drill bit and Phillips #2 driver bit
  • Hammer
  • Level or level app
  • Wall-safe tape
  • Included wall mounting template
  • Included wall mount and mounting hardware

Important: Read these tips before mounting your device.

  • Consider the height of everyone using the device. We recommend placing the device at eye level.
  • Find a mount location away from water or moisture.
  • Make sure there’s enough room to mount the device in either orientation.
  • Don’t drill holes over studs, electrical wire, or piping.
  • Before mounting, unplug the device from electric outlets.

To mount your Echo Show on your wall:

  1. Use the mounting tips and included mounting template to identify where to mount your device.

  2. Place the template on the wall in your chosen orientation.

  3. Use a level or level app to level the template, then tape the template in place.

  4. Use an electric drill with a 5/16” or 8 mm drill bit. Drill through the designated holes in the template. Remove the template after you drill the holes.

  5. Slowly hammer each of the four anchors into the holes until they are flat against the wall.

  6. Place the wall mount against the wall, then align the four holes with the installed anchors. Make sure the arrow on the wall mount is at the top.

  7. With the #2 driver bit, drive the screws through the wall mount holes until the screws are flat against the wall mount.

  8. Plug the supplied power cord into your device. Best to do this now, as it’s harder to access the power port once the device is mounted.

    Note: Don’t plug the device into a wall outlet yet.

  9. Place your device flat over the top of the wall mount.

  10. Slide your device down. Make sure that all four hooks in the wall mount are engaged with your device.

  11. Make sure that your device is placed with the camera at the top.

  12. Plug your device into a wall outlet.

To change your device’s orientation, unhook it from the wall mount. Remount it in the other orientation.

What Do the Audio Tones Mean on My Echo Buds (2023 Release)?

Echo Buds provide a simple and brief audio cue to communicate a change in device status.

Audio tones are used by Echo Buds (2023 release) for all notifications after setup.

In Ear Connected

Your Echo Buds is in-ear and Bluetooth connected to the phone.

In Ear Not Connected

Your Echo Buds are having a connection problem.

Low Battery

Your Echo Buds battery is low (10% or less).

Incoming Call

Lets you know when you are being called.

Volume Changed

When the volume on your Echo Buds changes.

Wake Word Success

Immediately after the wake word is used and Alexa begins cloud streaming.

End of Utterance

When you’ve finished speaking to Alexa and cloud streaming is closed.

Single Tap Gesture Success

Lets you know when a single touch action was successful.

Double Tap Gesture Success

Lets you know when a double touch action was successful.

Triple Tap Gesture Success

Lets you know when a triple touch action was successful.

Long Press Gesture Success

Lets you know when a long touch action was successful.

What Do the Indicators on Your Echo Device with a Screen Mean?

The light bar on your Echo Devices with a Screen to see how the device communicates its status.

If you have Alexa+, go to Indicators for Alexa+ on Echo Devices with a Screen.

Tip: Ask Alexa, “What does your light mean?”

Yellow

What it means:

  • A solid yellow bar means that Alexa has a message or notification, or there’s a reminder you missed. Say, “What are my notifications?” or “What are my messages?”

Cyan on Blue

What it means:

  • A cyan spotlight on a blue bar means that Alexa is listening. The spotlight moves briefly when Alexa is processing your request.

Teal Blue

What it means:

  • A teal blue bar indicates that Alexa is ready for you to speak. This means that you can speak directly to Alexa without first saying the wake word.

Red

What it means:

  • The red light bar tells you the microphones on/off button is pressed, and the device microphones and camera are off. Press the button again to turn on the device microphones and camera.

Orange

What it means:

  • Your device is trying to connect to the Internet.

Green

What it means:

  • The green light bar comes on when you’re in a call or a Drop In, and you leave the call screen. It shows that you’re still on an active call.

Purple

What it means:

  • When the Do Not Disturb feature is on, a purple light bar briefly shows after you make any request. Turn off Do Not Disturb to speak with Alexa again.

  • About Alexa’s Personality with Alexa+

What Do the Lights on Echo Auto Mean?

The lights on your Echo Auto are how the device communicates its status.

Cyan on Blue

  • A cyan on blue light will appear when Alexa is listening.
  • The cyan light moves toward the center of the device when Alexa has heard and is processing your request.
  • Side-to-side movement means that the device is starting up or waiting for a Bluetooth connection.

Red

  • A static or slowly moving red light appears when Alexa isn’t listening and the device microphone is turned off.
  • To enable your microphone again, press the Mute button on your Echo Auto.

Orange

  • When the device is in setup mode or trying to connect to the Internet, a sweeping or static orange light will appear.
  • A pulsing light may indicate that a factory reset is in progress.

Green

  • A green light appears when a call or message is in progress or when you have an incoming call. Say, “Answer the call.”

Yellow

  • When you have a new notification, a yellow light will appear. Say, “Read my notifications.”

Purple

  • During initial setup, a purple light may appear to indicate that setup has failed.

What Do the Lights on Echo Link and Echo Link Amp Mean?

The LED is how your device communicates its status.

Flashing Orange: You can set up the device.

Flashing Purple: The device setup failed. Try to set up the device again.

Flashing Red: There are connection issues.

Flashing Blue: The device is starting up.

What Do the Lights on the Echo Buds (2021 Release, 2nd Generation) Case Mean?

The three LED lights on your Echo Buds case show the charging status for both ear buds and the case.

Tip: To check the battery life of Echo Buds, ask, “Alexa, what’s my battery?”

Note: The LED light on the outside of the case means different things when the case is closed or open. When the case is closed, the LED light shows the battery status for whichever ear bud has the lowest battery level. When the case is open, the LED light tells you the battery status for the case. The two LED lights inside the case show the battery status for each ear bud.

To identify the battery level, first ensure that the Echo Buds are in the case. Then press the button on the case (or open the case lid).

  • LED Color: Green; Meaning: The ear bud is at least 40 percent charged and has more than 2 hours of battery life for streaming music remaining. The case has more than one full charge. For more information on battery life, refer to Echo Buds Battery Life Testing Information.
  • LED Color: Yellow; Meaning: The ear bud is less than 40 percent charged and has less than 2 hours of battery life for streaming music remaining. The case has less than one full charge. For more information on battery life, see Echo Buds Battery Life Testing Information.
  • LED Color: Red; Meaning: The case or ear bud is at a critically low level, and has less than 5 percent battery remaining.
  • LED Color: Flashing Green; Meaning: The case and ear buds are charging.
  • LED Color: Flashing Blue; Meaning: The device is in pairing mode.
  • LED Color: Flashing Red; Meaning: - The device is charging when the battery is critically low. - Or, there’s an error with the device. Make sure that the buds are clean and connecting with the charging pins.
  • LED Color: Flashing Orange; Meaning: Factory reset is starting.

What Do the Lights on the Echo Buds (2023 Release) Case Mean?

The LED light on the Echo Buds case communicate charging status for both the buds and the case.

Tip: To check the battery life of Echo Buds, ask, “Alexa, what’s my battery?”

With Echo Buds in the Case:

To view the battery level, press the button on the case (or open the case lid). The LED indicator displays the status of the earbud with the lowest battery level. For more information on battery life, go to Echo Buds Battery Life Testing Information

Green

Both of the buds are at least 50 percent charged.

Yellow

One or both of the buds are less than 50 percent charged.

Red

One or both of the buds are at critical level, and have less than 5 percent battery remaining.

Flashing LED (Green, Yellow, or Red)

The buds are charging.

Flashing Blue

The device is in pairing mode.

Rapidly Flashing Red

There’s an error with the device. Check to make sure that the buds are clean and connecting with the charging pins.

Flashing Orange

Factory reset is starting.

When Charging Case is Empty

Solid Green

The case has more than one full charge.

Solid Yellow

The case has less than one full charge.

Solid Red

The case has low battery.

Flashing LED (Green, Yellow, or Red)

The buds are charging.

Alexa FAQs

### 1. How do I use Alexa?

Alexa allows you to ask questions and make requests using just your voice. For instance, you can ask Alexa a question, such as “What is the weather today in New York?”, or tell Alexa to do something, like “Add batteries to my shopping list,” or “Play jazz.” When you speak to Alexa, a recording of what you asked Alexa is sent to Amazon’s cloud so we can process and respond to your request. You can access Alexa differently based on the type of device you are using. For example, for “hands free” devices, like the Amazon Echo, you can access Alexa by saying the wake word (e.g., Alexa, Amazon, Computer, Echo, or Ziggy). For other devices, like certain Fire tablets and the Alexa app, you can access Alexa by pressing a button and speaking, or by typing a request to Alexa. You can use Alexa across a range of Amazon devices and services, including to help you shop on Amazon.com and the Amazon Shopping app, and to search for music on Amazon Music. Certain functionality may not be available across all devices and services where Alexa is available. For example, if you ask Alexa to set a timer while using Amazon.com, you may be routed to Alexa.com or the Alexa app to complete your request. To learn more about Alexa on Amazon.com and the Amazon Shopping app, visit the Alexa for Shopping FAQs.

### 2. What is Alexa+?

Alexa+ is the newest version of Alexa with more knowledge, greater capabilities, and many new features. For example, you can ask Alexa almost any question, share files for Alexa to summarize, or ask Alexa to remember something for your later use. Alexa+ is available across all your compatible Alexa-enabled products, including the Alexa app and Alexa.com. Devices not compatible with Alexa+ remain in the original Alexa experience. Alexa+ is currently only available in the English language.

### 3. Is Alexa recording all my conversations?

No. By default, Alexa-enabled devices are designed to detect only your chosen wake word (e.g., Alexa, Amazon, Computer, Echo, or Ziggy). The device detects the wake word by identifying acoustic patterns that match the wake word. No audio is stored or sent to the cloud unless the device detects the wake word (or Alexa is activated by pressing a button). On certain devices, you can enable features that allow you to interact with Alexa without the wake word. For instance, Follow Up Mode allows you to make follow-up requests to Alexa without having to repeat the wake word and, on compatible devices, interrupt Alexa to make requests. When you join Alexa+, Follow Up Mode will be turned on for your compatible Echo devices and the Alexa app. See the FAQ “How does Follow Up Mode work?” for more information. You can also configure supported Echo devices to detect specific sounds, such as the sound of smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms, and glass breaking. See the FAQs “How does Alexa Emergency Assist work?” and “How do Routines with sound detection work?” for more information.

### 4. What happens when I speak to Alexa?

When you speak to Alexa, a recording of what you ask Alexa is sent to Amazon’s cloud, where we process your request and other information to respond to you. As part of that processing, we create a text transcript of your request to help Alexa interpret and understand what you said, take any requested actions, and provide a response. For example, when you ask “Alexa, play top hits on Amazon Music,” we use the recording of your request and information from Amazon Music to play top hits.

### 5. How does Alexa minimize the amount of data sent to the cloud?

Alexa-enabled devices are designed to record as little audio as possible and minimize the amount of background noise streamed to the cloud. By default, Alexa-enabled devices only stream audio to the cloud if the wake word is detected (or Alexa is activated by pressing a button). When an Alexa-enabled device detects the wake word and begins streaming audio to the cloud, Alexa performs a “cloud verification” of the wake word using the more powerful processing capabilities of the cloud to double-check the audio to confirm detection of the wake word. If the cloud verification does not also detect the wake word, Alexa stops processing the audio and ends the audio stream to the cloud. See the FAQ “How does Follow Up Mode work?” for more information about how audio is processed for a feature that allows you to interact with Alexa without the wake word.

### 6. What about “false wakes”?

In some cases, your Alexa-enabled device might interpret another word or sound as the wake word (for instance, the name “Alex” or someone saying “Alexa” on the radio or television). When this happens, we call that a “false wake.” We have a team of world-class scientists and engineers dedicated to continually improving our wake word detection technology and preventing false wakes from happening, including through the cloud verification mechanism described in the FAQ “How does Alexa minimize the amount of data sent to the cloud?”

Anytime your Echo device detects the wake word, a visual or audible indicator will signal it is recording audio to stream to the cloud, and you can review and delete the voice recordings associated with your account (including any audio resulting from a false wake) in Review Alexa History available at More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com).

### 7. Can I review and delete my Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?

Yes. You can review and delete Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts of those recordings, and typed requests to Alexa associated with your Amazon account by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). When you make a series of requests to Alexa, your requests may be grouped together for review into a single “chat” if Alexa determines those requests are related to one other. For example, if you ask several questions in short succession about places to visit in Paris, those requests may be grouped together into a single chat in Review Alexa History so you can easily go back to review the recommendations Alexa provided in that chat.

Deleting voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests may limit our ability to personalize your experience and make improvements based on your interactions with Alexa and cause certain features to stop working. For example, if you choose not to save any voice recordings, voice IDs associated with your account will be deleted and voice ID will not work. Similarly, if you delete the voice recordings Alexa used to create your voice ID (by, for example, choosing to have your Alexa voice recordings deleted automatically after 3 or 18 months), voice ID may not work.

If you have changed your default marketplace while using an Alexa-enabled product, you will need to delete all Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests associated with your account separately for each marketplace. To learn how to transfer your Amazon account to another marketplace, go here.

For voice requests you make to Alexa in the Amazon Shopping app, we automatically delete the voice recordings of those requests, but we retain their transcripts until you choose to delete them. See the Voice Shopping FAQs to learn more about how we handle your voice requests to Alexa in the Amazon Shopping app.

### 8. Can I choose to automatically delete my voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?

Yes, you can choose to automatically delete your voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa after a specified period of time (3 or 18 months), or you can choose to not save any voice recordings. If you choose automatic deletion after 3 or 18 months, we will delete the voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests associated with a chat once the specified period of time has passed since your last request to Alexa within that chat. If you choose not to save any voice recordings, we will automatically delete your voice recordings after we process your requests and automatically delete all existing voice recordings associated with your account, but your text transcripts of those recordings and any typed requests will be retained for 30 days after your last interaction with Alexa in a given chat, after which they will automatically be deleted. We retain those text transcripts and typed requests to allow you to review the requests you make to Alexa, and to improve your Alexa experience and our services. You can delete the text transcripts at any time by going to More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com).

### 9. What happens when I delete my Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?

When you delete Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa associated with a chat, we will delete those items from Amazon’s cloud. We may still retain other records of your Alexa interactions, such as attachments you shared with Alexa, information you provided through your interactions, records of actions Alexa took in response to your requests, records of products you searched for, and other information related to your requests. This allows us, for instance, to continue to provide your reminders, timers, and alarms, process your orders, personalize your experience, remember your preferences and the things you’ve shared with Alexa (like notes in Remember This and information relevant to you), show your shopping lists, tasks, and messages sent through Alexa Communication, and answer questions about attachments you’ve shared with Alexa. If your request was processed by an Alexa skill, deleting your voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa does not delete any information retained by the developer of that skill (skill developers do not receive voice recordings). For more information on Alexa skills, refer to the FAQ “How do Alexa skills work?” For more information on notes, refer to the FAQ “What is Remember This?” For more information on removing messages sent through Alexa Communication, refer to the FAQ “How do I remove Alexa messages from my conversation list?” For more information about reviewing, downloading, or deleting an attachment you’ve shared with Alexa, refer to the FAQ “How does Review Attachments work?” For more information on deleting the voice recordings you used to teach Alexa your voice when you created a voice ID, refer to the FAQ “How does voice ID work?”

### 10. How does deletion work?

You can delete certain data associated with your account. For instance, you can delete your voice recordings, text transcripts of those recordings, and typed requests to Alexa, as well as information Alexa receives from third-party smart home devices, using settings available in the Alexa app or at Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). When you request deletion, we begin the process of securely deleting your data from Amazon’s cloud storage systems.

Our deletion processes are designed to be comprehensive and can take some time to complete. While we are processing your deletion request, the data for which you requested deletion may still be used to personalize your experience, including by informing Alexa’s responses, and we may still provide that data to you in response to a data access request. We make every effort to ensure our deletion processes run smoothly; however, the specific timing of deletion may vary based on the type of information requested for deletion and the technical operation of our internal systems. Alexa does not support voice requests to delete data in all circumstances, and Alexa may not always interpret or execute requests to delete information made by voice correctly. We design our systems to continue securely processing your requests until deletion is completed. You can always review the voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa associated with your account at any time by going to More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). Data that is collected by third parties, like skill developers, and data stored outside of Amazon’s cloud, like data stored on your Echo or mobile devices, may not be deleted. Your deletion requests may not delete copies of data that have been de-identified and are no longer linked to you or your account. If we have used your data to improve our services, we may continue to retain and use the systems trained on your data after your data has been deleted from our data stores.

For more information on how deletion works in various contexts, see the FAQs “What happens when I delete my Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?”, “How can I delete the information Alexa receives from my third-party smart home devices?”, and “Can I review and delete my Alexa Emergency Assist audio recordings?”

### 11. What is the Review Alexa History feature?

Review Alexa History is a feature that allows you to play the audio of your voice recordings that were streamed to the cloud, review the text transcript of what Alexa thought you said, and review your typed requests to Alexa, as well as Alexa’s responses. This feature can help you better understand how Alexa works and what Alexa is and is not recording. You can also use it to recall answers Alexa gave you previously, such as the name of a restaurant Alexa recommended. If Alexa makes a mistake, you can use this feature to see what may have gone wrong, such as whether Alexa misunderstood a particular word or phrase. You can access Review Alexa History by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). You can also help us improve our services by providing feedback within Review Alexa History.

### 12. How can I manage the use of my voice recordings?

You can manage the use of your voice recordings to improve our services and develop new features by visiting More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Your Alexa Data in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com).

### 13. How does Alexa use my voice recordings, text transcripts, typed requests to Alexa, and other information?

Alexa uses your voice recordings, text transcripts, typed requests to Alexa, and other information, including your notes, calendars, emails, and attachments you send to Alexa, as well as information from third-party services, (such as your linked accounts) to answer your questions, fulfill your requests, and personalize and improve your experience and our services. For example, with Alexa+, Alexa can have human-like conversations by adapting the sentiment, tone, and content of its responses to address your request. This enables Alexa to sound excited or empathetic if, for example, your favorite sports team wins or loses. We also associate your requests and other information with your Amazon account to enable you to review your voice recordings, access other Amazon services, and provide you with a more personalized experience. For example, Alexa can pick up from where you left off if you ask Alexa to play an audiobook from Audible and can provide you with personalized recommendations and responses to your requests that are based on your order history, the songs you have listened to on Amazon Music, or the topics you have discussed with Alexa. We also personalize your experience based on conversations you’ve had with Alexa. For example, if you discuss your preference for Thai food with Alexa, Alexa may remember that preference and take it into account when you ask for restaurant recommendations. With Alexa+, we may also share relevant information from your interactions with our services to enable skill developers to provide you with a more personalized experience and deliver the content or services you request. See the FAQ “What information do we make available to developers to enable skill personalization in Alexa+?”

### 14. How do my voice recordings, text transcripts, typed requests to Alexa, and other interactions with Alexa improve Amazon’s services?

Alexa is designed to get smarter and more personalized every day. For example, we use your Alexa interactions to help improve Alexa’s ability to understand and respond to natural language requests and to train Amazon’s machine learning models. Training our models with real world interactions from a diverse range of customers is necessary for Alexa to respond properly to variations in our customers’ speech patterns, dialects, accents, and vocabulary, the acoustic environments where customers use Alexa, and the many ways in which customers engage with Alexa. This training relies in part on supervised machine learning, an industry-standard practice where humans review an extremely small sample of your Alexa interactions to help Alexa understand how to interpret your requests correctly and provide appropriate responses. For example, a human reviewing a customer’s voice request for the weather in Austin may identify that Alexa misinterpreted it as a request for the weather in Boston. And a human reviewing Alexa’s response to a request about a current event may determine whether Alexa’s response was accurate, appropriate, and properly personalized. Our supervised learning process includes multiple safeguards to protect customer privacy. For example, you can review and delete your voice recordings, and you can manage the use of your voice recordings to improve our services and develop new features, by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). We also may use your interactions with Alexa to improve other Amazon products and services. For example, when you shop on Alexa, we may use those interactions to improve the systems we use to help customers search for products.

### 15. How can I manage my Alexa advertising preferences?

Certain experiences on Alexa, such as streaming music or news videos on your Echo Show device, may contain ads. Some of those ads may be interest-based. Interest-based ads, sometimes referred to as personalized or targeted ads, present you with features, products, and services that might be of interest to you based on your interactions with certain content or services. For instance, if you ask Alexa to order paper towels or for recipe ideas, you might see or hear ads related to cleaning products or cooking utensils. We offer you settings to manage your interest-based advertising preferences.

We make available unique, user-resettable identifiers called advertising IDs to third-party skill developers and content providers (like radio providers) for advertising and analytics purposes. Each third-party developer and content provider receives a different Alexa Advertising ID for you, and a different Alexa Advertising ID for each device you use to access the applicable third-party skill or content. You can instruct these third parties not to use these advertising IDs to deliver interest-based ads to you or to build profiles for advertising. Developers and content providers are responsible for honoring your preferences.

To manage your preferences for third parties and reset your Alexa Advertising IDs, visit More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Skill Permissions and Ad Preferences in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). Even if you turn this setting off, developers and content providers will still receive Alexa Advertising IDs for other purposes, such as reducing ad repetition and fraud detection, but you can reset your Alexa Advertising IDs at any time.

You can also choose whether to receive interest-based ads delivered by Amazon on Alexa. If you choose not to receive interest-based ads from Amazon, you may still receive personalized recommendations and other similar features. You will still receive ads provided by Amazon, but they will not be based on your interests. You can manage this setting at More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Your Alexa Data in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). This setting does not apply to ads delivered by Amazon when you use other Amazon apps or services, such as Amazon Music and Fire TV, even if you use Alexa to interact with those apps or services. To learn more about Amazon’s interest-based advertising, see our Interest-Based Ads notice.

### 16. How do Alexa skills work?

Skills enable developers to make content or services available to you on Alexa. You can view and enable skills in the Alexa app and enable certain skills by voice. You can use a skill by saying a specific phrase, called the invocation name. When you use a skill, we may exchange relevant information with the developer of that skill, such as your answers when you play a trivia skill, your ZIP code when you ask for the weather, or the content of your requests, which may include text transcripts (but not your voice recordings). If you make a request to Alexa without using a skill invocation name, we may send the content of your request to several skills, and enable and launch the skill we think is best able to respond to your request. The Alexa app contains more information about skills, such as privacy policies and terms provided by skill developers. By default, we do not share your personal information with skill developers. You can choose to grant us permission to share additional information with a skill developer (such as your name and email address with a restaurant booking skill to make a reservation). With Alexa+, we may share relevant information from your interactions with our services to enable skill developers to provide a more personalized experience and deliver the content or services you request. For more information, see the FAQ “What information do we make available to developers to enable skill personalization in Alexa+?” You can see and manage the skills that you granted permission to access specific additional information through More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Skill Permissions and Ad Preferences in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). If you are an Alexa+ user, you can see and manage certain skills through More > Settings > Manage Alexa+ Services in the Alexa app.

### 17. What information do we make available to developers to enable skill personalization in Alexa+?

When you use a skill on Alexa+, we may share the content of your request and other relevant information from your interactions with our services to enable the skill developer to personalize your experience and deliver the content or services you request. For example, if you use your music skill to create a playlist for your upcoming vacation, Alexa may share information from prior discussions about snorkeling gear and beach destinations as well as your music genre preference with your music skill so that skill can create a relevant, personalized playlist for you. See the FAQs “How does Alexa use my voice recordings and other information?”, “Can I share an attachment with Alexa?“, and”What is Remember This?” for more information.

18. How does purchasing on Alexa work?

You can tell Alexa to order or reorder eligible products available for sale through the Amazon website. You can also subscribe to eligible services using Alexa or purchase Alexa skills and products and services through Alexa skills using your default payment and shipping settings. You can see product and order details in the Alexa app, at Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com) or at Order history (amazon.com) for those orders. To see product and order details for your Amazon Pharmacy orders, visit the Amazon Pharmacy Your Orders page. Just like orders placed through the Amazon website, orders placed through Alexa are subject to Amazon’s Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice and, in the case of a subscription for a service, the terms for the applicable service.

Some Alexa skills allow you to purchase products or services from the developer of the skill (for instance, to order food through a restaurant’s skill) using payment information stored in your Amazon account and that you provide permission to share. Amazon doesn’t share your full payment method details with the developer; however, we do share your full payment method details with payment processors to process the transaction. Amazon will share with the developer your Amazon account information necessary to complete a transaction, which may include your name, email address, shipping address and phone number, billing address and phone number, and the last 4 digits of your payment method used during checkout. For additional information on how skill developers and their payment processors can use your Amazon account information necessary to transact purchases, please refer to the Shopper FAQ at Help 201754640 (pay.amazon.com). You can view certain transaction details in the Alexa app or at Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com).

Some Alexa skills allow you to purchase products and services from the developer of the skill using a payment method you provide directly to the developer. Your voice purchasing settings may not apply to those purchases.

### 19. Can I manage settings related to purchasing on Alexa, and what controls do I have over kids-related purchases?

Yes. By default, Alexa enables purchasing through voice and other options, and you can adjust these settings by going to More > Settings > Account Settings > Voice Purchasing in the Alexa app. For purchasing by voice, you can require a confirmation code that Alexa will ask you to say out loud when you want to place an order from Amazon, or turn off all voice purchasing, or turn off voice purchasing only in kid skills. See the FAQ “What is a kid skill and how do I give or revoke permission to use kid skills?” for more information. By default, your approval will be required for each voice purchase from Amazon through a kid skill before the purchase will be completed. You can allow purchases in kid skills without additional approval by changing this default setting in the Alexa app. Voice purchasing is turned off for Amazon Kids on Alexa.

### 20. What are the return and cancellation policies for purchases I make using Alexa?

For information on return policies applicable to non-digital products purchased on Amazon using Alexa, see Amazon Return Policy. Purchases of digital content are final. However, if you accidentally purchase digital content or a subscription to a non-Amazon service through Alexa, that purchase is eligible for return and refund if we receive your request within 7 days of the date of purchase. To request a refund, please contact Customer Service.

Amazon’s return policies do not apply to purchases of non-digital products or services made through third-party Alexa skills (for instance, a food order placed through a restaurant’s skill). Instead, the returns policy of the applicable skill developer applies.

In the case of a subscription, you may cancel the auto-renewal of a subscription to a non-Amazon service by visiting the detail page for the applicable Alexa skill in the Alexa app and adjusting your subscription settings; you will not receive a refund of any fees already paid. For subscriptions to Amazon services, see the terms of use for the applicable subscription for information on refund eligibility and cancellation terms.

### 21. What is a kid skill and how do I give or revoke permission to use kid skills?

Kid skills are skills that have been identified by the developer as directed to children under age 13. Consistent with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act, we require permission from a parent before kid skills can be used. You’ll be asked to give permission the first time you attempt to use a kid skill. After you’ve given permission, you will receive a confirmation email.

You can review or change permissions by visiting the Manage Parental Consent page on Amazon.com or by contacting Customer Service (Contact us (amazon.com)).

To learn more, please visit our Children’s Privacy Disclosure.

Kid skills may offer digital products for sale that can be accessed or used within the skill, such as additional stories or trivia questions. You can manage your voice purchasing settings for kid skills in the Alexa app. See the FAQ “Can I manage settings related to purchasing on Alexa, and what controls do I have over kids-related purchases?” for more information.

### 22. What is Echo Glow and how do I use it?

Echo Glow is a smart lamp designed to be used by families with children, including children under age 13. Consistent with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act, we require permission from a parent before you can connect Echo Glow to Alexa, which you will be prompted to give if you have not previously provided consent to enable child-directed experiences on Alexa. After you’ve given permission, you will receive a confirmation email.

You can review or change permissions by visiting the Manage Parental Consent page on Amazon.com or by contacting Customer Service (Contact us (amazon.com)).

To learn more, please visit our Children’s Privacy Disclosure.

### 23. How does voice ID work?

You can create a voice ID for your profile so Alexa can call you by name, recognize you when you speak to your Alexa-enabled devices, and do more to personalize your experience. When you create a voice ID, Alexa uses recordings of your voice to create an acoustic model of your voice characteristics, to update that model over time, and to improve Alexa’s voice recognition capabilities. Alexa stores these acoustic models in the cloud. If your voice ID is not recognized for 18 months, we will automatically delete the acoustic model for your voice. If Alexa recognizes your voice when you are using a third-party skill, that skill may receive a numeric identifier that allows it to distinguish you from other users in your household to better personalize your experience. You can delete your voice ID or turn off personalization of third-party skills based on voice ID in the Alexa app. If you taught Alexa your voice by reciting training phrases that Alexa asked you to recite, deleting your voice ID will also delete the voice recordings of those phrases. If you taught Alexa your voice in the course of a conversation with Alexa, the voice recordings used to create your voice ID will appear in your Voice History and can be deleted there, but if you delete them, your voice ID may no longer work.

### 24. How does visual ID work?

You can create a visual ID on compatible Echo devices with cameras. Visual ID enables Amazon to provide you with a more personalized experience by recognizing you when you are near a supported device or using a supported service. For example, when your face is detected, Alexa may send a signal to the cloud to deliver reminders and news stories that are relevant to you. You can also create a visual ID for your child, to help Alexa show age-appropriate content on the device’s home screen when Alexa recognizes them. Visual ID uses images of your face to create a numeric representation of your facial characteristics (your visual ID), which may be considered biometric data in some locations. Your visual ID may be updated over time to improve Amazon’s ability to recognize you. You can delete your visual ID at any time through Settings on your device or in the Alexa app. If your face is not recognized for 18 months on any of your supported devices, we will automatically delete your visual ID. Deleting your visual ID will also delete the images used to create it.

Visual IDs created on Echo devices are not supported on Astro devices. For more information on visual ID on Astro, see the FAQ “How do person detection and visual ID work on Astro?” here.

### 25. What is Local Voice Control?

Local Voice Control allows Alexa to fulfill a limited set of requests on select Echo devices when the device is not connected to the internet, such as requests to control supported lights, plugs, and switches. After your Echo device regains its internet connection, the recording of your request is sent to the cloud and available to review at More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). You can turn Local Voice Control off by visiting More > Settings > Device Settings in the Alexa app.

### 26. How does Amazon use the permissions I grant the Alexa app?

The Alexa app requests mobile device permissions to hear your requests, provide more personalized results, help you set up your Alexa-enabled devices, and support certain Alexa features. Below is a list of certain permissions the Alexa app may request, along with a description of some of the ways Amazon currently uses those permissions. You can manage the permissions you grant to the Alexa app in the settings for your mobile device.

Microphone. We use your mobile device’s microphone to support voice interactions with Alexa. On some mobile devices, we also need microphone access and permission to process audio from your Alexa-enabled Bluetooth devices.

Contacts. We use your mobile device contacts to help you call, message, and connect with your friends and family. To learn more about how we use your contacts for Alexa Communication, please see the Alexa Communication FAQs below.

Location. We use your mobile device’s geolocation to help Alexa provide more relevant content (e.g., weather, traffic, and restaurant recommendations) based on where you are using the app and to enable certain features (such as location-based Reminders and Routines). On some mobile devices, we also need the location permission to discover and connect to nearby Bluetooth devices and wifi networks to help you set up certain Alexa-enabled devices and to use certain Alexa features (e.g., Find My). Learn more about how we use geolocation data and how to delete it.

Bluetooth. We use Bluetooth signals from your mobile device to discover and connect to new Alexa-enabled devices, help you send text messages hands-free, and to determine if your mobile device is near Alexa-enabled devices in order to enable certain Alexa features (e.g., Notify When Nearby).

Storage. To enable certain Alexa features, we may need to store data locally on the device. For example, to improve the performance of the Alexa app, we may store certain data (e.g., map data) locally.

Camera. We use the camera on your mobile device to enable video calling, simplify device setup (e.g., scanning a device barcode to initiate setup), and enable certain other Alexa features.

Notifications. We use notifications to send you alerts, such as when you receive new messages or calls.

Let the app always run in the background. To use certain Alexa-enabled devices (e.g., Echo Auto) and features (e.g., Reminders and Routines), the Alexa app needs permission to always run in the background on certain mobile devices.

### 27. How does Alexa Emergency Assist work?

With an Alexa Emergency Assist subscription, you can configure supported Echo devices to detect specific sounds you select, such as the sound of smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Similar to how the wake word works, the device detects these sounds by identifying acoustic patterns that match the sounds you select. Alexa Emergency Assist does not store or send audio to the cloud unless the device detects a selected sound. Alexa can send you a Smart Alert, via a mobile notification, that allows you to listen to detected sounds through the Alexa app. You or others in your household can say “Alexa, call for help” to speak with a trained agent and ask that they request emergency assistance on your behalf. Alexa Emergency Assist is not a replacement for an alarm system or life safety device and cannot automatically contact emergency services, such as the police or fire department, on your behalf. See the FAQ “How do I request emergency services using Alexa Emergency Assist?” to learn more

### 28. Can I review and delete my Alexa Emergency Assist audio recordings?

Yes. You can review Alexa Emergency Assist audio recordings associated with your account and delete those recordings one by one or all at once by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). You can also choose to have Alexa Emergency Assist audio recordings older than 3 or 18 months deleted automatically. Deleting Alexa Emergency Assist audio recordings may degrade your Alexa experience. This will not delete other information about Alexa Emergency Assist, such as your Alexa Emergency Assist preferences and device settings.

### 29. How do I request emergency services using Alexa Emergency Assist?

If you have an active Alexa Emergency Assist subscription, you or others in your household can say “Alexa, call for help” to speak with a trained agent through the Urgent Response helpline. The agent can help request assistance from emergency responders such as fire, medical, or police services on your behalf. Additionally, your emergency contacts will receive a notification when a call to the Urgent Response helpline is placed and when the call ends. If you call Urgent Response from the Alexa app and have enabled location sharing, then Alexa will share your last known location with the agent and your emergency contacts. Calls to the Urgent Response helpline may be recorded. Note that Urgent Response is not a 911 service, and may not work in the event of outages or connectivity issues.

Make sure your household members know that you’ve enabled Urgent Response, and understand how it works. If you or others in your household accidentally place a call, please inform the agent that the call was placed by mistake. In order to request the dispatch of emergency services via Urgent Response, you must speak to the agent who answers the call and describe the nature of your emergency so they can pass details to dispatchers. If you would like to prevent Urgent Response calls from a specific device, you should disable Alexa Communication for that device (Settings >[Your Device Name]> Communications, then toggle to Off).

### 30. What is Amazon Sidewalk?

Sidewalk is a shared network that uses Echo and Ring devices to securely keep other devices connected and help find lost items by reporting their approximate location to the owner. Sidewalk can enable supported devices to remain connected even when wifi is lost or the supported devices are outside the range of their home wifi. Sidewalk uses a small portion of your internet bandwidth and the approximate location of your devices to provide these benefits to you and your neighbors. If you have linked your Ring and Amazon accounts, your Sidewalk preferences on your Alexa or Ring app will apply to all of your eligible Echo and Ring devices. Sidewalk is turned on for your eligible devices unless you have previously turned off the setting. You can turn off Sidewalk at any time. To learn more, please visit Sidewalk (amazon.com).

### 31. How do Routines with sound detection work?

You can configure supported Echo devices to trigger a set of automated actions through Routines when a specific sound you select has been detected, such as snoring or coughing. Your device will only detect these sounds at times you’ve chosen. Similar to the wake word, the device detects these sounds by identifying acoustic patterns that match the sounds you select. No audio is stored or sent to the cloud to provide this sound detection feature.

### 32. How can I get phone notifications through Alexa?

In the Alexa app, you can enable Alexa to read push notifications from your mobile device on certain mobile devices and accessories, such as Smart Glasses with Alexa and Echo Buds. After granting the Alexa app permission to access your contacts and mobile device notifications, you can use the VIP Filter feature to select the specific apps and contacts from supported messaging apps (SMS and more) that you want to hear notifications read from. Notifications will be processed and stored in Amazon’s cloud for a limited time so you can ask Alexa to replay your recent notifications. If you use VIP Filter, app and contact names that you choose to receive notifications from will populate lists in the Alexa app and will be stored in the Amazon cloud to provide the feature. You may delete these lists from the Amazon cloud through the Alexa app.

### 33. How does Follow Up Mode work?

On supported devices, you can use Follow Up Mode to allow more natural interactions with Alexa. When you join Alexa+, Follow Up Mode will be turned on for your compatible Echo devices and the Alexa app. If you leave Alexa+, Follow Up Mode will remain on for your Echo devices and the Alexa app (unless you have turned it off for a specific device or the app).

When Follow Up Mode is on, you can make follow-up requests to Alexa without having to repeat the wake word. On compatible Echo Show devices, you can also interrupt Alexa, without saying the wake word, when your device detects you are in view of the camera and facing the screen. At times, Alexa may detect you are making a follow-up request when you are not – for example, if you ask Alexa a question and then start speaking to someone else in the room after Alexa responds.

Visual indicators will show you when you can speak to Alexa without having to repeat the wake word and when your device is recording audio to send to the cloud. You can review and delete your voice recordings at any time by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). To turn Follow Up Mode on or off, go to the Settings on your device or in the Alexa app, or say “Alexa, turn [on/off] Follow Up Mode.”

### 34. What are Alexa Voice Comments?

This feature allows customers to send brief recorded messages to their favorite DJs, radio hosts, podcast hosts, and other content creators. You can use supported Alexa-enabled devices to send Voice Comments to eligible skill developers to be shared with your favorite content creators. When you say “Alexa, send a Voice Comment,” you will have up to 40 seconds to record your message. When you are done recording, you will have the option to preview your Voice Comment, re-record it, or send it. You can also cancel it at any time prior to sending. If you choose to send, Alexa will send your Voice Comment to the applicable skill developer to enable them to make the Voice Comment available to the content creator. Skill developers and creators may use your Voice Comment in accordance with the skill developer’s terms of use and privacy policies, which may include broadcasting it or reading its contents aloud during a show. Once you send a Voice Comment, you will not be able to delete it.

### 35. How does Gestures work?

On supported devices, you can enable the use of Gestures to control certain features, like timers, without needing to touch your device or speak to Alexa. For example, if enabled, you can dismiss a ringing timer by simply holding up your hand with your palm facing the device’s camera. When a supported event occurs, such as a ringing timer, Gestures uses on-device processing to detect the presence of a recognized Gesture. No images or video are sent to the cloud to provide Gestures. You can turn on Gestures through Settings on your device.

### 36. Can I share an attachment with Alexa?

Yes, with Alexa+, you can share attachments, such as images, documents, notebooks, and emails, with Alexa. You can share an attachment by emailing alexa@alexa.com or using the Alexa app, Alexa.com, or select Kindle devices. When you share an attachment with Alexa, Alexa will extract information, such as text or descriptions of images in an attachment, so that we can process and respond to your requests. Your attachment and this related information will be stored in our cloud and used to provide and improve our services and personalize your experience. This enables Alexa to do things like answer questions about topics related to your attachment or to provide a summary of your attachment. For example, if you ask about Italian cuisine, Alexa may reference a recipe for meatballs you have shared, along with other information that may be relevant to Italian cuisine, in order to respond to your request. Alexa may also use the information from your attachment to create things like calendar events, reminders, and lists (e.g., if you share an attachment that includes dates for events, Alexa can suggest events for you to add to your calendar). See the FAQ “How does Review Attachments work?” for more information about deleting attachments you have shared with Alexa.

### 37. How does Review Attachments work?

Review Attachments allows you to review, download, or delete an attachment you have shared with Alexa using the Alexa app, Alexa.com, or select Kindle devices. You can access this page within Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com). If you delete an attachment you have shared with Alexa, Alexa may still retain information from your attachment, such as text extracted from the attachment, descriptions of images in your attachment, or summaries of the contents of your attachment to provide and improve our services and personalize your experience. We may also retain information related to your deleted attachment in your Alexa History and in items that you have created, like calendar events, shopping and to-do lists, and reminders. You can manage your Alexa History by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app or Alexaprivacysettings (amazon.com).

### 38. What is Remember This?

With Remember This on Alexa+, you can ask Alexa to remember important details for you so you can access the information whenever you need it. You can review the things you ask Alexa to remember – we call them notes – by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices. Alexa may use your notes to provide and improve our services and personalize your experience. Your notes in Remember This may be accessible to anyone using your Alexa-enabled devices.

Amazon Kids on Alexa and Echo Devices FAQs

### 1. What is Amazon Kids on Alexa?

Amazon Kids on Alexa is an Alexa experience just for kids, available on compatible Echo devices. When you use Amazon Kids on Alexa, Alexa will play music, answer questions, read stories, tell jokes, and more with younger ears in mind. Certain Alexa features may differ when Amazon Kids on Alexa is enabled. For example, voice purchasing from Amazon is turned off and Alexa Communication, if enabled, is limited to only within the household, with contacts you select, and to emergency numbers if you have enabled features that allow such calls. Learn more about Amazon Kids on Alexa here. To learn more about Alexa, please see the Alexa FAQs above. To learn more about Alexa Communication, please see the Alexa Communication FAQs below. To learn more about supported Echo devices, please see the Alexa-Enabled Echo Device FAQs below.

### 2. How can my child access Amazon Kids on Alexa?

Your child can access Amazon Kids on Alexa on your supported Echo device when you turn on Amazon Kids for that device. When you turn on Amazon Kids for a device, that device will provide the Amazon Kids experience to anyone who uses the device until you turn off Amazon Kids for that device.
