Safety and Compliance Information for Amazon Echo Frames (3rd Generation)

Safety and Compliance Information for Amazon Echo Frames (3rd Generation)

Indication for Use. Amazon Echo Frames (3rd Generation) are spectacle frames intended to hold prescription lenses. They come with non-corrective lenses.

IMPORTANT PRODUCT INFORMATION

[Image: Warning symbol: Triangle with exclamation mark]

SAFETY INFORMATION

READ ALL SAFETY INFORMATION BEFORE USING THE DEVICE. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

[Image: Warning symbol: Triangle with exclamation mark]

BE AWARE OF SURROUNDINGS

PAY ATTENTION. Similar to other electronic devices, use of your Amazon Echo Frames (3rd Generation) (your “Device”) may divert your attention from other activities or impair your ability to hear surrounding sounds, including alarms and warning signals. Usage of colored lenses at night may be inappropriate, particularly if driving. Do not wear while driving if the eyewear impairs your peripheral vision or impacts your ability to recognize traffic signals.

Your device also contains a visible LED light that may distract you. For your safety and the safety of others, avoid using this device in a way that distracts you from activities that require your attention. For example, distracted driving can be dangerous and result in serious injury, death, or property damage. Always pay full attention to the road. Do not allow interactions with this device or Alexa to distract you while driving. Check and obey the applicable laws and regulations on the use of this device while operating a vehicle. You are solely responsible for safely operating your vehicle and complying with all applicable laws regarding use of electronic devices while driving. Always observe posted road signs, traffic laws, and road conditions.

Turn off the device or adjust your volume if you find it disruptive or distracting while operating any type of vehicle or performing any activity that requires your full attention.

[Image: Warning symbol: Triangle with exclamation mark]

BATTERY SAFETY

HANDLE WITH CARE. Your device contains a rechargeable lithium-ion polymer battery and should be replaced only by a qualified service provider. Do not disassemble, remove or attempt to modify or access the battery in your device. Avoid dropping the device or battery. If the device or battery is dropped, especially on a hard surface, and the user suspects damage,do not attempt repair. Contact Amazon Customer Service for assistance.

For models that support use of a wireless charger, ensure there are no metallic or magnetic foreign objects on the charger (such as coins, jewelry, metallic cases, keys, bank cards or other items) when charging. In limited circumstances, use of third party accessories may void your device’s limited warranty. Read all safety instructions for any accessories before using with your device.

Your device should only be charged using the included USB-A to USB-C cable. The provided USB-A to USB-C cable should be powered using a certified USB charger or USB charging port that is compliant with safety standards IEC/UL 62368-1 and/or IEC/UL 60950-1

[Image: Warning symbol: Triangle with ear]

AVOID PROLONGED LISTENING AT HIGH VOLUME. Prolonged listening of the player at high volume can damage the ear of the user. To prevent possible hearing damage, users should not listen at high volume levels for long periods.

[Image: Warning symbol: Triangle with exclamation mark]

DO NOT USE AS EYE PROTECTION. The lenses of this device have been tested as impact resistant within the meaning of 21 CFR 801.410, but are not shatterproof or indestructible.

SUNGLASS LENS: DO NOT use the device for direct viewing of the sun or for protection against artificial light sources (e.g. tanning beds) as it may affect your vision or damage your eyes.

BLUE LIGHT FILTERING LENS: DO NOT use the device for direct viewing of the sun as it may affect your vision or damage your eyes.

[Image: Warning symbol: Triangle with exclamation mark]

THIS DEVICE CONTAINS MAGNETS

This device and included charging cable contain magnets. Under certain circumstances, magnets may cause interference with some internal medical devices, including pacemakers and insulin pumps. This device and these accessories should be kept away from such medical devices.

WATER PROTECTION

Although this device has been tested to comply with IEC 60529-IPX4, the device is not waterproof and should not be immersed in water or other liquids.

  • Do not rinse under running water.
  • Do not spill food, oil, lotion, or other abrasive substances on the device.
  • Do not expose the device to pressurized water, high velocity water, soapy water, or extremely humid conditions (such as a steam room).
  • Do not immerse or submerge the device in water or expose the device to seawater, salt water, chlorinated water, or other liquids (such as beverages).
  • Do not wear the device while participating in water sports, e.g. swimming, waterskiing, surfing, etc.

If your device is exposed to water or sweat, follow these instructions:

  • Wipe the device with a soft, dry cloth. Allow the device to fully dry in a well ventilated area.
  • Do not attempt to dry the device with an external heat source (such as a microwave, oven, or hair dryer).
  • Failure to properly dry the device before charging may lead to compromised performance, charging issues, or erosion of components over time.
  • Dropping or otherwise damaging the Echo Frames may increase the possibility that exposure to water or sweat could harm the device.

OTHER USE AND CARE INSTRUCTIONS

  • Clean this device with a soft dry cloth. Do not use water, chemicals, or abrasive materials to clean the frames. To clean the lenses, use an alcohol free lens cleaner and a soft cloth.
  • Improper maintenance of this device may lead to skin irritation or injury. If skin, hearing or other problems develop, discontinue use immediately and consult a physician.
  • To reduce the risk of electrostatic discharge upon contact with this device, avoid such contact in extremely dry conditions.
  • Do not expose this device to extreme heat or cold. Store them in a location where temperatures remain within the storage temperature ratings set forth in this guide. The device and the included accessories are designed to function within the operating temperature ratings set forth in this guide. If it is too hot or too cold, they may not turn on or function properly until they have warmed or cooled, as the case may be, to within the applicable temperature ratings.
  • Do not attempt to uninstall/install lenses into the device yourself, improper handling could damage the device or result in injury.
  • This device and its included accessories are not intended for children and should not be used by children under the age of 14.

For additional safety, compliance, recycling and other important information regarding your device, please see Devicesupport (amazon.com) and the Alexa app in Help & Feedback > Legal & Compliance.

SERVICE YOUR DEVICE

If you suspect the device or the included accessories are damaged, to avoid potential injury discontinue use immediately and contact Amazon Customer Support. Contact details can be found at Devicesupport (amazon.com). Faulty service may void the warranty.

If you experience discomfort, headache, or dizziness, immediately discontinue using the device.

FCC Compliance Statement

This device complies with part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation is subject to the following two conditions: (1) This device may not cause harmful interference, and (2) this device must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.

Note: The Products have been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class B digital device or external switching power supply, pursuant to part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference in a residential installation. The Products generate, use and can radiate radio frequency energy and, if not installed and used in accordance with the instructions, may cause harmful interference to radio communications. However, there is no guarantee that interference will not occur in a particular installation. If a Product does cause harmful interference to radio or television reception, which can be determined by turning the Product off and on, the user is encouraged to try to correct the interference by one or more of the following measures:

  • Reorient or relocate the receiving antenna.
  • Increase the separation between the equipment and receiver.
  • Connect the equipment into an outlet on a circuit different from that to which the receiver is connected.
  • Consult the dealer or an experienced radio/TV technician for help.

Safety and Compliance Information for Echo Frames

Indications for Use. Echo Frames consist of spectacle frames with non-corrective lenses.

Use Responsibly. Read all instructions and safety information before use.

FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

BE AWARE OF SURROUNDINGS PAY ATTENTION. Similar to other electronic devices, use of Echo Frames may divert your attention from other activities or impair your ability to hear surrounding sounds, including alarms and warning signals. Your device also contains a visible LED light that may distract you. For your safety and the safety of others, avoid using this device in a way that distracts you from activities that require your attention. For example, distracted driving can be dangerous and result in serious injury, death, or property damage. Always pay full attention to the road. Do not allow interactions with this device or Alexa to distract you while driving. Check and obey the applicable laws and regulations on the use of this device while operating a vehicle. You are solely responsible for safely operating your vehicle and complying with all applicable laws regarding use of electronic devices while driving. Always observe posted road signs, traffic law, and road conditions.

Turn off the device or adjust your volume if you find it disruptive or distracting while operating any type of vehicle or performing any activity that requires your full attention.

BATTERY SAFETY HANDLE WITH CARE. This device contains a rechargeable lithium-ion polymer battery and should be replaced only by a qualified service provider. Do not disassemble, open, crush, bend, deform, puncture, shred or attempt to access the battery. Do not modify or remanufacture the battery, attempt to insert foreign objects into the battery, or immerse or expose it to water or other liquids, expose to fire, explosion or other hazard. Only use the battery for the system for which it is specified. Use of an unqualified battery or charger may present a risk of fire, explosion, leakage or other hazard. Do not short-circuit a battery or allow metallic conductive objects to come into contact with battery terminals. Avoid dropping the device. If the device is dropped, especially on a hard surface, and the user suspects damage, discontinue use and do not attempt repair. Contact Amazon Customer Service for assistance.

Keep this device and the included power adapter in a well-ventilated area and away from heat sources, especially when in use or charging. For more information about batteries, go to Devicesupport (amazon.com). This device should only be charged using the cable and adapter included with the device. Do not charge this device near water or in extremely humid conditions. Use only accessories included with this device.

AVOID PROLONGED LISTENING AT HIGH VOLUME. Prolonged listening of the player at high volume can damage the ear of the user. To prevent possible hearing damage, users should not listen at high volume levels for long periods.

DO NOT USE AS EYE PROTECTION. The lenses of this device have been tested as impact resistant within the meaning of 21 CFR 801.410, but are not shatterproof or indestructible.

THIS DEVICE CONTAINS MAGNETS. This device and included USB charging cable contains magnets. Under certain circumstances, magnets may cause interference with some internal medical devices, including pacemakers and insulin pumps. This device and these accessories should be kept away from such medical devices.

Water Protection Although this device has been tested to comply with IEC 60529 IPX4, the device is not waterproof and should not be immersed in water or other liquids. Do not rinse under running water.

If your device is exposed to water or sweat, follow these instructions:

  • Wipe the device with a soft, dry cloth.
  • Allow the device to fully dry in a well ventilated area. Do not attempt to dry the device with an external heat source (such as a microwave, oven, or hair dryer).
  • Failure to properly dry the device before charging may lead to compromised performance, charging issues, or erosion of components over time.
  • Do not intentionally immerse the device in water or expose it to seawater, salt water, chlorinated water, or other liquids (such as beverages).
  • Do not expose the device to pressurized water, high velocity water, soapy water, or extremely humid conditions (such as a steam room).
  • Do not spill any food, oil, lotion, or other abrasive substances on the device.

If the device is dropped or otherwise damaged, the device may be compromised when exposed to water or sweat.

Other Use and Care Instructions

  • Clean this device with a soft, dry cloth. Do not use water, chemicals, or abrasive materials to clean the frames.  Lens cleaners and soft cloth can be used to clean the lenses.
  • Improper maintenance of this device may lead to skin irritation or injury. If skin, hearing or other problems develop, discontinue use immediately and consult a physician.
  • To reduce the risk of electrostatic discharge upon contact with this device, avoid such contact in extremely dry conditions.
  • Do not expose this device to extreme heat or cold. Store them in a location where temperatures remain within the storage temperature ratings set forth in this guide.  The device and the included accessories are designed to function within the operating temperature ratings set forth in this guide. If it is too hot or too cold, they may not turn on or function properly until they have warmed or cooled, as the case may be, to within the applicable temperature ratings. For example, do not leave in the car on a hot day.
  • The device and its included accessories are not intended for children and should not be used by children under the age of 14.

Send Alexa Messages in the Alexa App

You can use the Alexa app to send messages to your Alexa contacts.

[Embedded video omitted]

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select More .
  3. Open Communicate .
  4. Select Message.
  5. Select New Message .
  6. Select a contact, and then type your message. You can also send a voice message.

Send Alexa Messages with Your Voice

Use your Alexa device to send messages to your Alexa contacts.

[Embedded video omitted]

Say, “Message [contact].”

Set a Custom Action in an Alexa Routine

Use a custom action to put an Alexa voice command into a routine.

When adding an action to a routine, select Custom to create your own actions for Alexa.

Type in what you want Alexa to do, just as you might say by voice, but without the wake word. For example,

  • “Set a timer for 30 minutes.”
  • “What’s today’s weather?”
  • “Play my most recent playlist.”

After entering your Custom action phrase, select Preview this action to make sure that Alexa responds correctly.

Tip: If your Custom action doesn’t work, test it by saying the custom action phrase directly to Alexa. It could also help to check what Alexa heard when you said the custom action phrase. In the Alexa app, open More and select Activity > Voice History to see what Alexa heard. When you find the phrase that works, enter the text into your Custom action.

Tip: If your routine has another action after your custom action and the two actions overlap, add a wait action between your custom action and the next action.

Set a Preferred Default Podcast Service on Alexa

Set a preferred default podcast service in the Alexa app.

  1. Open the Alexa app.
  2. Select More , then select Settings.
  3. Select Family Default Services.
  4. Select Change under Podcasts.
  5. Select your preferred podcast provider.

If you don’t see your preferred podcast default service listed, confirm that the service you’re using is available on Alexa.

Tip: You can set different default music and podcast services for each Alexa Profile on your Alexa account.

  • Manage Music and Podcast Service Settings for Your Alexa Profile

Set a Volume Limit on Your Kids’ Echo Devices

Use Parent Dashboard to keep the volume down for devices in child mode.

The Parent Dashboard lets you manage the Amazon Kids content that kids engage with. It also lets you control the volume of the device they use to play that content.

  1. Sign in to the Parent Dashboard using your Amazon login.
  2. Select Settings at the top of your child’s profile.
  3. Under Your Child Echo Devices, select the device that you want to have a volume limit.
  4. Select the arrow at Set Max Volume, then use the slider to select the maximum volume level you want.
  5. Select another page or the back arrow to finish. The volume level that you selected automatically saves when you leave the Set Max Volume page.

A volume limit set on a device applies only with Amazon Kids turned on. It doesn’t affect other devices, or any devices with Amazon Kids turned off.

Note: You can use the Parent Dashboard to set the volume limit on these supported devices:

  • Amazon Echo (3rd Gen or later)

  • Echo Dot (3rd Gen or later)

    • Note: Some versions of Echo Dot (3rd Gen) don’t support this feature.

  • Echo Show 5 (3rd Gen)

  • Echo Flex

  • Echo Pop

  • Set Controls for Amazon Kids on Alexa with the Parent Dashboard

Set Controls for Amazon Kids on Alexa with the Parent Dashboard

Set controls, such as a daily time limit, using the Parent Dashboard.

  1. Open the Parent Dashboard.
  2. Sign in with your Amazon credentials.
  3. Select the settings icon next to your child’s name.
  4. Select from the available options to manage your child’s experience.

Set Reminders with Alexa

Set Alexa Reminders either by voice command or in the Alexa app.

You can say:

  • “Remind me to pick up dry cleaning.”
  • “Remind me to schedule a car service appointment.”
  • “Make sure I call Janet at 4PM today.”
  • “Create a follow up reminder to pay rent.”
  • “Remind Josh to unload the dishwasher every day at 8 pm.”
  • “Remind Dad to buy milk at 7 pm.”
  • “Remind everyone to drink water at 9 am.”

The reminder is announced on the device you spoke the request to.

You can also set or edit reminders in the Alexa app on your mobile device.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Reminders.
  3. Select Add Reminder, then enter the details you want, including the Alexa device you want to announce the reminder.

Note: You can only assign a reminder to someone who has an Alexa profile on the same Amazon Alexa Account.

Set Up Alexa Emergency Assist

Set up Alexa Emergency Assist from the Alexa app or a compatible Echo device.

Before you set up Emergency Assist, make sure that:

  • Your Alexa app is up-to-date.
  • You have Alexa Communications turned on.

To set up Alexa Emergency Assist from the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open .
  3. Select Alexa Emergency Assist.
  4. Select the Settings icon, then select Your Information to review your profile. Make sure that you add an emergency address and phone number.
  5. Optional: Select Manage to add Critical Information like gate codes and medical conditions.

Note: The information in your Alexa Emergency Assist profile will be shared with Urgent Response agents and first responders to help you get the help you need.

Once you’ve reviewed your profile information, add Emergency Contacts and Smart Alerts to complete setup.

  • Add or Remove Emergency Contacts in Alexa Emergency Assist
  • Turn Alexa Emergency Assist Smart Alerts On or Off
  • Test Urgent Response Using Alexa Emergency Assist

Set Up Automatic Grouping for Your Smart Devices

Set up automatic actions and Alexa can take proactive actions on your smart devices, such as grouping them together.

Turn on automatic actions in the Alexa app:

  1. Select More .
  2. Select Settings .
  3. Scroll down and select Hunches.
  4. Select Set Up Hunches. Once complete, automatic actions for Hunches are turned on.

To activate or deactivate your individual automatic actions:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select More .
  3. Select Settings .
  4. Scroll down and select Hunches.
  5. Select the Hunches Settings icon.
  6. Select the automatic actions that you want Alexa to act on, including Lights, Plugs & Switches, and Groups.

Note: Under Groups, automatic grouping is activated by default but can be turned off. Automatic grouping automatically adds devices to groups based on their typical grouping.

  • What Is Alexa Automatic Grouping?

Set Up News and Flash Briefings for Alexa

Get news, local weather, and more from popular broadcasters with flash briefings.

To customize your new channel and flash briefings:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Select News, then select My News Channel or Flash Briefing.
    • Select My News Channel and choose your primary news channel for long-form news content.
    • Select Flash Briefing and choose multiple news sources for short updates and top stories.

Note: Alexa helps you select your preferred news providers when you ask to play news or a flash briefing for the first time. A list of available news providers is available in the Alexa Skills store.

Share Photos with Your Alexa Contacts

Use the Alexa app to share photos with your Alexa contacts.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select More .
  3. Select Communicate , then select Share.
  4. Select a photo. The photo can’t exceed 120 MB.
  5. Select a contact, then select Share.

Note: Shared photos are stored on Amazon Photos. If you unshare or delete photos in the Amazon Photos app, the recipient can no longer access them on their Echo device with a screen, Fire TV device, or Amazon Photos app. The photo is still viewable from the message thread in the Alexa app.

Sound Detection FAQs

1. What sounds can Alexa detect?

Alexa Emergency Assist can detect and notify you about the sound of smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms, and glass breaking.

2. What happens when Alexa detects a selected sound?

If a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm is activated Alexa will send a Smart Alert to your phone that includes an audio recording of the detected event so you can take action if you’re away from home. Tapping the notification opens the Alexa app where you can play back what Alexa heard or Drop In for live audio. If you need emergency help, you can tap the icon to call Urgent Response.

3. How does Alexa detect selected sounds?

Echo devices use the same technology used to detect the wake word (for example, “Alexa”) as supported Smart Alert sounds such as smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. If an Echo device detects an acoustic pattern that matches the selected sound, Alexa will send you a Smart Alert. Alexa is always getting smarter, and its ability to accurately detect specific sounds will improve the more you use Alexa Emergency Assist.

4. How do I enable Alexa to detect selected sounds?

Smart Alerts are disabled by default. To enable Alexa to detect smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and glass breaking, go to Alexa Emergency Assist > Settings > Smart Alerts in the Alexa app.

5. Can any Alexa-enabled device detect selected sounds?

No. Only Echo smart speakers and smart displays such as an Echo Dot or Echo Show can detect selected sounds and send you a Smart Alert. You should test Smart Alerts from each of your devices to confirm that that device is supported.

6. How can I test Smart Alerts?

To test Smart Alerts, you will need an eligible Echo device. If you want Emergency Assist to detect the sound of smoke alarms or carbon monoxide alarms, you will also need a separate smoke detector or carbon monoxide detector that is capable of emitting an audible alarm. To improve the performance of Emergency Assist, a supported Echo device should be in the same room or space and in close proximity to the source of the sound you want Alexa to detect, such as a smoke detector or carbon monoxide detector. Emergency Assist may not detect the sound of all smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors. Press the “test” button on your smoke or carbon monoxide detector until it emits an audible tone for at least 30 seconds. Echo devices are not capable of detecting the presence of smoke or carbon monoxide. You should not cover Echo devices with cloth or other objects because doing so could impair the device’s ability to detect the sounds you’ve selected.

7. How many Echo devices do I need in my home?

To best ensure that Alexa can detect selected sounds and is within voice range in an emergency, we recommend having at least one Echo device in each room or space in your home. To best ensure that Alexa detects selected sounds in your home, place your Echo devices close to the smoke or carbon monoxide detector that you want to monitor.

8. Is Alexa Emergency Assist a professional monitoring service?

No, Emergency Assist is not a professional monitoring service. If an alarm is detected Alexa will send a Smart Alert to your phone. Smart Alerts are provided for informational purposes only and if you get an alert, you should listen to it and make an independent judgment whether to contact Urgent Response.

Stay On Top of Bills With Alexa Bill Planner

Use your voice to link Alexa Bill Planner to your utility providers.

To link Alexa to a utility account say:

  • “Link my electric bill.”
  • “Link my water bill.”

If your utility provider allows access, follow Alexa’s directions to link your account. Have information ready to confirm that you own the utility account, such as:

  • Your account number for the biller
  • Your home address
  • Your email address

To use Bill Planner, say:

  • “When is my water bill due?”
  • “How much do I owe on my cable bill?”
  • “Is my electricity bill higher than it was last month?”
  • “What are my notifications?”

Tip: Bill Manager notifications are turned on when you link an account. If you don’t get notifications of upcoming bills, use the Alexa app on your phone. Go to Settings > Notifications > Skills, and turn on Bill Planner.

Syncing Issues with Books Read by Alexa with Kindle Assistive Reader

Kindle book doesn’t sync to the furthest page when Alexa begins reading.

Note: Kindle Assistive Reader isn’t available on Alexa+.

Alexa starts reading from the most recent page read on any device. To help set context, Alexa may start reading from the previous paragraph from your most recent page.

Try these troubleshooting steps if the Kindle Assistive Reader isn’t starting from the place you last read across any device:

  1. Open the book on the Amazon device or Kindle reading app where you were last reading.
  2. Confirm that the device has internet connectivity, and then open the book you were reading manually to the furthest page read.
  3. Select the Menu icon [Image: three dots icon] and sync the book manually to the furthest page read.
  4. Once the sync is complete, ask Alexa to play your Kindle book. Reading picks up from that location.
  • Update Your Sync Settings for Kindle

Test Urgent Response Using Alexa Emergency Assist

You can make test calls from a compatible Echo device to make sure Urgent Response calling is working correctly.

To make a test call on your compatible Echo device or through the Alexa App, say or type “Alexa, test urgent response.” Test calls are answered by an automated system.

Important: If you have a real emergency, say or type “Call for help.”

  • Call Urgent Response with Alexa Emergency Assist

Turn Alexa Communication Enhanced Features On or Off

Turn on the Enhanced Features setting to use Alexa Communication features like Group Calling, Group Drop In, Reactions, and AR Effects.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select More, then select Settings.
  3. Go to Alexa Preferences, then select Communication.
  4. Select Enhanced Features.
  5. Turn Enabled on or off.

Turn Alexa Emergency Assist Smart Alerts On or Off

Get notified when danger is detected in your home.

Alexa can detect the sound of smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms. If these sounds are detected, Alexa can ask if you want to call Urgent Response.

To set up Smart Alerts:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open .
  3. Select Alexa Emergency Assist.
  4. Select the Settings icon, then select Smart Alerts.
  5. Turn Smoke & CO Alarm Sounds on or off.

Turn Alexa Phone Notifications On or Off

To turn Alexa phone notifications on or off, use the Alexa app.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Select Notifications.
  4. Select Reminders on this device.
  5. Toggle Notifications on or off.

Turn Alexa Skills Notifications On or Off

Turn skills notifications on or off in the Alexa app. Not all skills have notifications.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More .
  3. Select the Alexa+ Store.
  4. Select the gear icon in the top right of the Alexa+ Store.
  5. Select Original Alexa Skills under Quick Links.
  6. Select Manage Permissions.
  7. Turn notifications on or off.

Turn Alexa Skills On or Off

Turn Alexa skills on or off with your voice or in the Alexa app. You can also turn themes on or off.

To turn Alexa skills on or off:

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  2. Open More .

  3. Select Alexa+ Store.

  4. Search for the Alexa skill you want to turn on or off. You can also search for Alexa themes you want to turn on or off.

  5. Select Enable Skill or Disable Skill.

    Note: You can also view your currently enabled skills by selecting the gear icon in the top right of the Alexa+ Store, then selecting Original Alexa Skills under Quick Links.

You can also turn skills on or off using your voice. Say something like:

  • “Enable [skill name].”
  • “Disable [skill name].”

Visit the skill page or theme page for the skill that you’re trying to turn on or off for more help.

Note: Child Directed Themes are only available to customers with an Amazon Kids+ subscription. Only kids with voice ID or an Amazon Kids enabled device can use this feature. Child Directed Themes can only be turned on or off by voice.

  • Create an Alexa Voice ID for Your Child
  • Turn Amazon Kids on Alexa On or Off Using the Alexa App

Turn Alexa Voice Purchasing On or Off

To turn Voice Purchasing on or off for your account, use the Alexa app.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Select Account Settings.
  4. Select Voice Purchasing.
  5. Turn Voice Purchasing on or off.

Note: You can limit purchasing so that only recognized Amazon Family members can place orders with Alexa.

  • Manage an Alexa Voice ID for Purchases with Alexa

Turn Amazon Kids on Alexa On or Off Using the Alexa App

Use the Alexa app to set up and manage Amazon Kids on compatible Echo devices.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select Echo & Alexa, then your device.
  4. Select the settings icon, then Amazon Kids.
  5. Turn Amazon Kids on or off.
  6. After turning on Amazon Kids, follow the on-screen prompts to create a profile or select an existing profile. You will be asked to provide parental consent.

Turn Amazon Kids on Alexa On or Off Using Your Echo Device with a Screen

Go to settings on your device to set up and manage Amazon Kids on compatible Echo devices.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Privacy & Permissions.
  3. Select Amazon Kids, and toggle on or off.
  4. After turning on Amazon Kids, follow the on-screen prompts to create a profile or select an existing profile. You will be asked to provide parental consent.

Turn Explicit Filtering On or Off in the Alexa App

You can use the Alexa app to turn explicit filtering for songs on or off.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings.
  3. Select Music & Podcasts, and then Explicit Language Filter.
  4. Switch the feature on or off.

Note: Some music services do not support explicit filtering. If the music service doesn’t launch, turn off the explicit filter and try again.

Turn Follow Up Mode On or Off

You can turn Follow-Up Mode on or off by voice, through your device settings, or in the Alexa app.

To turn Follow-Up Mode on or off, say:

  • “Turn on Follow-Up Mode.”
  • “Turn off Follow-Up Mode.”

To turn Follow-Up Mode on or off from your Echo Show:

  1. Select Settings.
  2. Select Alexa and then Follow-Up Mode.
  3. Turn Follow-Up Mode on or off.

To turn Follow-Up Mode on or off from the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa App .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select your device.
  4. Select Device Settings .
  5. Scroll down and select Follow-Up Mode.
  6. Turn Follow-Up Mode on or off.

To be able to interrupt without using the wake word on your compatible Echo Show, make sure:

  • The camera shutter is open.
  • The device’s camera and microphone on/off button is turned off.
  • The device mute button is off.
  • You’re in frame of the device’s camera and facing the screen.

Note: Follow-Up Mode isn’t available during media playback and calling.

  • What is Follow Up Mode?
  • Turn Your Echo Device’s Microphones On or Off

Turn Off an Alexa In-Skill Subscription

Use the Alexa app to turn off in-skill subscriptions. You can choose between two options: Turn off Autorenew or End Subscription.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More .
  3. Select Alexa+ Store.
  4. Select the gear icon in the top right corner.
  5. Select Original Alexa Skills under Quick Links.
  6. Select the skill with the subscription.
  7. Select Manage Subscriptions.
  8. If prompted, sign in to your Amazon account.
  9. Turn off Autorenew or select End Subscription.

Turn Off Communications for Specific Alexa Devices

Use the Alexa app to deactivate Communications on a specific device.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select Echo & Alexa.
  4. Select your device.
  5. Select Communications.
  6. Turn off Communications.
    • Turn off Announcements to stop broadcast messages to your device.
    • Turn off Drop In to stop household members and contacts from connecting to your device.

Disabling Communications turns off all communication options on your device.

  • Green Light Won’t Turn Off on Your Echo Device
  • Yellow Light Won’t Turn Off on Your Echo Device
  • Turn Drop In On or Off for Your Device

Turn On Captioning on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

You can use Closed Captioning, Call Captioning, or Alexa Captioning on your Echo Device with a Screen when available. Just say, “Turn on all captions.”

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

To turn on captions on your Alexa App or Echo devices with a screen:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Accessibility.
  3. Select Captioning.
  4. Check the boxes for the captioning settings you want to turn on:
    • All Captioning: Turns on all captioning options
    • Alexa Captioning: Turns on captioning for Alexa’s responses
    • Closed Captioning: Tuns on captioning for video playback
    • Call Captioning: Turns on captioning for Alexa calls and Drop Ins
    • Alexa Captioning: Turns on captioning for Alexa’s responses

To manage your Captioning preferences including font style and size:

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Accessibility.
  3. Select Captioning.
  4. Select Captioning Preferences.
  5. Manage your preferences.

Note:

  • Not all of Alexa’s responses support Alexa Captioning.

  • If you turn on both Alexa Captioning and Closed Captioning, only Closed Captioning appears when watching videos.

  • What Hearing Accessibility Options are Available for Echo Devices?

Turn On Featured or Shared Alexa Routines

Enable featured routines built by Amazon, or routines shared by others, using the Alexa app.

Use your mobile device to turn on a featured or shared routine. Scan the QR code or follow the links from texts, social media, or on the web, and then follow the steps in the app.

  1. Make sure that you have the Alexa app installed on your mobile device.

  2. Select the link or scan the QR code for the routine.

  3. Look for options in yellow text, which show that you need to make a selection to complete the setup. Select your device or follow the prompts as needed.

  4. Select Enable or Save to save and turn on the routine.

    Note: Some options for actions your devices can’t perform, or devices you don’t own, will be in yellow text. To turn on a routine, at least one action in the routine has to be correctly set up. If you see an inappropriate routine, Contact Us.

Turn On Gestures for Your Echo Show

Manage Gestures through Settings on your Echo Show.

Gestures allow you to use your hand to dismiss timers on Echo Show 8 (2nd Generation) and Echo Show 10 (3rd Generation) devices.

To activate Gestures:

  1. Swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  2. Select Gestures.
  3. Turn on Dismiss timers and alarms.
  • Gestures Aren’t Working

Turn On Hearing Accessibility Settings on Echo Devices with a Screen

Use the device settings to turn on accessibility options for hearing impairments.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings .
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings .
  2. Select Accessibility.
  3. Turn on the available features.
  • What Hearing Accessibility Options Are Available for Echo Devices?

Turn on the Kindle Assistive Reader to access your list of supported Kindle books.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open .
  3. Select Settings .
  4. Select Accessibility.
  5. Select Kindle Assistive Reader.

Turn On or Off Screen Magnifier on Your Echo Devices with a Screen

Use on-screen settings to turn on or off the Screen Magnifier.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

  1. Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.

Urgent Response FAQs

1. How do I call Urgent Response?

Once you’ve purchased your Emergency Assist subscription, you or others in your household can say “Alexa, call for help” to a compatible Echo device or the Alexa App to be connected to a trained Urgent Response agent. If you are away from home and receive a Smart Alert you can tap the “Call Urgent Response” button in the notification and be connected via your mobile phone. Note: Urgent Response calling will not work during power outages or if you’re experiencing internet connectivity issues, but you can still reach Urgent Response via the Alexa app on your mobile phone provided you have cellular connectivity with data.

2. Why can’t I just ask Alexa to dial 911 in case of emergency?

Urgent Response is not a 911 service, and by default, Alexa does not support calling to 911. AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile customers can link their mobile number to Alexa to make and receive hands-free calls over Wi-Fi on an Alexa-enabled device, like the Echo Dot or the Echo Show 15. To get started, you’ll first need to link your mobile phone number to your Alexa account. To do this, go to More > Settings > Communication in the Alexa app. Under Accounts, select your mobile carrier and follow the instructions to link your account. Once connected, you’ll be able to quickly make and receive calls from anyone in your contacts list, just like you would on your phone. Note: Any incoming calls to this mobile phone number will also ring on the Echo devices in your home.

3. What do I need to access Urgent Response?

To use Urgent Response, you must have an active Alexa Emergency Assist subscription, a valid emergency address, a verified phone number associated with your Alexa account, and a supported Echo device with Alexa Communications turned on. Note: Alexa Emergency Assist is only available in the 50 U.S. States.

4. Can I call Urgent Response with any Alexa-enabled device?

No. You can only call Urgent Response from an Echo smart speaker, smart display (such as an Echo Dot or Echo Show), or Alexa App with Alexa Communications turned on. You should make a test call to Urgent Response from each of your devices to confirm that that device is supported.

5. How can I test Urgent Response?

To test Urgent Response, go to your Echo device and say “Alexa, test the emergency helpline”. Stay on the line until you hear the message that you have successfully tested the helpline. To test Urgent Response from your mobile phone, open the Alexa app and say or type “Alexa, test the emergency helpline”.

6. What happens in the event of an emergency call? Who is dispatched?

When you say, “Alexa, call for help,” Alexa will connect you with Urgent Response. Trained response agents can then request dispatch from police, the fire department, or an ambulance on your behalf—based on the information you provide during the call. Unless you specify an alternate address, help will be sent to the emergency address you provided during setup by default. If you call Urgent Response from the Alexa App and have enabled location sharing, then Alexa will share your last known location with the agent. Calls to Urgent Response may be recorded.

7. What information is shared with the Urgent Response provider?

In addition to your emergency address, we also share the name, phone number, and Echo device name that you registered with the Alexa profile from which you placed the call, along with any Critical Information (e.g., medical conditions, home access information, etc.) you choose to provide. If you call Urgent Response from the Alexa app, we will also share your last known location if you have granted the Alexa App permission to access location data from your mobile device. If an emergency dispatch is requested, the Urgent Response agent may share any of this information with your local police, fire, or ambulance responder so they can be prepared when they reach you.

8. Are emergency services automatically dispatched if someone in my home calls Urgent Response?

No. Someone must speak with an Urgent Response agent and describe the nature of their emergency so that they can pass those details on to emergency dispatchers. If the call is disconnected or the caller hangs up without speaking to the agent, the agent may attempt to call them back on their Echo device. If the call is not answered, the agent will call your Emergency Contacts (up to 3) and request permission to dispatch.

9. What if I call Urgent Response by accident or request help in a non-emergency situation?

If you or someone in your household accidentally calls Urgent Response, please inform the agent that the call was placed by mistake. If you are away from home, you should review any Smart Alerts prior to calling Urgent Response. You can also Drop In on your Echo device from the Alexa app to check on your home. If you would like to prevent Urgent Response calls from a specific device, you should disable Alexa Communication for that device via Devices > Echo & Alexa > [Your Device Name] > Communications in the Alexa app. Some local emergency responders assess fines, penalties, or fees for false, excessive, or other misuse of emergency services. You are responsible for any such fines, penalties, or fees resulting from your use of Urgent Response.

10. What if my emergency address is incorrect?

It is important to keep your emergency address up-to-date. When you call, the Urgent Response agent will confirm your address before requesting dispatch. However, in some circumstances (e.g., if the call drops, or if you cannot be understood) the agent may be unable to verbally verify your address, so the address you provided during sign-up may be used as part of your emergency request. You can update your emergency address from the Emergency Assist dashboard in the Alexa app.

11. Can I call Urgent Response if I’m away from home?

Yes. You can call Urgent Response whether you are at or away from home. If you are away from home and need help, simply open the Alexa app and say or type “Alexa, call for help” and Alexa will call Urgent Response.

12. Will the Urgent Response agent know where I am if I’m away from home?

If you call Urgent Response from your mobile device, Alexa will share your last known location with the agent. To ensure that Alexa can share your location, you must enable Location Services in the Alexa app.

13. Is there a limit to the number of times customers can call Urgent Response?

No. As an Emergency Assist customer, you can call Urgent Response any time you need emergency assistance.

14. Does Urgent Response work on Echo devices that are in Amazon Kids mode?

Yes. To avoid placing emergency calls by mistake, please ensure other members of your household know that you’ve enabled Urgent Response. If you’d like to exclude a particular device from accessing Urgent Response, you can disable Communications for that device within the Alexa app. If you would like to prevent Urgent Response calls from a specific device, you should disable Alexa Communication for that device via Devices > Echo & Alexa > [Your Device Name] > Communications in the Alexa app. This will disable all Alexa Communications capabilities for the selected device.

15. Will Alexa Emergency Assist work if the power or internet are out?

No. Emergency Assist is a cloud service. Echo devices must be plugged into an adequate power supply and have a reliable connection to the internet to work. Your power and internet connection may be disrupted during a weather-related emergency and Emergency Assist will not work if that happens, even if briefly. You can still reach Urgent Response via the Alexa app on your mobile phone if it is connected to the internet. If your device experiences a power interruption, after power resumes, check the device and its connections to ensure the device works as intended.

16. What happens if my Echo device is in Do-Not-Disturb mode?

If your device is in Do-Not-Disturb mode, you can place a call to Urgent Response. If the call is disconnected or the agent is unable to hear you, they will call you back on your device. An incoming call from Urgent Response will override the Do-Not-Disturb setting.

Welcome to Amazon Sidewalk

Amazon Sidewalk is a community network that can help devices like Amazon Echo devices, Ring Security Cams, outdoor lights, motion sensors, and Tile trackers work better at home and beyond the front door. Sidewalk can unlock unique benefits for your device, support other Sidewalk devices in your community, and even locate pets or lost items.

The benefits of Amazon Sidewalk

Amazon Sidewalk creates a low-bandwidth network with the help of Sidewalk Bridge devices including select Echo and Ring devices. These Bridge devices share a small portion of your internet bandwidth which is pooled together to provide these services to you and your neighbors. And when more neighbors participate, the network becomes even stronger.

Find lost items

Sidewalk is designed to work with tracker devices, like Tile, to help find valuables outside your home.

Designed to protect your privacy

Sidewalk is designed with multiple layers of privacy and security.

It’s all on your own terms

Don’t think you need Amazon Sidewalk? No worries. You can update this anytime in the Alexa app (under Account Settings) or Ring app (in Control Center).

Get started as a Sidewalk device developer

Device manufacturers interested in creating devices that work with Amazon Sidewalk can view more information on the Sidewalk Developer Console. Learn more about creating devices that work with Sidewalk at Sidewalk (developer.amazon.com).

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Amazon Sidewalk? Amazon Sidewalk is a community network that helps devices work better. Operated by Amazon at no charge to customers, Sidewalk can help simplify new device setup, extend the low-bandwidth working range of devices, help find lost items, and help devices stay online even if they are outside the range of their home wifi.

Why should I participate in Amazon Sidewalk? Amazon Sidewalk helps your devices get connected and stay connected. For example, if your Echo device loses its wifi connection, Sidewalk can simplify reconnecting to your router. For select Ring devices, you can continue to receive motion alerts from your Ring Security Cams and customer support can still troubleshoot problems even if your devices lose their wifi connection. Sidewalk can also extend the working range for your Sidewalk-enabled devices, such as Ring smart lights, pet locators or smart locks, so they can stay connected and continue to work over longer distances. Amazon does not charge any fees to join Sidewalk.

What are Sidewalk Bridges, and which devices are able to become Sidewalk Bridges? Sidewalk Bridges are devices that provide connections to Amazon Sidewalk. Today, Sidewalk Bridges include many Echo devices and select Ring devices. Sidewalk Bridges include, but are not limited to: Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro, Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Plus, Ring Wired Doorbell Pro (Video Doorbell Pro 2), Ring Wired Doorbell Plus (Video Doorbell Pro), Ring Alarm Pro Base Station, Ring Floodlight Cam, Ring Spotlight Cam Wired, Echo (3rd gen and newer), Echo Dot (2nd gen and newer, including Kids edition), Echo Dot with Clock (3rd gen and newer), Echo Pop, Echo Plus (all generations), Echo Show (2nd gen), Echo Show 5, 8, 10, 15, 21 (all generations, including Kids edition), Echo Hub, Echo Spot (all generations), Echo Studio, Echo Input, Echo Flex.

How do I turn Amazon Sidewalk off? Customers can turn Sidewalk on or off at any time from Control Center in the Ring app or Account Settings in the Alexa app. This setting will apply to all applicable Echo and Ring devices linked to the customer’s account.

How will Amazon Sidewalk impact my personal wireless bandwidth and data usage? The maximum bandwidth of a Sidewalk Bridge to the Sidewalk server is 80Kbps, which is about 1/40th of the bandwidth used to stream a typical high definition video. Today, when you share your Bridge’s connection with Sidewalk, total monthly data used by Sidewalk, per account, is capped at 500MB, which is equivalent to streaming about 10 minutes of high definition video.

If I turn off Amazon Sidewalk, will my Sidewalk Bridges still work? Yes. All of your Sidewalk Bridges will continue to have their original functionality even if you decide to turn off Amazon Sidewalk. However, turning it off means missing out on Sidewalk’s connectivity and location related benefits. You also will no longer contribute your internet bandwidth to support community extended coverage benefits such as locating pets and valuables with Sidewalk-enabled devices.

What happens if there are not a lot of Bridges in my neighborhood? Amazon Sidewalk coverage may vary by location based on the number of participating Bridges in a location. The more Sidewalk Bridge customers who participate, the better the network becomes.

How does Amazon Sidewalk protect customer information? Preserving customer privacy and security is foundational to how we’ve built Amazon Sidewalk. Sidewalk is designed with multiple layers of privacy and security to secure data traveling on Sidewalk and to keep customers safe and in control. For example, Sidewalk Bridge owners do not receive any information about devices owned by others connected to Sidewalk. Learn more here.

How does Amazon Sidewalk work? Customers with a Sidewalk Bridge (today, many Echo devices, Ring Floodlight Cams and Ring Spotlight Cams) can contribute a small portion of their internet bandwidth, which is pooled together to create a community network that benefits all Sidewalk-enabled devices in a community. Amazon Sidewalk uses Bluetooth, the 900 MHz spectrum and other frequencies to extend coverage and provide these benefits.

Will I know what other Sidewalk-enabled devices are connected to my Bridge? Preserving customer privacy and security is foundational to how we’ve built Amazon Sidewalk. Information transferred over Sidewalk Bridges is encrypted and Bridge customers are not able to see that Sidewalk-enabled devices are connected to their Bridge. Customers who own Sidewalk-enabled devices will know they are connected to Sidewalk but will not be able to identify which Bridge they are connected to. For more information, visit our whitepaper here.

What does it mean to share the location of my Sidewalk Bridge? Sharing your Bridge’s approximate location will help to provide others with benefits like helping them locate their pet. Neighbors with Sidewalk-enabled devices won’t be able to see the exact street address of your Sidewalk Bridge. They will only see an approximate location. This setting will apply to all of your Sidewalk Bridges.

What is a Sidewalk-enabled device? Sidewalk-enabled devices are devices that connect to Sidewalk Bridges to access Amazon Sidewalk. Sidewalk-enabled devices will support a range of experiences from helping find pets or valuables, to smart security and lighting, to diagnostics for appliances and tools. We are working with device manufacturers on new low-bandwidth devices that can run on or benefit from Sidewalk, with no recurring fees to access Sidewalk. Sidewalk-enabled devices include Sidewalk Bridges because they can benefit from connecting to other Sidewalk Bridges too.

What types of devices can connect to Amazon Sidewalk? Only devices authorized by Amazon to use Sidewalk’s low-bandwidth connections are allowed to connect to Amazon Sidewalk.

Is Amazon Sidewalk a replacement for a home wifi network? No. Sidewalk Bridges require wifi access for normal operation. When Sidewalk is on, your Bridge can share a low-bandwidth connection with Sidewalk-enabled devices, like sensors and smart lights that are installed in locations around and outside your home where wifi may not be available. Amazon Sidewalk does not support high-bandwidth connections like a wifi or cellular network would, so you would still use those connections for streaming movies, posting on social media or sending email.

How does Sidewalk help in finding Tile trackers?

Tile uses Bluetooth technology to locate lost items, and with Sidewalk, your Bridge is able to extend Tile’s network coverage even further to help you locate your misplaced keys, wallets, and other items. Alexa securely obtains the last known location of the item either from the Tile service or from a nearby Sidewalk Bridge.

When a Tile is near a Sidewalk Bridge associated with your Alexa account, Alexa will tell you the name of that Bridge, making the Tile easier to find even if you don’t have your mobile phone nearby. Sidewalk also extends the Tile network beyond your home by using other Sidewalk Bridges in your neighborhood that participate in Sidewalk’s Community Finding feature.

What is the Community Finding feature in Sidewalk?

Community Finding helps others find important items connected to Sidewalk by sharing the approximate location of the Sidewalk Bridge that the compatible Sidewalk-enabled device is close to.

Do you need to turn on Sidewalk for the in-home finding experience?

No. The in-home finding experience is not impacted by the Sidewalk setting and works out of the box with your Sidewalk Bridges. The Sidewalk setting controls the sharing of your Internet bandwidth with others for them to receive Sidewalk benefits. If you also use the Tile app to find your Tile, the ‘Device address’ permission in your Tile skill must be enabled to ensure the location is synced in your Tile app. To learn more about Amazon’s Find My feature, from the Alexa app see Devices > Trackers > Settings > About Find My

Do I need to share my bandwidth through Sidewalk to get the benefits from neighbors for finding my Tile trackers?

No. You do not need to enable Sidewalk and Community Finding to get the benefits of finding your own Tile devices. However, the value of the network grows for everyone as more participate.

What Sidewalk Bridges support Community Finding with Tile?

All Echo devices that are Sidewalk Bridges support this feature.

What does Amazon charge for use of the network? Amazon does not charge any fees to join Amazon Sidewalk, which uses a small portion of bandwidth from a Sidewalk Bridge’s existing internet service. Standard data rates from internet providers may apply.

What is Sidewalk Developer Service (SDS)? SDS is a collection of approved silicon chipsets along with purchasable development boards, device software development kits (SDKs), device provisioning tools, technical documentation, and a cloud integration (see Amazon Sidewalk Integration for AWS IoT at Features (aws.amazon.com)). Collectively, these tools help device manufacturers develop, and easily launch, devices that are Sidewalk-enabled.

How do manufacturers start using SDS, to begin building Sidewalk-enabled devices? To get started building a proof-of-concept Sidewalk-enabled device, first review the Quick Start Guide on the FSDS Console (Sidewalk (developer.amazon.com)) then review technical documentation, decide which approved development board and Sidewalk Bridge to purchase, and then download an SDK.

Are you a device manufacturer, ready to get started, but have more questions?

Contact our technical team here to request more information at Amazon Sidewalk (build.amazonalexadev.com).

Where is Amazon Sidewalk available? Sidewalk is currently only available in the US, but will be available in Canada and Mexico beginning February 26, 2026.

What Are Alexa Profiles?

Alexa Profiles gives each person in your home their own Alexa experience.

You can enroll your Amazon Profile in Alexa as an Alexa Profile. Alexa Profiles gives each person in your home their own individual Alexa experience. You can create an Alexa Profile for you and your family members when setting up your device.

Alexa Profiles can be created from your device after setup. Select an existing Amazon Profile on your Amazon Account or create a new Amazon Profile. Existing Amazon Profiles include profiles enrolled in other programs, like Prime Video.

Important: To receive individualized Alexa experiences on your devices, you must create your Alexa Profiles on the same Alexa Account. Profiles from other Amazon Accounts like Amazon Family won’t have individualized experiences on your devices.

To create an Alexa Profile in the Alexa app, sign in to the Alexa app with the account credentials used to register your Alexa-enabled device. Once signed in, follow the on-screen instructions. If you are an adult, you can also create profiles for kids.

Voice ID

You can create an Alexa voice ID for your Alexa Profile. With an Alexa voice ID, you’ll get personal content and features when Alexa recognizes your voice. To create an Alexa voice ID, go to Create an Alexa Voice ID. You can also create a voice ID for kids in the Alexa app by going to Settings, and then Amazon Kids.

Visual ID

You can create a visual ID for your Alexa Profile. A visual ID personalizes your experience on compatible Echo Show devices. When Alexa recognizes you, you’ll see content and recommendations just for you on your Echo Show device. To create a visual ID, go to Enroll in Visual ID on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

Phone ID

You can turn on phone ID from your Alexa profile. Phone ID helps Alexa recognize you when you’re near an eligible Echo device to deliver personalized experiences. Phone ID also displays personalized content on compatible Echo Show devices.

To turn Phone ID on or off, go to Turn Phone ID On or Off.

What Can You Do with Alexa Routines?

Routines are shortcuts for Alexa, saving you time by grouping together actions so you don’t have to ask for each one individually.

You can have up to 200 routines on your account at a time. For example, say “Start my day” to have Alexa turn on your compatible smart lights and tell you the weather forecast.

You can kick off Routines in several ways including voice commands like saying “Good morning,” a specific time of day, sound detection, like the sound of a dog barking or a person snoring, Presence Detection, or when an alarm goes off.

You can also start a routine using your Visual ID or a member of your household’s Visual ID, through Personal Presence Detection.

Routines can contain one or multiple actions, such as:

  • Start an Alexa skill
  • Get briefings or traffic reports from Alexa
  • Make a call
  • Turn on compatible Fire TV devices
  • Arm connected home security systems
  • Play music
  • Adjust dimmable lights
  • Turn on or off smart home devices
  • Turn on compatible smart home devices based on your home’s indoor temperature (with Echo Dot 5th Generation and Echo Pop)

What Do I Need to Place Orders with Alexa?

Before placing orders with Alexa, make sure that you meet these requirements.

Note: Visit About Alexa for shopping for more information about shopping with Alexa on the Amazon website and mobile app.

Alexa uses the default shipping address and payment settings in Your Account.

To place orders, you need:

  • a valid payment method.
  • an Amazon account.
  • a device with access to Alexa.

Tip: Verify your purchasing settings in the Alexa app.

What Hearing Accessibility Options are Available for Echo Devices with a Screen?

Customize your Echo devices with hearing accessibility features.

  • Closed Captioning converts the audio content of a video broadcast into text. You can customize text on supported video content.
  • Alexa Captions displays captions for Alexa’s responses.
  • Real Time Text (RTT) creates a live chat feed during an Alexa call or Drop In on Echo Show. You can send text messages that appear on all devices during the call or Drop In.
  • Call Captioning shows real-time captions for Alexa calls on supported Alexa devices. Call Captioning is available in English, Spanish, French, and Portuguese.
  • Preferred speaking Rate slows down or speeds up Alexa’s reading speed.

Note: Call Captioning supports calls in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Brazil.

  • Accessibility for Alexa
  • Turn On Hearing Accessibility Settings on Echo Devices with a Screen

What Is Alexa Automatic Grouping?

Automatic grouping allows Alexa to add your connected smart devices to groups based on their names or how you typically use them together. This makes it easier to control multiple devices at once.

Automatic grouping is turned on by default. When turned on, Alexa proactively adds devices to groups so you can manage them together.

For example, if you have a smart light and a smart plug in the same room, Alexa may group them together so you can control them with a single command.

You can manage your smart home device status and usage history at any time. To learn more, go to Alexa Privacy Settings.

  • Set Up Automatic Grouping for Your Smart Devices

What Is Alexa Calling and Messaging?

Use the Alexa Calling and Messaging feature to make calls and send messages between supported Echo devices and the Alexa app.

With Alexa Communication, you can:

  • Make calls to Alexa contacts.
  • Make calls to groups of Alexa contacts.
  • Make calls to mobile and landline numbers (in the U.S., U.K., Canada, and Mexico) at no additional cost.
  • Send Alexa-to-Alexa messages from the Alexa app on a compatible mobile device.

What is Alexa Emergency Assist?

Alexa Emergency Assist is a subscription service that provides an extra level of protection to keep your family safe.

Alexa Emergency Assist is a subscription service that helps keep you and your family safe with hands-free access to a dedicated Urgent Response agent 24/7. If an emergency happens in your home, Emergency Assist keeps everyone in your family network informed.

Your subscription includes:

  • 24/7 Urgent Response: Urgent Response agents are available 24/7, 365 days a year if you need help from police, fire, or ambulance.
  • Smart Alerts: Alexa can detect smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and notifies you when you’re away from home.
  • Emergency Contacts: Add up to 25 Emergency Contacts to be automatically notified when a call is placed to the emergency helpline and when the call ends.
  • Critical Information: Provide critical information like medical conditions, property gate codes, and details about pets in the home, so first responders will be prepared when they arrive.

To request help in an emergency, say “Call for help.” Alexa will connect you with a dedicated agent who can request dispatch of emergency services.

Important: By default, Alexa does not support calling to emergency services numbers (for example, “911”).

Alexa Emergency Assist does not support Echo on-the-go devices.

  • Set Up Alexa Emergency Assist
  • Test Urgent Response Using Alexa Emergency Assist

What Is Amazon Kids+ on Alexa?

Amazon Kids+ on Alexa lets you create a personalized experience for your kids and choose what content they access on their device.

With Kids+ on Alexa, your kids can:

  • Listen to music.
  • Call and message your household and approved contacts.
  • Use Drop In and Announcements on household devices.
  • Get kid-friendly answers to questions. Alexa can answer questions about spelling, math, and more.
  • Ask for kid-friendly jokes, songs, stories, fun facts, greetings, and more.
  • Play games.

Note: If you’ve enabled features that allow calls to emergency numbers, your child may also place emergency calls. For instance, if you’ve linked your mobile phone service with Alexa, your child may call 911 through that phone service.

To set daily time limits, monitor activity, share content, and manage your child’s experience, use the Parent Dashboard.

What Is an Alexa Emergency Contact?

Alexa attempts to call and text your emergency contact when you or someone in your house says, “Alexa, call for help.”

After you set up Alexa Communications, you can assign a contact as an emergency contact in the Alexa app. After you select a contact, a message is sent to that number informing the recipient they’ve been selected as your emergency contact.

Alexa attempts to call and text your emergency contact when you use any of the following phrases:

  • “Call for help.”
  • “Call my emergency contact.”
  • “Call my contact for help.”
  • “Call my help contact.”
  • “Help.”
  • “I need help.”

If your emergency contact misses your call, your contact can use the Alexa app to call your Echo device.

Note:

  • This service isn’t a substitute for emergency response services or 911.
  • If anyone from your household asks Alexa to call for help (including from devices in Amazon Kids mode), Alexa attempts to call and message your emergency contact.
  • If your Echo device isn’t connected to Wi-Fi or the phone number is incorrect, Alexa is unable to call or text your emergency contact.
  • If your emergency contact opts out from receiving messages, or they have a landline number that doesn’t support SMS, Alexa is unable to text them.
  • Alexa calling doesn’t support calls to the following types of numbers:
    • Emergency service numbers (for example “911”)
    • Premium-rate numbers (for example “1-900” numbers, or toll numbers)
    • Three-digit numbers / abbreviated dial codes (for example “211”)
    • Dial-by-letter numbers (for example “1-800-FLOWERS”)
    • Special characters or extension numbers (for example “4255551234;,” or “4255551234,567”)
  • Set Up Calling and Messaging

  • Remove Your Alexa Emergency Contact

What Is Audio Guest Casting with Alexa?

Guests can play audio on your supported Echo devices when they connect to your Wi-Fi network.

Guest Casting lets anyone on your Wi-Fi network play audio from a supported music service to your Echo devices. When it is on, anyone connected to your Wi-Fi network will be able to see your device names and discover these devices. To disable Guest Casting, go to Turn Guest Casting On or Off.

When Guest Casting is on, your device name is visible to others on your Wi-Fi network. To learn how to change your device name, go to Change Your Echo Device’s Name.

Guest Casting works with newer Echo devices. To see which device you have, go to Which Echo Device Do I Have?.

How Guest Casting Works

Guest Casting lets anyone with access to your Wi-Fi network play audio from their supported music service app to your Alexa devices. You do not need to link a music service account in your Alexa app to use Guest Casting.

Casting music does not include full Alexa voice features. For example, if you pause the music that you cast, you won’t be able to tell Alexa to restart it by voice.

Link a Supported Music Service

For voice control, hands-free playback, and the ability to move music between devices, link your music service account in the Alexa app. To learn more, go to Link Music Streaming Services to Alexa.

What is News and Flash Briefing for Alexa?

Listen to news broadcasts from select news providers.

Use Alexa to listen to news broadcasts from a variety of news providers. For news from a specific provider, say:

  • “Play the news from [provider].”

Note: Most skills are developed by third-party developers. Individual skill developers determine whether to offer their skill as a news skill.

To listen to extensive news broadcasts from your primary News Channel, or a specific news provider, say:

  • “Play the news.”
  • “What’s the news?”

To hear short updates and top stories from multiple sources in a Flash Briefing, say:

  • “Play my Flash Briefing.”

Alexa helps you select your preferred news providers when you ask Alexa to play the news or flash briefing for the first time.

A list of available news providers is available in the Alexa App.

What Is Personal Presence Detection with Alexa+?

Some Echo devices can detect presence in a room through your Visual ID profile.

Person Presence Detection is available on:

  • Echo Show 8 (2nd Generation and newer)
  • Echo Show 10
  • Echo Show 11 (2025 release)
  • Echo Show 15
  • Echo Show 21

Personal Presence Detection uses your Visual ID profile to start a personalized routine. When Alexa recognizes you or a member of your household with a Visual ID, the device starts a routine such as turning on the lights when you enter a room.

To create a Personal Presence Routine, go to Create a Personal Presence Routine with Alexa+.

What is Show and Tell for Alexa?

Show and Tell for Alexa lets you use your Echo Show’s camera to identify products you’re holding.

Show and Tell is an accessibility feature that identifies common pantry items and other objects. Just hold up a product in front of your Echo device with a screen and ask Alexa to identify it.

Alexa tells you what you’re holding and provides a brief description. To hear the tutorial and learn more about this feature say, “Help with Show and Tell.” The tutorial gives you product placement hints, sounds to expect, and camera tips. For more help with using Show and Tell, say “More help with Show and Tell.”

Show and Tell is available on all Echo devices with a screen.

  • Identify Products with Your Echo Devices with a Screen

What is Tap to Alexa?

Tap to Alexa lets you interact with Alexa using touch on Echo devices with a screen and Fire tablets.

When you turn on Tap to Alexa, a finger icon appears on the screen. Select this icon to open Tap to Alexa.

Tap to Alexa lets you interact with Alexa without speaking by touching the on-screen tiles. Select the “Ask Alexa” tile and type in a request using the on-screen keyboard.

Tap to Alexa is compatible with Switch Access on Fire tablets and supports Bluetooth switches.

  • Turn Tap to Alexa On or Off

What Is the Alexa+ Store?

The Alexa+ Store is a centralized location where you manage, discover, and engage with Alexa+ add-ons in one place.

Note: The Alexa+ Store is available in the latest version of the Alexa app in the U.S. only, with U.S. location and English language settings.

Use the Alexa+ Store in the Alexa app to:

  • Discover new add-ons from Amazon and developers.
  • Set up and manage your preferred services and add-ons.
  • Customize your Alexa+ add-ons.

Access the Alexa+ Store through the menu in your Alexa app.

To manage your add-ons and services, tap the gear icon to open the Manage page. Under My Experiences you can:

  • Manage account links and permissions for Alexa+ services.
  • Review and manage original Alexa skills through the Manage Original Skills option.

Note: Services and add-ons may vary by location and device. Some services may require extra subscriptions or purchases.

What Is Visual ID on Echo Show?

Visual ID lets Alexa recognize you and display personalized content on compatible Echo Show devices.

Visual ID is available on:

  • Echo Show 8 (2nd Generation or newer)
  • Echo Show 10 (3rd Generation)
  • Echo Show 11 (2025 release)
  • Echo Show 15
  • Echo Show 21

Visual ID uses on-device facial recognition to provide a personalized experience on your Echo Show. When Alexa recognizes you, the device shows content from your Alexa profile, such as your calendars and reminders, skills, or interests.

Other things to know:

  • Visual ID is an opt-in Alexa Profile feature. It isn’t on by default.

  • You can delete your Visual ID at any time on your device or in the Alexa app.

  • You can turn off Visual ID temporarily. Press the Microphones & Camera Enable/Disable button to turn off the camera and microphones.

  • Your household members can also enroll in Visual ID.

Your TV or Video Service Provider Doesn’t Work with Alexa

Alexa commands don’t work with your TV or video service provider or setup fails.

  • Check that you have the latest version of the Alexa app.

  • Make sure that you’ve completed setup for your service provider’s Alexa Video Skill. Some providers require additional authentication steps before you can connect with Alexa.

  • Make sure that you’re using compatible equipment from your TV or video service providers.

  • Check that your equipment is on the latest software or firmware version.

    Tip: The Dish TV Alexa Skill requires an Internet-connected Hopper satellite box on the latest software version.

  • Check that the device you use to access your TV or video service is on the same Wi-Fi network as your Alexa-enabled device.

  • Unlink your TV or video service provider and relink it in the Alexa app.

  • Download the Alexa App

Alexa Smart Home

Activate Your Home Security System with an Alexa Routine

Use your voice to turn on your Alexa-supported home security system when you leave the house.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Routines .
  3. Select Plus to create a routine.
  4. Select When this happens to set what starts the routine. This is the action or phrase that you want to turn on your security system.
  5. Select Add an action.
  6. Select Smart Home and then select your connected home security system.
  7. Select the armed mode so that the routine sets your system as armed.
  8. Select the arrow at the top of the screen to save the routine.

Note: A routine can only be set to arm your security system, not to disarm it.

Adding or Moving Devices in Map View

If you’d like to add new devices or change your devices’ location in Map View, try these tips.

  • To add or move devices, go to your floor plan settings. Go to How to Edit Map View for more information on this step.

  • To add groups, you can add the entire group to your floor plan.

  • To add your group, drag the square with the rounded corners from the bottom of your screen and place it on your floor plan.

  • To add individual devices from a group, tap the group icon and pin them to your floor plan.

  • To identify which device you’re trying to control, select your device and then select Test.

    • For lights, this test helps by turning the device on and off.

  • If you can’t remember the name of one of the devices that you already placed on the floor plan, select the device’s pin icon. The device pin icon shows the device’s name.

  • To make sure that you selected your device, press and hold it until it enlarges.

    • When you let go, it lands where the small blue dot is underneath it.

  • Some devices don’t work with Map View. These devices include:

    • Trackers, Ring car camera, printers, and others.

  • If you scanned multiple floors, you can place devices on another floor. Select the desired floor in the top-right corner of the map.
