Alexa Can’t Connect to My Smart Home Device Through Bluetooth

To set up Bluetooth smart home devices with Alexa, just power on your smart home device. Then say, “Discover devices.” If that doesn’t work, try these troubleshooting steps:

  • Make sure that your smart home device supports Bluetooth by checking the packaging and the device for a Bluetooth logo [Image: Bluetooth logo].
  • Make sure that your smart home device is compatible with Alexa by checking the manufacturer’s instructions or companion app.
  • Place your smart home device within 30 ft (9 m) of your Echo device.
  • Make sure that your Echo device software is up to date. Your Echo device software updates automatically.
    • You can manually check for updates by restarting your device, or by saying, “Check for updates.”
    • If you’re using an Echo device with a screen, swipe down from the top of the display and select Settings. Then go to Device Options and select Check for software updates.
  • For detailed steps specific to your device, open the Alexa app and go to Devices . Select the plus icon and then select Add Device. Select your brand or your device type, then follow the instructions in the app.
  • If you’re experiencing issues setting up your smart home device, make sure it’s in pairing mode. Pairing mode instructions are usually in the device manufacturer’s manual.

If you’re still having trouble connecting Bluetooth devices, reset your device.

  • Connect Zigbee Smart Home Devices to Alexa Using Your Echo with a Smart Home Hub
  • Alexa Gadgets & Echo Buttons

Alexa Gadget is Unresponsive

To resolve most issues with connectivity or setup, unplug the power adapter from your Echo device and then plug it back in.

  • Make sure that your Echo device is compatible with your Alexa Gadget. Reference the product detail page or manufacturer’s instructions for your Alexa Gadget.
  • Make sure that your Echo device and the Alexa app have the latest software version.
  • Confirm that your Alexa Gadget is listed under Connected Devices in the Alexa app. If you have an Echo device with a screen, confirm that your Alexa Gadget is listed in the Bluetooth section in Settings.
  • Make sure your Alexa Gadget is powered on.
  • If you’re using Alexa Skills, make sure the skill is enabled.
  • If the skill is unresponsive, disable and re-enable the skill.
  • Reach out to the manufacturer for further assistance.

Alexa Isn’t Controlling Smart Home Devices

Smart home devices aren’t responding to commands or are responding intermittently.

  • Check that your smart home device is on. If your device is battery operated, try inserting new batteries.
  • Make sure your Alexa device and the Alexa app have the latest software version.
  • If your smart home device uses a skill, try controlling your device with the manufacturer’s app.
    • If you can control your device with the manufacturer’s app, but not with Alexa, remove and then add the skill again in the Alexa app.
    • Otherwise, check your internet connection in the manufacturer’s app. If neither steps work, try resetting your Alexa device and smart home device.
  • If your device is next to your router, it may not work. Move your Alexa device at least 6 ft (2 m) away from your router.
  • Matter Wi-Fi devices must connect on the same 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network as your compatible matter controller (such as a compatible Echo device).
  • For Matter devices, make sure it’s within 30 ft (9 m) of your compatible Matter controller.
  • If your device has a Zigbee logo , make sure it’s within 30 ft (9 m) of your hub or another connected Zigbee smart home device.
  • If your device has a Bluetooth logo , make sure it’s within 30 ft (9 m) of your compatible Echo device.
  • If your connected home security system doesn’t arm in a routine:
    • Make sure that no monitored doors or windows are open.
    • Check that the system isn’t already in an armed mode.
  • Make sure that your smart home device is compatible with Alexa. Devices that have a “Works with Alexa” badge are certified to work with Alexa.

If these smart home troubleshooting steps don’t work, try resetting your Alexa device and smart home devices. To learn more about Alexa’s Matter support and compatible devices, go to Alexa Smart Home Connectivity.

For more help, try our Smart Home forum.

  • Alexa Device Software Versions

Alexa Isn’t Working with Your Amazon Smart Oven or Microwave

Voice commands aren’t working with your device.

  • Check the Wi-Fi icon on your microwave to confirm that it’s online.
  • Make sure that your Echo device and microwave are connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
  • Place your Echo device within hearing distance of your microwave. The minimum distance is 12” apart.
  • If you have an Amazon Family, check that you’re using the correct profile. Say, “Which profile is this?”

Checking Wi-Fi Connectivity on Smart Home Devices

Try these steps to check the internet connection for your Alexa-compatible device or fix connectivity issues.

Tip: For third-party devices that use Wi-Fi and aren’t Matter certified, set up your device in the manufacturer’s app before connecting to Alexa. With some devices, you can link your Alexa account and your third-party device account in the manufacturer’s app during setup. You can also connect Alexa by activating the related skill in the Alexa app as needed.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open Devices .
  3. Select your device.
  4. Select the gear in the top right.
  5. Under Wi-Fi Network, verify that the correct Wi-Fi network is visible.
  6. If the Wi-Fi network listed is incorrect, select Change and follow the on-screen instructions.
    1. You can only change the Wi-Fi network settings in the Alexa app for Amazon and Matter devices.
  7. If the network listed is correct but you’re still experiencing issues, check that your router is working. To determine if your Echo device or your network is the problem, check the internet connection with another device.

Note: For connection issues with third-party devices that use Wi-Fi and aren’t Matter certified, try controlling your device with the manufacturer’s app. If you can control your device with the manufacturer’s app, but not with Alexa, reactivate the skill in the Alexa app. Otherwise, check your internet connection in the manufacturer’s app. In case these troubleshooting steps don’t work, try resetting your Alexa device and smart home devices.

For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

page.

Connect Smart Home Device Using Bluetooth

Try these steps to connect and resolve issues for Alexa-compatible Bluetooth devices like smart bulbs and smart plugs.

To set up Bluetooth smart home devices with Alexa, just power on your smart home device. Then say, “Discover devices.” If you experience issues during setup, or if your Bluetooth device stops working, try these troubleshooting steps.

  1. Update your smart home device firmware. Check the manufacturer’s website or companion app for instructions to download firmware updates.
  2. Check if your device supports Bluetooth and Alexa. Inspect the packaging and the device for a Bluetooth logo . For Alexa compatibility, check the manufacturer’s instructions on their website or companion app.
  3. Place your smart home device within 30 ft (9 m) of your Echo device.
  4. Make sure that your Echo device software is up to date. Your Echo device software updates automatically. You can also manually check for updates by restarting your device, or by saying, “Check for updates.” If you’re using an Echo device with a screen, swipe down from the top of the display and select Settings. Then go to Device Options > Check for software updates.
  5. Check the instructions for your device. For detailed steps specific to your device, open the Alexa app and open Devices . Select the plus icon and then select Add Device. Select your brand or your device type, then follow the instructions in the app.
  6. If you’re experiencing issues connecting, make sure that your device is in pairing mode. Instructions for pairing mode are usually in the device’s manual.
  7. If you’re still having trouble connecting Bluetooth, try resetting your device.

Note: If your device uses a skill, see Checking Wi-Fi Connectivity on Smart Home Devices.

Editing Tips for Your Floor Plan

If you’re having problems with your floor plan in Map View, try these troubleshooting tips.

  • If your room looks inaccurate, try rescanning it. For simple modifications, use the editing options.
  • For rooms that aren’t in the right place, use the edit options and move the rooms to the right location.
  • Furniture and staircases don’t impact Map View functionality. You can’t edit furniture or staircase placement. To fix any inaccuracies with your furniture or staircase placement, rescan your room.
  • If door placement is inaccurate, you can add or remove doors with the editing options.
  • When you split a room vertically or horizontally, it adds a virtual wall. You can’t add doors to these walls.
    • Split rooms are permanent. The only way to remove a split is to rescan the room again.
  • To resize a room, use the edit options and select the room that you want to resize. If you can’t resize the room, detach the room from the rest of your floor plan, then resize the room.
  • You can only edit your floor plan on compatible iOS devices, but you can still view your floor plan on any iOS device.
    • You can’t access Map View on incompatible iOS devices until first creating a floor plan with a compatible iOS device.

How to Edit Map View

You can edit your existing floor plan in Map View with the Alexa app.

To edit your Map View:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select Map View .
  4. Select Preferences .
  5. Select Edit Floor Plan.

Some Map View editing options include:

  • Add Room.

  • Rename.

  • Split, which allows you to separate one large area into two separate rooms with a virtual wall.

    • Splitting a room is permanent. The only way to remove a split is to rescan the room again.

  • Rescan, which replaces an existing room with a new scan.

  • Move. When moving a room, green lines appear that show where a door can connect to the next room. If the lines are red, then you can’t connect the room in that location.

  • Resize. To resize, drag the room away from the floor plan. Then resize it and reattach it to your floor plan. You can’t resize walls that are still connected to other rooms.

  • Remove, which lets you remove a room from your floor plan.

  • Doors. Add, remove, or modify doors

How to Set Up Map View

Scanning tips:

  • Map View works best when you scan your entire home, even if some rooms don’t have smart home devices in them.

  • Make sure that you finish scanning one room before moving on to the next. Don’t scan your entire home all at once.

  • If your first scan of a room doesn’t work, try rescanning the room. Rescanning the room right away is easier than editing it.

  • When you select a door to add a new room to your floor plan, start scanning the next room from that doorway.

    • Standing in another doorway creates the room in the wrong location.

  • If you have trouble scanning a room, your room might be too dark or there may be objects blocking the corners of the room.

My Echo Wall Clock Hands are Detached

If the hands of the Echo Wall Clock have detached, factory reset your device (This does not apply to Echo Wall Clock Mickey Mouse Edition).

[Embedded video omitted]

To reset your Echo Wall Clock, unpair the device in the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  2. Open Devices.

  3. Navigate to find your Echo device, then select Bluetooth Devices.

  4. Select the icon next to your Echo Wall Clock, and then select Forget Device.

  5. Go back to the device settings page.

  6. Under Connected Devices, select Echo Wall Clock and then Unpair.

  7. Press the pairing button on your Echo Wall Clock five times to reset the device.

    The center post rotates to the 12:00 position, and the status light pulses blue.

  8. If the hands aren’t at the 12:00 position:

    1. Carefully lift the hands from their posts.
    2. Align the notches on the inside of the clock hands with their posts, so that they are at the 12:00 position.
    3. Push the clock hands back onto their posts. The shorter “hour” hand goes first.

    When complete, the status light turns solid green.

  • Set Up Your Echo Wall Clock

My Smart Home Device Doesn’t Connect to Alexa

To troubleshoot setup or connectivity issues, try these steps.

  • Make sure that your smart home device is compatible with Alexa. Devices that have a “Works with Alexa” badge are certified to work with Alexa.
  • Connect smart home Wi-Fi devices on 2.4 GHz bands.
  • Restart your Alexa device and your smart home device by unplugging and plugging them back in.
  • Check that your home internet has connectivity and if your Echo device responds. Say, “Are you online?”
  • If a “No new devices found” message appears in the Alexa app, your device may have connected automatically using Amazon’s Frustration-Free Setup technology. To confirm your device’s connection, check in the Alexa app under Devices.
  • For third-party smart home devices that use Wi-Fi and aren’t Matter certified, download the manufacturer’s app for your smart home device, and complete device setup. Alexa connects to your device with the associated skill.
    • With some devices, you can link your Alexa account and your third-party device’s account in the manufacturer’s app during setup. Then it may activate the relevant skill to connect with Alexa.
    • If the relevant skill isn’t active after setup in the manufacturer’s app, activate the skill as needed in the Alexa app.
  • Download and install any software updates available for your devices.
  • Matter Wi-Fi devices must connect on the same 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network as your compatible Matter controller (such as a compatible Echo device).
  • For Matter devices, make sure it’s within 30 ft (9 m) of your compatible Matter controller.
  • For Zigbee devices, make sure it’s within 30 ft (9 m) of your Zigbee hub or another connected Zigbee smart home device.
  • Make sure that your device is in pairing mode. Pairing mode instructions are usually in the device manufacturer’s manual. Devices that use pairing modes include:
    • Zigbee
    • Bluetooth
    • Matter
  • If your smart home device stops working after successfully connecting to your Alexa Device:
    • Disconnect your smart home device in the Alexa app. Then, activate your smart home device again.
    • If your smart home device uses a skill:
      • Try controlling the device in the manufacturer’s app.
      • If you can control your device with the manufacturer’s app, but not with Alexa, reactivate the skill in the Alexa app.
      • Check your internet connection in the manufacturer’s app.

If these smart home troubleshooting steps don’t work, try resetting your Alexa device and smart home devices. To learn more about Alexa’s Matter support and compatible devices, go to Alexa Smart Home Connectivity.

If your clock is unresponsive, or the hands have detached, factory reset it.

[Embedded video omitted]

Note: To reset your Echo Wall Clock to its factory settings, unpair the device in the Alexa app:

  1. Open the Alexa app .

  2. Open Devices .

  3. Navigate to your Echo device and select Bluetooth Devices.

  4. Select the icon next to your Echo Wall Clock and select Forget Device.

  5. Go back to the device settings page.

  6. Under Connected Devices, select Echo Wall Clock and then Unpair.

  7. On your Echo Wall Clock, press the pairing button five times to reset the device. The center post rotates to the 12:00 position, and the status light pulses blue.

    When the reset is complete, the status light turns solid green.

  8. If the light doesn’t turn solid green, and the hands aren’t at the 12:00 position:

    1. Carefully lift the hands from their posts.
    2. Align the notches on the inside of the clock hands with their posts, so that they are at the 12:00 position.
    3. Push the clock hands back onto their posts. The shorter “hour” hand goes first.

    When the reset is complete, the status light turns solid green.

  9. Set up the Echo Wall Clock again.

Scanning Tips for Map View

If you’re having scanning issues with Map View, try these troubleshooting tips.

Note: You can only use Map View on compatible iOS devices. Learn more at Mapview (amazon.com).

  • If your room doesn’t look right, try rescanning it.
  • Don’t scan your entire home or multiple rooms at the same time. Complete one room before moving to the next.
  • For large rooms without walls, like a combined kitchen and dining room, scan them as one room.
    • To designate each space as its own room, split them horizontally or vertically with the editing tools.
    • Splitting a room is irreversible. The only way to remove a split is to rescan your room again.
  • For the best result, try to spend less than 5 minutes scanning a single room.
  • Make sure that you scan every wall in your room before you select Finish Room.
  • If you can’t begin your scan, make sure that you mimic the on-screen animation in your Alexa app.
    • Keep your phone steady as you scan from floor to ceiling.
    • Try to avoid starting the scan looking at a blank wall.
    • If your scan is still freezing, restart the Alexa app by force closing it. If that doesn’t work, try restarting your phone.
  • Furniture and staircases don’t impact Map View functionality.
    • If your stairs or furniture are missing, try rescanning the room (but don’t stand on the staircase while scanning).
    • When you’re at the bottom of the staircase, carefully scan slowly while moving your camera upwards. If you’re at the top, carefully scan slowly while moving your camera downwards.
  • You don’t have to scan small spaces, like closets or cupboards. If you do want to scan them, stay as far away from the wall you’re scanning as possible.
  • Map View doesn’t support scanning bay windows or round walls.

Set Up Your Echo Wall Clock

Pair Echo Wall Clock with a single compatible device. Say, “Set up my Echo Wall Clock.”

Important: To avoid damage, don’t push or move the clock hands.

[Embedded video omitted]

Make sure that your compatible Echo device is set up. To find compatible devices, go to Echo Wall Clock.

  1. Insert four AA batteries into your Echo Wall Clock.

  2. On your compatible Echo device, say, “Set up my Echo Wall Clock.”

  3. Put your Echo Wall Clock in pairing mode. Press and hold the blue pairing button on the back of device for up to 10 seconds. The status LED on the front pulses orange.

    • When the status LED turns blue, the device is paired and the time sync begins.
    • The light pulses blue as your clock syncs with your compatible Echo device.
    • The hands start and stop several times during this process.
    • Once the time is set, the status LED turns off.

    Pairing takes up to 10 minutes to complete.

  4. Install your clock with the mounting hardware included in the box.

Note: If setting up your Echo Wall Clock with your voice does not work, make sure the Echo Wall Clock is in pairing mode and try one of the following methods.

  • For devices without a screen:
  1. In the Alexa App, select Devices.
  2. Select Echo & Alexa.
  3. Select Choose the Echo device you want to pair.
  4. Select Bluetooth Devices.
  5. Select Pair a New Device.
  6. Select Echo Wall Clock.
  • For devices with a screen:
  1. On your device, select Settings.
  2. Select Bluetooth.

Switching Between Home and Away Modes

Use the Alexa app, voice commands, or your device to switch between modes.

Say to Alexa:

  • “I’m leaving” or “We’re heading out” to switch to away mode.
  • “I’m home” or “We’re back” to switch to home mode.

Note: Voice commands don’t switch modes if you’re already using them as a response for a Routine. To allow these voice commands to switch modes, change your Routine’s prompt to a different voice command.

In the Alexa app, switch modes by selecting Modes or on the top right of the home screen.

On Echo Hub, switch modes by selecting Modes or on the top right of the home screen.

Troubleshoot Error Codes for Amazon Smart Home Devices

If you see an error code in the Alexa app when setting up your Amazon Smart Home device, such as your Amazon Smart Thermostat, try some of these troubleshooting steps.

  • App Error Code: 3:1:0:1; Issue: The device couldn’t connect because of issues processing your Wi-Fi credentials.; Troubleshooting: 1. Perform a factory reset on your device. 2. Open the Alexa app and select Devices . 3. Select Add Device to proceed through setup instructions.
  • App Error Code: 3:2:0:1; Issue: The Alexa app password was incorrect and authentication failed.; Troubleshooting: Confirm your correct password and re-enter.
  • App Error Code: 3:5:0:1; Issue: The device connected to the Wi-Fi router, but it still doesn’t have internet connectivity.; Troubleshooting: Ensure you have internet access on other devices. If not, reach out to your internet service provider to restore access.
  • App Error Code: 3:10:0:3 3:11:0:3 3:13:0:3; Issue: This is a registration error.; Troubleshooting: Retry setup process.
  • App Error Code: 3:14:0:3; Issue: Setup failed, either due to a Wi-Fi or registration issue.; Troubleshooting: Retry setup process.
  • App Error Code: 3:15:0:3; Issue: Device registration succeeded and the system waited but timed out to complete post-registration steps.; Troubleshooting: You might be able to start using the device despite this error. If not, retry setup process.
  • App Error Code: 3:0:0:3; Issue: This is a miscellaneous setup failure.; Troubleshooting: Retry setup process.
  • App Error Code: 3:16:0:1; Issue: This happens when a router is detected and the system tried to connect with it, but connection was unsuccessful. This could be because the router went down or the Wi-Fi signal is low and the system failed to detect it.; Troubleshooting: Move the device closer to the router (or the router closer to the device), and try setup again.
  • App Error Code: 3:20:0:3; Issue: The device is unable to connect to the router/access point.; Troubleshooting: Retry setup process.

What Are Low Supply Notifications & Smart Reorders?

Alexa can notify you or reorder essential items when you’re running low.

After connecting a device with Alexa that is compatible with smart reorders, like a printer, Alexa activates low supply notifications automatically.

With low supply notifications, you’ll receive notifications for compatible products when your supply is running low.

Alternatively, you can activate smart reorders for automatic reordering on products you choose when Alexa detects low supply.

Note: Low supply notifications and smart reorders can’t be active at the same time. If you activate smart reorders, it turns off low supply notifications. And if you activate low supply notifications, it turns off smart reorders.

Additional things to know:

  • You can deactivate low supply notifications and smart reorders together in the Alexa app.
  • When low supply notifications are active, you’ll receive notifications via email and on any Echo devices you own.
    • You can order products from the notification email or by voice confirmation on your Echo device.
    • If you don’t have an Echo device, you can still use low supply notifications and smart reorders in the Alexa app.
    • You might also get notifications about low supplies on the Amazon Shopping app or website.
  • When you activate smart reorders, you can choose products to automatically reorder during setup.
    • You can only set smart reorders for items that appear on the smart reorder setup screen on your device.
    • You can change your product choice in the Alexa app.
  • How to Set Up Smart Reorders
  • How to Turn Off Low Supply Notifications & Smart Reorders

What Are Modes?

Control your smart home devices all at once when you leave or return home, when it’s nighttime and when you go on vacation.

With modes, assign smart home or other Alexa actions you want to occur. Like Routines, modes let you save time by grouping together multiple actions. Switch modes manually with Alexa or on your Alexa-enabled device.

As you switch between modes, Alexa performs actions that correspond to each mode. For example, switching to away mode may look like this:

  • Arm security system

What Are Smart Home Groups?

Smart home groups let you use Alexa to control multiple devices at once.

  • You can add multiple types of devices to a smart home group to control lights, music, and other smart home devices.

  • When you add an Echo device to a smart home group, you can use Alexa to control all the devices in that group. For example, you can create a smart home group for “Living Room.” Then say, “Lights on” to turn on all the lights in that group.

    Note: Echo devices can only be added to one smart home group at a time.

  • When creating smart home groups with multiple speakers, you can set a default speaker for music playback.

What Do the Echo Wall Clock LED Colors Mean?

The status LED is how your device communicates its status.

Pulsing Orange

Echo Wall Clock is in pair mode.

Solid Blue for Three Seconds

You paired your Echo Wall Clock.

Pulsing Blue

Echo Wall Clock syncs the time during setup or receives a software update.

Three Blue Blinks

Echo Wall Clock is disconnected from your Echo device.

Pulsing Blue Followed by Solid Green

The blue pairing button was pressed five times, and Echo Wall Clock was reset. Say, “Set up my Echo Wall Clock.”

Pulsing Perimeter LEDs

Your paired Echo device has a timer or alarm sounding.

Yellow

You have a new notification on the paired Echo device.

Single Red Blink

Echo Wall Clock has a low battery.

Note: After changing the batteries, it takes up to 10 minutes for the time to sync.

  • Set Up Your Echo Wall Clock

What Is Away Lighting with Alexa?

Use Away Lighting when you leave to make it appear as though you’re home.

When Away Lighting is on, Alexa turns connected smart lights on and off periodically to make it look like someone is home.

To turn on Away Lighting with your connected your smart bulbs, plugs, and switches:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select Devices .
  3. Select any light.
  4. Select Settings .
  5. Select Away Lighting.
  6. Followed the guided setup instructions for Away Lighting.

To turn Away Lighting on or off, go to the Alexa app home screen and navigate to the Favorites section. Select the Away Lighting tile to turn the feature on or off.

Note: Sync Away Lighting with home and away modes to turn Away Lighting on or off automatically. For example, add Away Lighting to away mode so the feature turns on when you switch to away mode, and off when you switch to home mode.

What Is Doorbell Live View?

When the doorbell is pressed, you get a live feed of your camera on Echo devices with screens.

If you’re using your Echo device, Alexa pauses streaming music or video for the live camera feed. On Fire TV, Alexa displays the live camera feed. Audio is muted on the doorbell and on the device by default. To turn audio on, tap the Mic icon on the screen or say, “Talk to the front door”.

Doorbell Live View is supported on all generations of Fire TV, Echo Show and Echo Spot.

Note: If you have more than one device, Alexa makes the doorbell announcement on the preferred device you selected in the Alexa app.

What Is Frustration-Free Automation?

Alexa may automatically create Routines for you when you set up a new smart home device.

During setup of an Alexa-enabled smart home device, Frustration-Free Automation automatically creates Routines for compatible, connected devices to work together.

For example, if you set up a smart light bulb for your patio, Alexa looks for devices in the same smart home group with compatible functions. Alexa may find a Ring outdoor camera, and create a Routine to increase the brightness of your patio light when the camera detects motion.

Alexa sends a notification in the Alexa app when it creates a Routine for you. To view, edit, deactivate, or delete Routines created by Frustration-Free Automation:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Select .
  3. Select Routines.
  4. Select Your Routines. Routines created by Frustration-Free Automation are labeled by Alexa.
  5. Select the Routine that you wish to view, edit, deactivate, or delete.

To deactivate Frustration-Free Automation from creating Routines for you, go to Manage Your Content & Devices.

Map View provides a simple way to view, manage, and control your compatible smart home devices using the Alexa app. Map View with Alexa+ also lets you open and control your devices using compatible Echo Show devices.

About Ambient Sounds with Alexa+

Use Alexa to listen to your favorite ambient sounds to help you sleep, relax, focus, or mediate.

You can get access to Alexa’s Ambient Sounds ad-free with Alexa+. Ambient sounds let you playback content for up to 10 hours without disruption.

Ask Alexa to “play ambient sounds,” or ask for specific sounds like, “play thunderstorm sounds.” You can conversationally ask Alexa, “what are some ambient sounds I can listen to?”

There are different sounds, such as rain, ocean, thunderstorms, crackling fire, and white noise.

On Echo devices that support visual experiences, Alexa ambient sounds also offers immersive visuals. To find a full list of ambient sounds available on Echo devices with a screen, go to Music and More > Soundscapes.

Alexa remembers your preferences and can help you find sounds you listened to previously. You can ask, “What was that focus sound I listened to last week?”

You can set a routine to listen to Alexa ambient sounds by asking Alexa to “set up a sleep time routine every night to start thunderstorm sounds.”

Images

After requesting content, Alexa generates a discussion with generative AI host(s) who will explore your chosen topic.

About Dining Reservations with

        Alexa+ {#about-dining-reservations-with-alexa}

Make reservations at restaurants with Alexa using supported Alexa-enabled devices or the Alexa app.

You can use Alexa to search for and reserve tables with restaurants through supported third-party services. For steps on linking your third-party accounts, managing permissions, or to learn more about the service, go to How Third-Party Services Work with Alexa+.

To start, say something like, “I’d like to book a dinner reservation for two people tonight.” Alexa may ask follow up questions to help you finish choosing a restaurant. This could include confirming the type of food you’re looking for, reservation time, and location.

If your preferred restaurant or time isn’t available, Alexa suggests alternative restaurants. For restaurants that don’t accept reservations through Alexa, contact information may be provided when available.

Once Alexa has confirmed the basic details, Alexa provides a few recommendations from the linked service. On devices with a screen, Alexa provides details about restaurants such as distance, food type, and ratings. You can interact with the on-screen details to further expand the available information.

As you make a reservation, you can make adjustments, ask for details about the restaurant, save restaurant information for later, and more. Try saying things like:

  • “I’d like to change my reservation to four people.”
  • “What’s the rating on this restaurant?”
  • “Remember this restaurant for later.”

Before making a reservation, Alexa asks permission to share certain profile details with the corresponding third-party reservation service. After confirmation, you’ll receive an email from the third-party service, and the event will be automatically added to your calendar.

Note: If you need to update your linked calendar, go to Link Calendars to Alexa.

After creating a reservation, you can ask Alexa to help with things like rescheduling, canceling, or adjusting the party size. The third-party service’s terms apply to reservations and may include cancellation fees.

About Food Ordering with Alexa+

Alexa’s food ordering feature lets you order food with third-party services. You can order food from your favorite places using Alexa-supported devices.

For steps on linking third-party accounts, managing permissions, or to learn more about the service, go to: Connect Your Third-Party Services to Alexa+

To start, say something like, “What can I get delivered for dinner tonight?” Alexa guides you through the ordering process, by helping choose a restaurant, adding or removing items from your cart, modifying items, and checking out.

While ordering, you may be able to add special instructions like requesting the removal of certain ingredients or providing any dietary needs.

Note: The option to customize orders is determined by the restaurant.

Alexa can answer questions, make adjustments, or take you to checkout. For example, just say:

  • “I’d like to remove an item.”
  • “I’d like to add special instructions to an item in my cart.”
  • “I’m ready to checkout.”

You can manage your order by voice or on-screen options.

You can review your cart and say checkout. When you say “checkout” or select the checkout button, you’ll be taken to the checkout summary screen where you can review your delivery address and payment method used.

Note: After placing the order, you need to contact the third-party service to cancel. Alexa can’t cancel orders. If you have a question about an order that has been completed, you have to contact the third party directly. For more information on when to contact the third-party service go to, How Third-Party Services Work with Alexa+

Once your place your order with Alexa, you receive a notification from your chosen third-party provider. Alexa will also notify you about your order status. For example, you can ask “where is my Grubhub order.”

You can also ask Alexa to reorder past favorites, including the special requests you had.

About Remember This with Alexa+

Use Alexa to create, update, go to, and archive notes that you want to remember in the future.

To create and store information, you can ask Alexa to create a note. For example, “Remember my friend’s birthday,” or “Remember that I want to eat more healthy greens.” There’s no limit to the number of notes that you can create.

To retrieve notes, you can say things like:

  • “What do you remember about dinner on Tuesday night?”

To update a note, ask about the information you want to remember, and then ask Alexa to change it. For example, “What is my son’s shoe size?” and then, “Change my son’s shoe size to 7.”

While Remember This is primarily a conversation only experience, you can also go to and archive your stored notes in the Alexa app.

About Routines by Voice with Alexa+

Create routines with your voice using Alexa to create automations for actions such as controlling smart home devices, playing music, getting weather updates, and more.

Alexa Routines are automations that save you time by grouping multiple actions together. You can create a routine by voice using any supported Alexa-enabled Echo devices, the Alexa app, and supported Alexa-enabled Fire TV devices.

With Alexa Routines by Voice, you can create a routine that includes multiple actions, but not limited to:

  • Controlling smart home devices.
  • Playing music.
  • Controlling your Fire TV.
  • Getting the weather.
  • Reading your calendar for the day.
  • Making announcements.
  • Setting custom responses.

To learn more about routines, go to What Can You Do with Alexa Routines?

To create a routine with your voice, describe to Alexa what you want to happen and when. For example, you can say, “Can you play music and turn the lights on in my bedroom every weekday at 7AM?”

Alexa creates and saves the routine in the Alexa app, then notifies you of successful creation or provides you with any errors that occurred.

You can make changes to your routines, such as adding, updating, or deleting actions, immediately after routine creation.

If you can’t adjust the routine with your voice, go to Update Your Alexa Routines.

About Share with Alexa+

Share files, images and webpages with Alexa to draft replies to emails, provide summaries, answer questions related to the shared material, and more.

You can share files, images, and webpages with Alexa by emailing them to alexa@alexa.com or in the Alexa app.

There are a few things to keep in mind when you’re sharing files with Alexa:

  • Alexa recognizes emails from the email addresses associated with your Alexa profile. If you need to update, add, or remove your email address, follow the steps in Manage the Email Address Used for Share with Alexa+.
  • Emails and files must be under 25 MB and in one of the following formats: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, HEIF, PDF, DOCX, RTF, TXT.
  • Alexa can reference text within files and recognize objects in images that you share.
  • Alexa doesn’t support videos or password-protected documents.
  • You can review the files you’ve shared in your Alexa Privacy Settings.

Alexa saves the shared files and uses them to help you with the following:

Add Events to Your Calendar and Set Alexa Reminders

Alexa searches your shared emails, files and webapges for event names, dates, times, and locations. Using that information, Alexa suggests events and reminders to add to your schedule. For future instances, you can also choose to automatically add events and reminders to your schedule (events will be added to your default calendar).

Alexa sends you a confirmation email or phone push notification with details of the suggested or added events and reminders. Select the push notification to review and add extracted items or remove added items.

Answer Questions and Give Summaries

You can ask Alexa questions about your shared emails, files, and webapges or have Alexa summarize them. Alexa references your shared files whenever someone asks questions on your supported Alexa-enabled devices or the Alexa app.

Analyze Images and Get Creative Suggestions

Alexa can also reference the images you share when you ask questions on your supported Alexa-enabled devices or the Alexa app. For example, you can say, “What plants are in this image,” or “Describe this image in three sentences.”

Add Personal Recipes to Your Cooking l ibrary

When you share a recipe with Alexa, Alexa will extract the recipe and save it to your Cooking Library. You’ll have the ability to edit recipe details including ingredients and preparation steps, customize recipe cover photos, and organize all your personal recipes in a centralized location.

These recipes become part of your Cooking Library and appear alongside other recipes when you search for cooking inspiration using Alexa, making it easy to access both your personal recipes and professional content hands-free while you’re cooking.

You can access your Cooking Library by saying “show my personal recipes” or by navigating to your Cooking Library in your Alexa app under More or Echo device.

Draft Replies to Emails

When you share emails with Alexa, you can ask for suggested replies. Alexa uses the context and tone of the original email and creates a reply to get you started.

About Sharing Your Alexa Experience in the

        Alexa App {#about-sharing-your-alexa-experience-in-the-alexa-app}

Adults in your home can share a single Alexa account and Alexa+ membership, while keeping a personalized experience through profiles in the Alexa app.

As an account owner, you can send invites through the Alexa app. Recipients can create a profile and have a personalized experience in the Alexa app, without needing you account login information. You can send a maximum of six invitations at a time. Invitations expire after seven days, but can be resent to the same recipient after expiration.

Note: Kids profiles can’t receive invitations.

Members added as a profile to your Alexa app can:

  • Use their own profile on Alexa-enabled devices registered to your Amazon account.
  • Access shared Alexa features and services.
  • Use the Alexa app.
  • Manage your Echo device, smart home devices, and shared Alexa features, including Voice Purchasing.

Members added as a profile to your Alexa app can’t:

  • Switch between profiles in the Alexa app.

  • Access other Amazon apps or services.

Search, book, and create notifications for tickets to various events using your compatible Alexa devices or the Alexa app.

Booking Tickets:

You can ask Alexa to book tickets to live events such as concerts, movies, comedy shows, theatrical plays, and sports events. To get started, say something like, “I’d like to book two tickets to the Seahawks game.” Alexa guides you through the booking process, asking follow-up questions to confirm details like the event date, venue, and seating preferences.

If you have a device with a screen, you can review these details on your screen. Alexa provides booking recommendations based on your initial requests.

As you book tickets, you can make changes, ask for details about the event, and more. Try saying things like:

  • “Show me the best seats.”
  • “Is there a different show time?”
  • “Are there any sets of four tickets, seated together?”

After you confirm the details and the booking is complete:

  • The third-party service sends ticket details to your Alexa account email address.
  • Alexa provides verbal confirmation and visual confirmation on devices with a screen.
  • Alexa adds the reservation to your Alexa calendar.

Creating Ticket Notifications:

You can ask Alexa to create a ticket notification for specific artists, events, or shows. You can customize the notification based on preferences like the number of tickets, price range, dates, and seating.

To review your ticket notifications, go to the notification center in the Alexa app. You can also ask Alexa, “What tickets are you tracking for me?”

Note: If you have a dispute, cancellation, or refund request, contact the third-party ticketing service directly for support. For more information on when to contact a third party, go to How Third-Party Services Work with Alexa+.

About Top Connections with Alexa+

The Top Connections widget on your compatible Echo device with a screen lets you easily communicate with your household members and most important contacts.

You can use the Top Connections widget to quickly start a call with your contact or Drop In on their supported Alexa devices.

The widget also shows helpful information about your contacts, including their recently active devices and birthday reminders.

From the Top Connections Menu , you can manage your calling and Drop In settings and customize which contacts appear in your widget.

To get started with Top Connections:

  • Add the Top Connections widget on your device.
  • Add your contacts and information like their birthday by following the steps in Manage Your Alexa Contacts.

Note: You don’t need to turn on Drop In to use Top Connections.

  • Add Widgets on Your Echo Device with a Screen
  • Turn Drop In On or Off for your Device

About Travel Planning with Alexa+

Plan and manage your travel itineraries with the help of Alexa+.

You can use Alexa on supported Alexa-enabled devices or the Alexa app to create and manage travel itineraries for trips up to 14 days long. Alexa shares information from third-party services to provide personalized recommendations for destinations, activities, accommodations, and more.

To start planning a trip, say something like, “I’d like to plan a trip to Seattle for next week.” Alexa may ask follow-up questions to help create an itinerary. This could include confirming your travel dates, interests, preferred activities, and accommodation preferences.

Alexa uses the shared details and preferences to provide recommendations for the trip, including attractions, hotels, restaurants, and activities. On compatible devices with a screen, you can interact with the on-screen details to further expand the available information.

As you create your itinerary, you can make adjustments, ask for details about specific locations, and more. Try saying things like:

  • “Add this restaurant to day three of my itinerary.”

  • “What’s the best time to visit this attraction?”

  • “I’d like to continue planning my trip for next week.”

  • “Send this itinerary to my email.”

  • Compatibility of Alexa+ with Alexa Enabled Devices

About Videos with Alexa+

Alexa+ gives you more ways to explore your video content, ask for recommendations, and navigate your video experience.

Explore your video content through natural conversation with Alexa+ on Alexa devices and Fire TV devices. Alexa+ learns your preferences and can make suggestions about movies or TV shows from Prime Video and supported streaming services.

For example, you can say things like, “What movie do you recommend if I like Top Gun?” or “Can you help me find some action-packed movies that will make me laugh?” when navigating through your supported streaming service.

Activate Alexa+

You can sign up for Alexa+ at Alexaplus (amazon.com). Alternatively, if you have an Echo device, you can say “Alexa, upgrade!”

Alexa+ Requirements

If Alexa+ isn’t available on your device, check your account or device settings.

Alexa+ has a few account and device requirements beyond device compatibility. Before you get started, review the steps below to make sure everything is ready.

Note: Not all devices support Alexa+. Check Compatibility of Alexa+ with Alexa Built-in Devices. If notifications about Alexa+ requirements appear during device setup, finish setting up your device first. Then return to this page to address them.

Language and Location

  • Set your device to use a supported language during setup. Learn how to Change the Language on Your Echo Device.
  • Alexa+ is available only for personal Amazon accounts set to a supported location. Learn how to Update Country Settings for Access to Country Specific Features.

Account Type

  • Alexa+ works only with personal Amazon accounts. It is not compatible with Amazon Enterprise or Business accounts.
  • To use Alexa+ on a device registered to a business account, factory reset the device and set it up with your personal account. Learn how to Reset Your Echo Device.

Amazon Family Compatibility

  • Alexa+ is compatible with devices in an Amazon Family.
  • If Alexa+ doesn’t perform at its best on all of your Family devices, some adjustments in your Amazon Family might help. To learn more, visit Using Alexa+ with Amazon Family.

Purchased Device Eligibility

If Alexa+ came with a device purchase, access to Alexa+ belongs to the Amazon account used to register that device.

After Setup

Once you’ve addressed any remaining compatibility requirements in your account, your Alexa+ experience should be available soon.

For more information about availability and frequently asked questions, go to: Alexaplus (amazon.com).

Tip: If you still can’t access Alexa+ after addressing these requirements, check whether your device software needs an update. Say, “Check for software updates.”

Ask for Music and Recommendations with Alexa+

Alexa+ gives you more ways to ask for songs, get recommendations, and review your listening history.

Alexa+ can help you find music and make recommendations through natural conversation like you would talk to a friend.

Tip: For examples of common playback commands, go to Play Music with Alexa Using Your Voice.

You can speak to Alexa conversationally when you make a request, but some examples of things you can say are:

Ask Alexa to play some music:

In addition to common requests like searching by a song title or artists, you can make more complex requests. Ask Alexa for what you’d like based on your mood, genre, setting, and more:

  • “Play [artist 1], [artist2], and [artist 3].”
    • For example, “Play Adele, Beyoncé, and Taylor Swift.”
  • “Play ’90s music by Metallica, but not the high tempo songs.”
  • “Play some songs that you may hear at a [genre] festival.”
  • “Play music from the artists who headlined at [event] last year.”
    • For example, “Play music from the artists who headlined at Coachella last year.”
  • “Play [genre] music that’s best for [activity].”
    • For example, “Play rock music that’s best for working out.”
  • “Play the artist who won album of the year at the Grammys’s.”

Ask Alexa to play the radio:

  • “Play [radio station name].”
  • “Play a [genre] radio station from [location].”
    • For example, “Play a radio station from San Francisco.”
  • “Play [radio frequency] [AM or FM].”

Ask Alexa to recommend music and radio stations:

  • “Recommend a [genre] to listen to while doing [activity].”
    • For example, “Recommend rock music to listen to while cleaning the house.”
  • “Recommend [mood] music for me.”
    • For example, you can ask for rainy day, uplifting, sad, or happy songs.
  • “Who are some artists like [artist name]?”
  • “Recommend a [genre] radio station.”
    • For example, you can ask for sports, local, or live news radio stations.
    • “Play the second one” (After Alexa suggests options).

Search for and play music by lyrics, artists, movies, TV shows, and more:

  • “What is the main theme song in [movie, TV show, podcast]?”
  • “What is the song that goes [lyrics]?”
  • “What was the song in [movie name]?”
  • “Who headlined at [event] last year?”
  • “What are some radio stations in my area?”

Ask Alexa to play music you’ve listened to previously.

  • “Play my top artist.”
  • “What did I listen to earlier this morning?”
  • “What did I play on Spotify?”
  • “What did I hear this week?”
  • “What are the artists that I heard most recently?”
  • “Recap my listening history for this week.”
  • “What was that song by [artist] I was listening to earlier?”
  • “What songs did I listen to in [playlist] yesterday?”

Ask Alexa About Your Listening History

Alexa+ gives you insights into your household listening habits and patterns on Alexa over the last 30 days, including music, podcasts, radio, and audiobooks.

  • “What is my top [artist, songs, playlists, station, albums, audiobooks, or podcast]?”
  • “What is my top [artist, songs, playlists, station, albums, audiobooks, or podcast] today?”
  • “What is my top song from [artist, album, or playlist] ?”
  • “How many times have I listened to [artist, songs, playlist, station, album] this week?”
  • “What are my top [number] [ artist ] albums?”
  • “How many times did I listen to [artist]?”

Note: Support for Alexa+ music features may vary depending on the music provider.

Bluetooth Set Up for Text to Contacts with

        Alexa+ {#bluetooth-set-up-for-text-to-contacts-with-alexa}

Download or update the Alexa app from your mobile device’s app store and turn on the feature from your phones mobile app for the Echo device.

Bluetooth Setup:

  1. Open up the Alexa app .
  2. Select the More icon .
  3. Select the Settings icon.
  4. Select Communication.
  5. Select Texting.
  6. Select Enable for your Echo device and follow the on-screen instructions.
  7. Once you’re directed to Start Pairing, select this link to access your phone’s Bluetooth Settings page.
  8. Your device shows up in the available devices list for pairing.
  9. Select your device’s name and follow the instructions on the page:
    1. For Android devices, select Allow to allow texting and Pair when prompted for Bluetooth pairing.
    2. For iOS devices, select the i icon next to your device. Then, accept both permission pop- ups to turn on Show Message Notification.

Note: To verify setup completion, return to Settings , then Communication, and Texting to confirm your Echo device shows’ Enabled for texting status.

Continue Chats with Alexa+ on Your Browser

Find and keep previous conversations with Alexa, even those started with devices or on the Alexa app.

Along with starting new conversations with Alexa, you can use Alexa+ on your browser to review or resume previous chats. You can copy any of Alexa’s answers for your reference, or save entire conversations.

Note: Alexa+ on your browser is available only with Alexa+.

When logged in to Alexa+ on your browser, in the left navigation, select Recent Chats to open your chat history with Alexa.

Select a conversation from the list to open it as the main chat.

  • To continue the chat, enter what you want to say in the chat bar.
  • To keep one of Alexa’s responses, go to the end of the response and select Copy text response .
  • To keep the entire conversation, go to the end of the chat and select Download full discussion .
  • If Alexa’s answer wasn’t quite what you wanted, you can select Rephrase .

Controlling Your Smart Home with

        Alexa+ {#controlling-your-smart-home-with-alexa}

Speak to Alexa naturally to complete household actions.

You don’t have to memorize a list of commands or device names to control your smart home devices. Use conversational language when making requests or asking questions to Alexa.

Some ways to talk with Alexa to manage your Alexa-connected smart home devices:

Request Multiple Actions

Alexa completes multiple requests from a single statement. Say something like, “Turn on the kitchen and living room lights, and open my blinds,” and Alexa completes these actions for you.

Make General Statements

For example, say to Alexa, “It’s dark in this room,” and Alexa adjusts lighting levels in the appropriate room. Alexa interprets general statements about the state of the home, and takes action based on those statements.

Ask About Device Status

With Alexa+, you can ask Alexa about non-grouped devices. To check the status of a set of non-grouped devices, say something like, “Have you turned off all my lights?” Alexa answers for all lights, even if they’re not in a group. For grouped devices, use the group name when talking with Alexa.

Control Devices Without Memorization

Don’t remember the names of your smart home devices? Use other words that signal the device you want to Alexa. You can say, “Turn on the new light in the living room,” and Alexa turns on the recently connected light in your living room.

Conversations with Alexa+

With Alexa+ you can interact with Alexa conversationally, without having to memorize a list of commands.

When interacting with Alexa+, you can maintain a conversational tone and follow-up without having to repeat the wake word every time. On compatible Echo Show devices, you can also interrupt Alexa without having to say the wake word.

Alexa understands the context of your conversations and, when specifically asked, can remember the details from previous communications. If Alexa doesn’t understand a request, Alexa asks clarifying questions to get the details needed to move the conversation forward.

For example, if you say, “Can you help me plan a trip this summer?” Alexa may respond with, “Sure, how many days are you thinking of traveling this summer?”

Here are just some of the ways you can talk with Alexa:

Ask and Explore

You can have in-depth conversations with Alexa on a wide variety of subjects. Alexa lets you ask follow-up questions to explore subjects in more detail, and Alexa will adapt the responses accordingly.

You can ask Alexa to research any topic, summarize key details, and get a concise and informative overview. Alexa adapts its responses based on how you’re interacting, providing longer responses and visual content when you’re using text, while keeping voice responses more concise.

To get started, simply ask Alexa an open-ended question.

Continuous Learning

Alexa asks questions to get to know you better and provide more personalized recommendations and assistance, like:

  • Recipe search based on your dietary preferences, the ingredients, and cuisines cooking methods you like.
  • Updates on your favorite sports teams and leagues.
  • Alexa learns to remember what song you meant. If Alexa ever plays another song than what you had in mind, you only need to correct it once and it will remember if you meant to play “Hello” by Adele or Lionel Richie.

Continue Conversations Between Devices

Alexa+ remembers the context of conversations so that you can seamlessly pick up where you left off, whether on your Echo device or in the Alexa app.

For example, you can ask Alexa for dinner recipes and continue building out your weekly grocery list in the Alexa app on the way to the grocery store.

Delete Voice and Text Chat History in the Alexa App

To delete some or all of your Alexa chat history, you can use the Alexa app.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More .
  3. Select Alexa Privacy.
  4. Select Review Voice History, and use the drop-down to select a date range, or filter by device or profile.
  5. Select the chats that you want to delete.

Note: Voice recordings are used to improve the accuracy of your interactions with Alexa. Deleting voice recordings associated with your account could degrade your experience.

How Follow Up Mode Works on Alexa+

With Follow Up Mode, you don’t need to repeat the wake word when talking to Alexa+.

When Follow Up Mode is turned on, Alexa+ lets you have natural conversational interactions. You’ll see a visual indicator when you can talk to Alexa without repeating the wake word.

On compatible Echo Show devices, you can also interrupt Alexa without having to use the wake word when you are in view of the camera and facing the screen.

Note: When Follow Up mode is off, Alexa requires a wake word for follow-up interactions.

How Third-Party Services Work with Alexa+

Alexa+ can help you purchase tickets, request rides, reserve a table, and book other services.

You can link different third-party services to Alexa+. Just ask and Alexa helps you connect those services.

After you place an order or book a service through Alexa+, you’ll receive a confirmation email from the service provider. Emails go to the email address associated with your Amazon account.

If you’ve used Alexa to make a purchase from a third-party service, and you have questions or need help, you will need to contact the company directly. You can find their contact details in the email confirming your purchase, or on their website.

  • Connect Your Third-Party Services to Alexa+

How to Book Local Services with Alexa+

Alexa+ lets you find and schedule appointments with nearby businesses for services like haircuts and massages.

To book a local service with Alexa+:

  1. Ask Alexa for help with booking a service, you can say, “help me book a manicure appointment.”
  2. Alexa shows a list of businesses for the service that you requested. Alexa uses the context in the request to infer the type of service and the schedule needed.
  3. Link Account: If needed, Alexa guides you to create and link a third-party account to complete bookings. For steps on linking third-party services to your Alexa account, go to Connect Your Third-Party Services to Alexa+.
  4. Booking: Alexa asks question if needed to complete the booking such as availability and appointment details. Alexa confirms the information before initiating the booking with the third party and completes the booking on your behalf once you confirm the details. If Alexa didn’t understand your request, or you account details accurately, you can tell Alexa.
  5. Alexa confirms the final request with the third party.

Once confirmed, you receive a notification on your device and also a confirmation email from the third party.

Note: You can request to cancel a booking with Alexa. If there are any fees associated, Alexa notifies you and only cancels if you agree. If you have a question about a booking that has been completed, you have to contact the third party directly. For more information on when to contact the third-party service go to, How Third-Party Services Work with Alexa+.

  • Compatibility of Alexa+ with Alexa Built-in Devices
  • Connect Your Third-Party Services to Alexa+
  • About Local Booking with Alexa+

How to Book Rides with Alexa+

Alexa’s ride booking feature lets you book rides with third-party services. You can book rides to your favorite places using supported Alexa-supported devices.

To book a ride:

  1. Ask Alexa to book a ride. You can say things like, “I want to book a ride to the mall.”

  2. If you haven’t granted permissions and linked your rideshare account with your Alexa account, Alexa guides you through the account linking process. For more information, go to Connect Your Third-Party Services to Alexa+.

  3. Confirm or edit the service. Alexa provides options based on where you want to go and asks clarifying questions to select the best ride option for you before booking it.

    Note: The rideshare service charges the default payment card on your rideshare account. If you don’t have an existing card, you can go to the rideshare app to add one.

  4. Alexa confirms your ride request to completing the booking with the third-party provider.

Once you confirm your ride, Alexa announces the status of the arrival through notifications. You receive notifications on the Alexa app and on your rideshare app.

Note: You can request to cancel a ride with Alexa. If there are any fees associated, Alexa notifies you and only cancels if you agree. If you have a question about a ride that has been completed, you have to contact the third party directly. For more information on when to contact the third-party service go to, How Third-Party Services Work with Alexa+.

Indicators for Alexa+ on Echo Devices with a Screen

The visual indicators on your Echo device with a screen communicate various device statuses and interactions. Understanding these indicators can help you better use your device and troubleshoot any issues.

Note: You can ask Alexa about the lights or indicators you see.

Here is an overview of the indicators for Echo devices with a screen:

Bell Icon

A bell icon with a blue badge in the top left-hand corner of your device means that Alexa has a message or notification, or there’s a reminder you missed. Say, “What are my notifications?” or “What are my messages?”

Listening Indicator

A pulsing blue light at the bottom of the screen means that Alexa is listening. The pulsing matches your voice - wider pulses for louder speech, shorter pulses for softer speech.

[Embedded video omitted]

Alexa+ Light - Listening

Ready-to-Listen Indicator

A small, solid blue light at the bottom of the screen indicates that Alexa is ready for you to speak. This means you can speak directly to Alexa without first saying Alexa.

[Embedded video omitted]

Alexa+ Light - Ready to Listen

Processing Indicator

A blue light moving like an ocean wave from left to right means that Alexa is thinking or processing your request.

[Embedded video omitted]

Alexa+ - Processing Indicator

Camera/Microphones Indicator

A red light tells you the camera and microphones on/off button is pressed, and the device microphones and camera are turned off. Press the button again to turn on the device microphones and camera.

[Embedded video omitted]

Alexa+ Camera/Microphones Indicator

Call in Progress

A green light comes on when you’re in a call or a Drop In, and you leave the call screen. It shows that you’re still on an active call.

[Embedded video omitted]

Alexa+ - Call in Progress

Do Not Disturb

When the Do Not Disturb feature is on, a crescent moon icon shows in the top left-hand corner after you make any request. Turn off Do Not Disturb to speak with Alexa again.

Note: Listening, Processing, and Ready-to-Listen Indicators will be visible on the Alexa app.

  • About Alexa’s Personality with Alexa+

Light Indicators for Alexa+ on Echo Dot Max and Echo Studio (2025 release)

The visual indicators on your Echo device communicate various device statuses and interactions. Understanding these indicators can help you better use your device and troubleshoot any issues.

Note: You can ask Alexa about the light indicators you see.

Communication Indicator

A green light comes on when you are receiving an incoming call or in an active call.

[Embedded video omitted]

Communications

Do Not Disturb Indicator

When Do Not Disturb Feature is on, a purple light will show briefly when Alexa finishes speaking.

[Embedded video omitted]

Listening Indicator

A pair of pulsing blue lights on the left and right side of the light ring means that Alexa is listening. The pulse matches your voice - wider pulses for louder speech, shorter pulses for softer speech.

Listening

Notification Indicator

A yellow light comes on when you have a pending or unread notification.

[Embedded video omitted]

Notification

Microphones Indicator

When the microphones on/off button is pressed, the button will show a red light and the light ring will display a temporary red light. Press the button again to turn on the device microphones and the red light will disappear.

[Embedded video omitted]

Privacy On

Responding Indicator

When Alexa is speaking, a blue pulsing light will come on at the bottom of the light ring. The pulsing matches Alexa’s voice - wider pulses for louder speech, shorter pulses for softer speech.

Responding

Thinking Indicator

Manage Your Calendar with Alexa+

Alexa+ lets you manage your calendar by summarizing events and through visualization, natural interaction, and conflict awareness.

The following table lists calendar features available with Alexa+ and their descriptions:

  • Feature: Summarized Calendar Events; Description: Alexa can summarize your schedule and tell you how busy your day is going to be. You can ask Alexa to check your schedule, find free time slots, and access your upcoming day. Just say things like, “What does my day look like tomorrow?”

  • Feature: Monthly and Weekly Overview; Description: Stay on top of your schedule with Alexa+ calendar features. You can say things like, “Show me my calendar for the week,” and your Alexa-supported devices with a screen displays upcoming events and appointments. You can even access a monthly overview by trying, “Show my calendar for next month.”

  • Feature: Conflict Awareness; Description: Alexa alerts you to schedule conflicts, both in your existing calendar and when adding new events.

  • Feature: Create, Edit, and Delete Events; Description: Add new events to your calendar as one-time or recurring events. You can also update the date, time or title of existing events, or delete an event from your schedule.

  • Feature: Calendar Notifications; Description: Alexa can notify you of upcoming events through announcements on the Echo device you choose. To opt in, visit the calendar setting in your Alexa app: 1. Select More. 2. Select Settings. 3. Select Calendar. 4. Select Calendar Notifications.

  • Feature: Multiprofile Support; Description: Each person with their own Alexa profile can link their individual accounts to Alexa, for personalized calendar management. Each Alexa profile can have multiple linked calendars. You can set a default personal calendar and a shared family calendar for household events.

  • Feature: Voice ID Personalization Visual ID Personalization; Description: Create an Alexa Voice ID to get notification from your selected calendars. To learn more, go to Create and Alexa Voice ID. You can also enroll in Visual ID on your Echo Show devices and receive a personalized calendar when recognized. To learn more, go to Enroll in Visual ID on Your Echo Devices with a Screen.

  • Feature: Enhanced Widget Sizes; Description: You can change widget sizes on compatible Echo devices to modify the size of your calendar. For more information on how to change your widget size, go to Remove or Arrange Widgets.

Manage Your Oura Experience on

        Alexa+ {#manage-your-oura-experience-on-alexa}

Connect your Oura ring to bring your health and wellness scores into your daily routines with Alexa+.

Note: Availability for this preview feature will roll out across compatible devices over time.

Link Your Oura Account

You can link one Oura account per Amazon account, which connects to your Alexa profile. Only the primary account holder can link an Oura account. Non-primary profiles cannot link their Oura ring to Alexa. You can check whether you are the primary account holder by visiting your Amazon Family page.

When linked, Oura shares health metrics (Sleep, Readiness, Activity, Heart Rate, and SpO2) that are encrypted and stored securely in the Amazon Cloud. All data is handled according to Amazon’s Privacy Notice and is used to personalize your experience and improve our services. Learn more about built-in protections and controls that you can see, hear, and touch by visiting the Alexa Privacy Hub.

Health metrics shared by Oura are accessible using your Alexa devices. You can unlink your Oura account at any time to stop sharing data with Alexa.

Note: Recommendations made by Alexa are generalized wellness recommendations and don’t constitute personalized health or medical advice.

Wellness Briefing

Alexa provides a personalized summary that includes information from the day before (like how you slept) and your readiness. Alexa uses wellness scores from your Oura Ring along with the weather forecast and your calendar to provide actionable guidance like activity suggestions to meet your goals.

To set up your wellness briefing:

  • Say, “Set up my daily wellness briefing routine” or “Give me my wellness briefing.”
  • Setup in the Alexa app:
    1. Open the Alexa App.
    2. Select More.
    3. Select Routines.
    4. Select Wellness Briefing Routine from the Health & Wellness category.

Wellness Briefing is also available as an action to add to your existing routines or to create new routines.

Personalized Bedtime

Alexa uses Oura’s recommended optimal bedtime to help you set up a routine for a good night’s sleep. You can use Oura’s optimal bedtime to create Routines for actions like adjusting your thermostat temperature, turning off your lights, or playing calming music.

To set up your personalized bedtime routine:

  • Say, “Set up my bedtime routine with Oura.”
  • Setup in the Alexa app:
    1. Open the Alexa App.
    2. Select More.
    3. Select Routines.
    4. Select Personalized Bedtime Routine from the Health & Wellness category.

Oura’s Optimal Bedtime is also available as a trigger to add to your existing routines or to create a new routine.

Health & Wellness Widget

See your sleep score, readiness, activity progress, optimal bedtime, and more on your eligible Echo device with a screen throughout the day. Choose a tile on your device or speak to Alexa to dive deeper into any metric that interests you.

Conversational Q&A

Alexa+ answers your questions about Oura metrics. Whether you want to check your sleep score while making breakfast, ask about your heart rate variability while getting dressed, or inquire about trends over time after a workout, just ask Alexa.

Example questions include:

  • “Suggest a workout.”
  • “How did I sleep last night?”
  • “Tell me more about my Readiness Score”
  • “How long did I sleep on average this week?”
  • “What was my resting heart rate last night?”
  • “How is the readiness score calculated?”
  • “How is my step count trending this week?”

Personalization with Voice ID & Visual ID

Use voice or visual ID to personalize Alexa’s responses. When recognized, Alexa shares relevant metrics on the home screen widget of your supported Echo device.

Learn more about setting up Voice ID and Visual ID in your Alexa Profile Settings.

Managing Reminders and Tasks with

        Alexa+ {#managing-reminders-and-tasks-with-alexa}

Alexa+ helps you stay on top of your tasks.

A single task list shows your reminders and to-dos for easy reference. You can access your task list at any time by asking Alexa “What’s on my task list?” or “What are my reminders?” or in the “Reminders & Tasks” section of the Alexa apps on iOS and Android.

You can display the task list on your Echo Show’s home screen by installing the widget for “Reminders & Tasks.”

Just say, “Remind me to walk the dog every day” or “Add water the plants to my to-do list.” When your reminder is due, Alexa alerts you with a voice announcement and phone notification.

Reminders by default ring on the device that you set it on.

Just tell Alexa what you want a reminder for, and when to remind you.

  • “Remind me to schedule a haircut.”
  • “Tell me to feed the fish at 8 o’clock.”
  • “Add change tires to my task list.”
  • “Add book dentist appointment to my to-dos.”

Set Recurring Reminders

  • “Remind me to stretch every day at 9 am.”
  • “Remind me to call Dad every Saturday.”

Assign Personal Reminders

  • “Remind Vinny to stop watching TV in an hour.”
  • “Remind James to get the dress tomorrow at 6 pm.”
  • “When you see Jill, remind her to feed the fish.”

Note: When assigning a reminder to someone else, please make sure they already have created a profile on Alexa. For more help, go to: What Are Alexa Profiles?.

Tip: Presence-based reminders (like “When you see Jill, remind…”) require that the recipient has set up Visual ID on the device. To learn more about Visual ID, go to What Is Visual ID on Echo Show?.

Ask Alexa to Follow Up for Important Reminders

  • Ask Alexa to follow up on your reminders using the examples below. Alexa sends you reminder notifications every hour or day until you confirm that you’ve completed the task. “Make sure that I take out the trash bins.”
  • “Follow up on my reminder to pay rent.”
  • “Create a follow-up reminder.”

Snooze Reminders

  • “Snooze reminder for 20 minutes.”
  • “Remind me again in an hour.”

Check Reminders for Yourself or Others

  • “What are my reminders?”
  • “What are my Monday reminders?”
  • “What are John’s reminders?”
  • “What are John’s tasks?”
  • “What are my tasks today?”

Note: If you set up VisualID or VoiceID for your profile, Alexa responds more easily to you with reminders applicable to you.

Tip: Not near your Alexa device when a reminder is announced? A yellow light on your Echo device or an on-screen notification on Echo Spot or Echo Show devices tells you that you have missed reminders. Say, “What are my reminders?”

Manage Reminders in the Alexa App

Edit or add to reminders in the Alexa app on your phone or mobile device. Alexa can also send reminders to your phone. Your tasks and reminders are visible to everyone in your household.

Note: If you reset or deregister your device, any reminders that you set up on your device may be lost.

Photo Gallery Unlimited with Alexa+

Photo Gallery Unlimited transforms your home screen into a dedicated photo frame with your personal photos displaying continuously.

Note: Photo Gallery Unlimited is a device-level subscription. You can purchase multiple subscriptions on your account, but each Echo Show device requires its own subscription to access Photo Gallery Unlimited. Photo Gallery Unlimited isn’t available for Echo Spot or Echo Hub.

Photo Gallery Unlimited is an add-on subscription that allows your personal photos to display on your Echo Show home screen. Your home screen displays only your photos, creating an uninterrupted viewing experience dedicated to your personal collection.

Automatically filtering out irrelevant images like screenshots, whiteboards, and receipts, Photo Gallery Unlimited ensures that only your meaningful photos are displayed. Your selected photos stream continuously on your home screen with smart display features like side-by-side pairing of related portraits. Single portrait photos use opaque gradient bars to maximize your screen space and showcase your memories clearly.

For example, you can set up your Photo Gallery Unlimited subscription by saying, “Tell me about Photo Gallery Unlimited,” or go to Menu > Settings > Display & Appearance on your Echo Show to find the subscription card.

Use the Alexa app to review or delete the attachments you’ve uploaded to Alexa+.

To review or delete your attachments:

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open
  3. Select Alexa Privacy.
  4. Select Review Attachments, and use the drop-down to select a date range, or filter by profile or file type to view attachments.
  5. Select the delete icon beside each attachment to delete individual attachments.

You can view or download your attachments at: Review Attachments).

Review Your Alexa History

You can review, listen to, or delete your Alexa history from the Alexa app or Your Account.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More .
  3. Select Alexa Privacy.
  4. Select Review Alexa History and then select an entry, review a specific date range, or filter by device or profile. You can also clear everything by selecting Delete all History.

You can also go to Alexa Privacy Settings on your web browser.

To learn more, go to Alexa and Alexa Device FAQs.

Note:

  • Voice recordings are used to improve the accuracy of your interactions with Alexa. Deleting voice recordings associated with your account may degrade your experience.
  • Deleting voice recordings doesn’t delete your Alexa messages.
  • Voice recordings are visible until the deletion request has finished processing.

Send Alexa+ Responses to Yourself

You can request to have Alexa’s responses or communication sent to your phone or email.

During interactions with Alexa, You can have a copy of communications or responses Alexa says sent to your email or phone. These utterances might include, “create an itinerary for a week at the beach,” or “create dinner recipes of the week that take under 30 minutes.”

If there’s a response from Alexa that you would like to email yourself or send to your phone, say “Email me that response,” or “Send that to my phone.” Alexa sends responses to the email and phone number associates with your profile, which can be found in the Alexa app.

  • Manage the Email Your Alexa Responses Are Sent To

Set Up Email to Contacts with Alexa+

Alexa’s Email to Contacts feature lets you send emails to your contacts using just your voice. Stay connected and coordinated without the hassle of composing messages yourself.

To setup Email to Contacts:

  1. Open the Alexa App .
  2. Select .
  3. Select Settings .
  4. Select Email my contacts, and then review the instructions and permissions.
  5. Select Link Email Accounts.
  6. Select a default email address.
  7. Allow access to your contacts and email accounts for Alexa to send emails.

Alexa syncs the contact information from your linked email accounts and stores it in the cloud.

If you haven’t linked your email account, Alexa can still draft emails for you but needs to send them to your own inbox first. Once you’ve connected your email, Alexa can draft messages with text, formatting, images, and links. Alexa also learns your contacts over time to make sending emails quicker.

Note: Alexa can only email your own contacts, not other household member’s contacts.

  • Using Email to Contacts with Alexa+
