Shopping with Alexa+ (Alexa+ gives you more ways to find products)

Alexa+ gives you more ways to find products and explore deals all through natural conversation.

When you have Alexa+, you can speak conversationally when you make a request. These request types can also be used as chats to shop on Alexa+ on your browser.

Search with Alexa+

Ask Alexa to search for products by name or category:

  • “Search for [item name].”
  • “Show me [item name] under [price].”
  • “Find [category of item].”

You can create instant shopping lists with Alexa+ on your browser. In a chat, you could say something like,

  • “Tell me basic supplies I need for an overnight camping trip, and add those to my Vacation list.”

Explore Product Deals

In addition to common requests, you can now ask Alexa complex questions about a product’s details:

  • “What is the warranty on [item]?”
  • “What are the reviews for [product]?”
  • “What is the rating for [product]?”
  • “Does that [food item] contain peanuts?”
  • “What should I consider when buying a [product]?”
    • For example, you can ask about TVs, furniture, and game consoles.

You can ask Alexa follow-up questions for search results. For example, you can say, “Shop for running shoes,” and then ask, “How do they compare to [brand]?”

Create Deal Alerts

Explore personalized deal recommendations based on your previous shopping activity:

  • “What are my deals?”
  • “Do you have any deals on [product]?”
  • “Show me deals.”
  • “What deals are on right now?”
  • “What are the customer ratings for [recommended deal].”

Note: To create a deal alert for specific products or keywords, follow the steps in Use Alexa to Find Deals on Amazon.

Place Orders or Reorder

Ask Alexa to place an order or customize your reorder:

  • “Place my order.”
  • “Cancel my order.”
  • “Buy [item] now.”
  • “Check out my cart.”
  • “Reorder [product name].”
  • “Show me a [product].”
  • “Shop [product name].”
  • “Add or remove [item] from cart.”

Manage Orders

Ask Alexa for order updates, details on your upcoming orders, and your order history:

  • “Where’s my stuff?”

  • “When did I last order [product]?”

  • “When will my last order arrive?”

  • “What is the update on my order?”

  • “Where are my returns?”

  • “Where are my refunds?”

  • Use Alexa to Find Deals on Amazon

Themes on Alexa+

Personalize your Alexa+ experience with themes that match your interests.

With an Alexa+ Theme, Alexa responds to your interactions with sounds and visuals that match the theme you select.

For example, when you turn on the Space Theme, Alexa may recommend fun facts or tell jokes fitting the theme.

You can turn themes on or off at no cost. When you turn on a theme, Alexa tells you about the theme and the experiences it offers. Also, the primary account holder receives an email with additional information.

The list of available themes rotate throughout the year. You can explore available themes from home cards on Echo Show devices or ask Alexa directly.

The Ultimate Guide to Creating Your Smart Home with Alexa+

What Is a Smart Home?

A smart home is a residence that runs internet-connected devices for task and device action automation. Smart home automation benefits its residences and users with convenience, security, and comfort. A well-functioning smart home often has its devices operating together to perform multiple actions efficiently and in sync.

Benefits of an Alexa+ Smart Home

An Alexa+ smart home offers many benefits for a user looking to add convenience and automation into their life:

  • Unified ecosystem
  • AI-powered voice assistant
  • “Works with Alexa” certification
  • Voice routine creation and customization

Basic Requirements for an Alexa+ Smart Home

  • Amazon account
  • Access to Alexa+
  • Alexa app
  • Internet connection
  • Alexa-enabled device (such as an Echo device)
  • Compatible smart home device

Selecting Your Home Automation Devices

Smart Speakers

Household smart speakers, such as Echo, Echo Dot, and Echo Pop, are common Alexa+ virtual assistant devices. You can place these devices anywhere in your home to control your smart home devices, play music, and get updates on news and the weather.

Smart Home Hub

A smart home hub is the control center of a smart home. It acts as the central point for connecting and managing various smart home devices, and allows you to automate your devices from a single platform. Instead of sending commands to multiple devices, a hub provides one central place to send commands to all devices.

Smarts Lights and Plugs

Smart lighting devices, such as bulbs, plugs, and switches, are some of the most common smart home devices. Smart lighting solutions offer customization, convenience, and lower energy use to any home.

Smart Cameras & Home Security

A smart home security system is a device or set of interconnected devices that work to protect your home. Smart home security devices include:

  • Smart cameras
  • Motion sensors
  • Smart locks
  • Window sensors

Smart Climate Control

Smart thermostats allow you to set temperature schedules that are based on the weather, your schedule, and whether you’re home. For example, program your thermostat to cool down the house an hour before bed and warm up the house one hour before you wake up.

Alexa+ and Ring Smart Camera Features

If you have a Ring home subscription and Alexa+, you can:

  • Ask Alexa for a summary of events detected by your Ring cameras. For more information, go to Use Camera Event Summaries with Alexa+.
  • If you have a Ring premium subscription and compatible Echo Show, ask Alexa to show you footage of events detected on your Ring camera. For more information, go to Use Ring Smart Video Search with Alexa+.

Connecting Your Smart Devices with Alexa+

To set up your smart home devices in the Alexa app directly, go to Connect Smart Home Devices to Alexa.

Setting Up and Using Voice Routines with Alexa+

Routines are short cuts for Alexa, saving you time by grouping together device actions so you don’t have to ask for each one individually.

With Alexa+, you can create Routines by voice. To learn more about Routines by voice, go to About Routines by Voice with Alexa+.

Use Alexa to Find Deals on Amazon

Ask Alexa to notify you when specific Amazon products or types of products go on sale.

To create an Amazon shopping deal notification, go to the product page or search result for the product you’re interested in. Once you’ve found the product, say things like, “Let me know when [product] goes on sale.” You can also create a notification by adding keywords or by price point. Just say, “Tell me when [product name or keyword] goes on sale,” or, “Let me know when [product name or keyword] is 25% off.”

Once you’ve created a notification, Alexa monitors the item for 30 days. If a deal becomes available, Alexa sends a notification to your compatible Alexa devices. To hear a list of which deals you are tracking, say, “What products are you tracking for me?”

If you would like to turn your Amazon shopping deal notifications off, say, “Stop finding deals on [product],” or “Stop all deal tracking.”

Use Camera Event Summaries with Alexa+

Ask Alexa to provide event summaries captured by your Ring cameras.

Alexa can summarize certain events detected on your Ring camera. Ask Alexa questions about events involving people, packages, motion activity, and your doorbell. Questions about events can be from a specific day, or from a general time frame. You can say:

  • “What happened around my house today?”
  • “Was there any activity around my house on Tuesday?”
  • “When was the last time my camera saw something?”
  • “What time did someone ring my doorbell this morning?”
  • “Did you see anyone on my outdoor camera last night?”

Camera event summaries are available only for Ring cameras connected to Alexa, and require a Ring subscription. For setup instructions, visit Set Up Smart Home Camera Features with Alexa+.

Note: Alexa can only summarize new camera events that occur after you complete the setup steps.

  • Set Up Smart Home Camera Features with Alexa+
  • Use Ring Smart Video Search with Alexa+

Use Night or Vacation Mode with Alexa+

Night and Vacation modes let you automate household devices based on specific scenarios - managing your home’s nighttime settings or protecting your home during extended absences.

For example, you can:

  • Lock the doors.
  • Arm the security system.
  • Turn off indoor lights.
  • Turn on the patio light.
  • Set your Echo devices to Do Not Disturb.
  • Set your smart thermostat to a desired temperature.
  • Turn on Away Lighting.

Control modes by:

  • Saying “Good night,” “Switch to night mode”
  • Saying “Turn on vacation mode,” “Switch to vacation mode”
  • Using the Alexa app
  • Using the mode controls on Echo Show devices

Note: Night and vacation modes require you setting up home and away modes. The option to Add Night Mode or Add Vacation Mode appear once the setup of home and away modes is complete. For instructions to set up home and away modes, go to Set Up Modes.

  • What Are Modes?
  • Set Up Modes

Use Ring AI Features with Alexa+

Use Alexa to hear a description of who is at your door, or ask for recordings of events captured on your Ring camera.

Descriptive Announcements

When someone rings your doorbell, Alexa announces a detailed description of who’s at the door based on Ring’s AI descriptions. For example, you might hear “A pizza delivery man is at the front door.” Turn on AI Descriptions in the Ring app, and make sure doorbell press announcements are turned on in the Alexa app.

AI Video Search

Ask Alexa to show you footage of specific events recorded by your Ring camera. With Alexa’s integration with AI Video Search, you can search for footage related to people, packages, vehicles, animals, and more. Say “Show me packages delivered to my front door today” or “Did you see any black cats?” and your compatible device brings up the relevant video based on your request

AI Video Search is available on the following devices:

  • Echo Show 8 (all Generations), Echo Show 10 (3rd Generation), Echo Show 11 (2025 release), Echo Show 15 (all Generations), Echo Show 21
  • Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Generation), Fire TV Stick 4K (2nd Generation), Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series, Fire TV 4-Series, Fire TV Omni QLED Series

Note: Ring AI features require a Ring AI Pro subscription.

Using Alexa+ with Amazon Family

How to ensure the best Alexa+ experience on all devices in your Amazon Family.

You can use Alexa+ as part of an Amazon Family. Alexa+ doesn’t support account switching. So, to help everyone in your household use Alexa+, we recommend adjusting your Amazon Family setup, with one of the following options.

To enable Alexa+ for your family, go to Alexaplus (amazon.com).

Upgrade All Amazon Family Member Accounts to Alexa+

The best Alexa+ experience on Amazon Family comes when all members of the Family have upgraded to Alexa+. We recommend that all adult Family members accept the upgrade invitation from their individual Amazon accounts.

Once your Amazon Family is created, wallet sharing must be completed to activate Prime benefit sharing, including Alexa+. To learn more, go to our help page Wallet Sharing with Amazon Family.

Consolidate Devices under One Amazon Account with Alexa+

Alternatively, consolidating your Alexa devices under a single Amazon account can improve the Family Alexa+ experience. Pick one account in your Family to be the primary, then upgrade that account to Alexa+, and register all the devices under that account.

Tip: To reduce setup later, make the primary account the one with the most devices, smart home setups, routines, or group spaces already established.

To consolidate the shared devices under the primary account:

  1. Reset each device to factory settings. To learn more, go to our help page Reset Your Echo Device.

  2. Set up each device with the guided on-screen or Alexa app instructions.

    Important: Sign in and register each device with your chosen primary Amazon account.

  3. Create a profile in the primary account for each household member. You can say, “Create a Profile,” or use the Alexa App.

Create an Amazon Family around an Account with Alexa+

Once you’ve upgraded to Alexa+, add adult members of your household, who live at the same address, to your Amazon Family. Everyone can share Alexa+ benefits, while keeping their individual accounts. Learn how to Create Your Amazon Family.

Using Email to Contacts with

        Alexa+ {#using-email-to-contacts-with-alexa}

Send emails to your contacts through voice commands.

Alexa’s Email to Contacts feature lets you easily send emails to your contacts using just your voice, helping you stay connected with loved ones and friends. To turn on this feature, Alexa syncs contact information from your linked email accounts and stores it in the cloud.

To get started:

  1. Open the Alexa App .
  2. Select More.
  3. Select Settings.
  4. Select Communicate.
  5. Turn on Email my contacts.
  6. Select Add Account and follow the steps to complete email linking.
  7. Verify your default email address.

You can now send emails to your contacts. Just say, “Email [contact name],” and your message. Then, review the draft and confirm to send.

If you haven’t linked your email account, Alexa can still draft the email but will need to send it to your own inbox first. Alexa can draft emails with text, formatting, images, and links, and learns your contacts over time.

Note: Alexa can only email your own contacts, not other household member’s contacts.

  • Set Up Email to Contacts with Alexa+

What Is Briefing with Alexa+?

Listen to personalized news briefings generated by Alexa.

Alexa helps you stay up to date on the latest news and topics of interest in a quick briefing that updates throughout the day. Listen to short summaries of news developments across all your Alexa+ supported devices.

When you’re ready to hear your briefing, just ask Alexa. You can ask for your briefing at any time of the day and say things like, “What’s my daily briefing?” or “What’s trending?” or “What are today’s headlines?” to hear your briefing.

Your briefing pulls from local, national, and globally sourced articles licensed from Alexa News partners.

Turn Notifications On or Off for Your Echo Devices

To turn notifications on or off, use the Alexa app.

  1. Open the Alexa app .
  2. Open More and select Settings .
  3. Select Notifications.
  4. Select a feature or service, and use the toggle to turn notifications on or off.

What Is Alexa Voice ID?

Alexa voice ID helps Alexa recognize you when you speak and provide a personalized experience.

You can create an Alexa voice ID for a personalized experience when Alexa recognizes your voice. With Alexa voice ID, Alexa can call you by name and provide enhanced personalization. To set up Alexa voice ID, go to Create an Alexa Voice ID.

With an Alexa voice ID, you can get a personalized experience for:

  • Alexa Calling and Messaging: Send and receive your own personal messages.
  • Calendar: Hear your personal upcoming schedule and add events to your calendar.
  • Flash Briefing: Skip stories and news items that you’ve already heard.
  • Music: If you have the Amazon Music Unlimited Family Plan, Alexa customizes music playback based on your voice.
  • Music and Podcast Services: Set default music and podcast services for each Alexa profile on your Alexa account.
  • Reminders: Create personal reminders and get them delivered just to your phone.
  • Shopping: Limit purchasing so that only recognized household members can place orders with Alexa.
  • Skills: Receive personalized responses for supported skills.

Voice ID uses voice recognition to recognize you and display personalized content on compatible Echo Show devices.

  • Create an Alexa Voice ID
  • Create an Alexa Voice ID for Your Child
